name: kosif-superpowers
description: Capability self-awareness and thinking upgrade for Claude. One front door (scripts/hub.py find) maps a task in the user's words to the runnable tools, catalog powers and guides that fit, and says what this machine can run now. Covers what Claude can do in the current session (tools, connectors, installable libraries, surfaces), how to think, create and verify better, and a searchable catalog of 5,300+ powers in 10 domains (thinking, writing and Arabic, code, data, documents, research, apps, image and audio, product and finance, motion graphics and video), each with requirements, an evidence badge and proofs. Use at the start of any substantial or creative task, when asked what Claude can do, told to use its superpowers, or given this skill's repository link; and for motion graphics, montage, captions, reels, video edits, drawing, 3D, image design and lawful software investigation. Arabic triggers - قدراتك، القدرات الخارقة، تقدر تعمل ايه، فكّر بعمق، خريطة ذهنية، موشن جرافيك، مونتاج، ريلز.
paths_note: Tool paths and examples are relative to their root: 'skill' = this folder, 'repo' = the kosif-tool repository root.

areas.about: Know what this session can do and pick the right capability: briefings, catalog search, routers, requirement checks.
Thinking engines, idea generation, sizing estimates and writing-quality checks.
Author editable motion graphics (SVG/HTML/Canvas), scaffold real-library projects, render to MP4 and check the delivery.
Read a reference video, rebuild an editable edit with the user's footage, plan and render cuts, gate quality.
Measure real audio: energy cues, timed words, tempo hypotheses, and map them to motion decisions.
Code-drawn characters and scenes, painting, IK and full-body animation, sketch assist.
Blender-free 3D rendering and GLB export, plus optional Blender bridges for Cycles and cinematic renders.
Operations on the user's photos and designs (develop, repair, effects, layouts) and font matching.
Find and fetch external references, media and repositories safely, with licences and rights recorded.
Lawful inspection of apps, binaries, installers and repositories (REA, Ghidra, triage, packing).
Local MCP servers that give a client bounded, consented access to a workspace.
Build, check and package the catalog, the skill and the style atlas.

commands.name: build
commands.does: Rewrites the tracked files data/capability_graph.json and references/capability-graph.html, then prints node counts per kind, the edge count and how many Graphify edges were confirmed. Running the script with no arguments does the same.

commands.name: build --check
commands.does: Writes nothing. Exits 1 and names the stale file(s) if a fresh build would differ from the committed ones; otherwise prints 'capability graph up to date'.

commands.name: build --out-dir
commands.does: Writes capability_graph.json and capability-graph.html into the given folder instead of the tracked locations.

commands.name: stats
commands.does: Prints node counts by kind and edge counts by relation (Python Counter reprs), read from the committed data/capability_graph.json.

commands.name: path
commands.does: Prints up to 3 nodes whose id contains the key, or whose family ID prefix equals it, with their incoming and outgoing edges (has, needs, runs, imports, tested_by). Keys can be a family stem, a requirement such as ffmpeg, or a script such as scripts/powers.py. Exits 1 with 'no node' when nothing matches.

tools.inputs: data/powers/*.json, data/requirements.json, data/graphify_code_layer.json (a local snapshot; no network), the scripts/ sources (AST), and tests/*.py plus evals/*.py|*.mjs (scanned for script file names). path takes one key.
tools.outputs: data/capability_graph.json (nodes and edges) and references/capability-graph.html (self-contained, no CDN, light and dark themes), or both files in --out-dir. Plus one-line build summaries, stats Counters or path edge listings on stdout.
tools.consent: build (and a bare run with no arguments) overwrites the tracked files data/capability_graph.json and references/capability-graph.html; use build --check or build --out-dir <folder> to preview. --help and a mistyped flag only print usage.
tools.limits: Edges are inferred from text mentions (script paths in how/proof fields, file names inside tests) and import statements, so 'tested_by' means a test names the script, not that it passed; stats and path read the committed JSON, which may be stale.
tools.evidence_note: Live HEAD 524e22a: tests.test_capability_graph 4/5 passed; the determinism assertion passed but 'committed files are current' failed because data/capability_graph.json and references/capability-graph.html predate the new runnable-tools family, hub.py, kosif_mcp.py and evals/test_hub.py. git-archive snapshot of HEAD (skill + tests) in scratch after running build there: 5/5 passed. commands.does: Ranks powers for a brief across domains (spread across families), adds reference styles and the output format for motion briefs, and lists chapters and hints

commands.name: styles
commands.does: Lists watched reference styles from data/styles.json, filtered by genre

commands.name: domains
commands.does: Counts per domain, then family, then status, with Arabic and English titles

commands.name: mindmap
commands.does: Prints a Mermaid mindmap of domains and families, or drills into one domain down to its top powers

commands.name: mindmap-html
commands.does: Writes a standalone HTML page that renders the map with Mermaid from a CDN and falls back to a text list offline

commands.name: env
commands.does: Runs probe_env.py with the given flags

tools.inputs: Free-text words or a brief (Arabic or English), a power id (e.g. GLOW-03), a family stem or prefix (light-glow-bloom or GLOW), --domain (mind, craft, code, data, docs, research, build, media, strategy, motion), --status filters and --genre. Reads data/powers/*.json and data/styles.json.
tools.outputs: Text lines or JSON on stdout; search, show and family exit 1 when nothing matches. mindmap prints Mermaid text, or with --html PATH writes an HTML page and creates parent folders. env prints the probe_env card or JSON.
tools.consent: `env` runs probe_env.py, which contacts public hosts unless --no-network is passed and installs packages from PyPI and npm with --install-test. `mindmap --html PATH` writes a file at PATH, and the page loads Mermaid from cdn.jsdelivr.net when opened.
tools.limits: It ranks catalog records by keyword and intent matching; a match or badge describes a recorded recipe, not a run on this machine, and nothing in a record is executed.
tools.evidence_note: tests.test_superpowers 8/8 passed; evals/test_rea_routing.py 2/2 passed; evals/test_installer_triage.py 23/23 passed (one of its tests calls powers.intent_of)

tools.summary_en: Probes the current machine (OS, CPU/RAM/disk/GPU, runtimes, CLI tools and versions, Python and Node packages, Arabic fonts, browsers, credential env-var names, proxy and network reach). It prints a Markdown capability card or JSON that maps each finding to the power families it unlocks.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص الجهاز الحالي: النظام والمعالج والذاكرة والقرص ووحدة الرسوميات، وبيئات التشغيل والأدوات وإصداراتها، وحزم بايثون وNode، والخطوط العربية، والمتصفحات، وأسماء متغيرات المفاتيح، والوكيل وإمكانية الوصول إلى الشبكة. ثم يطبع بطاقة قدرات بصيغة Markdown أو JSON تربط كل نتيجة بعائلات القدرات التي تفتحها.
use_when: افحص الجهاز وشوف ايه المتاح عليه
هل عندي ffmpeg وخطوط عربية ومتصفح هنا؟
Probe this machine before I promise a render
Can this sandbox reach pypi and npm?
Write a dated environment snapshot to a file

commands.name: card
commands.does: Markdown capability card, including HEAD requests to 11 public hosts (default budget 18 s)

commands.name: json
commands.does: The same probe as JSON (probe, host, system, gpu, bins, versions, python, node, fonts, browsers, proxy, network, keys, docker, catalog, domains, unlocks, gaps, timed_out, elapsed_s)

commands.name: no-network
commands.does: Skips the public-host reachability checks (offline or CI); the loopback agent-proxy status query still runs

commands.name: budget
commands.does: Sets the total time budget in seconds (minimum 3, default 18)

commands.name: write
commands.does: Also writes a dated Markdown snapshot to the given path (the parent folder must already exist)

commands.name: install-test
commands.does: Also times a real venv+pip install (six, plus packaging via uv) and an npm install (is-number) inside a temp dir

tools.inputs: No required input. Flags: --json, --no-network, --budget SECONDS, --write PATH, --install-test.
tools.outputs: A Markdown card or JSON on stdout, and an optional dated Markdown snapshot at --write PATH. The exit code is always 0; checks that time out are listed under timed_out.
tools.consent: A default run sends HEAD requests to 11 public hosts (pypi.org, registry.npmjs.org, github.com, api.github.com, huggingface.co, cdn.jsdelivr.net, fonts.googleapis.com, api.anthropic.com, example.com, en.wikipedia.org, plus an apt mirror); use --no-network if outbound contact is not wanted. --install-test downloads and installs packages from PyPI (six, packaging via uv) and npm (is-number) into a temp dir and needs explicit approval. Every run also executes local version commands, writes and deletes a 32 MB temp file, and runs 'sudo -n true' when not root.
tools.limits: It detects presence and reachability only (version strings, import specs, HEAD responses), not whether a tool produces correct output, and the card holds only for this machine at this moment.
tools.evidence_note: No test file exercises probe_env.py. Smoke run here: --help rc 0; 'python3 scripts/probe_env.py --no-network --budget 10 --json' (TMPDIR pointed at the scratch folder) rc 0 in 2.4 s, host label 'Claude Code cloud session', nothing timed out. It still queried the loopback agent-proxy status endpoint despite --no-network. --install-test and the default network run were not executed.

tools.summary_en: Reports whether each named Python distribution (up to 50) has installed metadata and which version it is, without importing, installing or contacting the network.
tools.summary_ar: يبيّن لكل توزيعة بايثون مذكورة (حتى 50 توزيعة) هل بياناتها الوصفية مثبتة وما إصدارها، دون استيرادها أو تثبيتها أو الاتصال بالشبكة.
use_when: هل pandas وnumpy متسطبين على الجهاز ده؟
تأكد من وجود مكتبة httpx قبل ما أكتب الكود
Check which of pandas, numpy and httpx are installed here
What version of pillow is available in this Python?

commands.name: probe (positional names)
commands.does: For each distribution name, prints status (distribution_metadata_found or not_found_in_environment), version, and import_tested, execution_tested and ready_for_production, which are always false.

tools.inputs: From 1 to 50 pip distribution names, such as pillow or opencv-python-headless. Import names such as PIL or cv2 are reported as not found.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout with the Python version, one record per package and the scope current_environment_only_no_install_no_network.
tools.limits: Reads installed distribution metadata only and never imports the package, so a found package is not proven to import or work.
tools.evidence_note: 15/15 passed (6 tests exercise this probe, one of them through the CLI; the other 9 cover architecture_sizer.py)

tools.summary_en: Reports what each catalog power needs (tools, pip/npm packages, keys, platforms, fonts, models), which of those this machine has, and the install commands for the powers suggested for a task. Maintainer subcommands re-derive the `requires` fields and regenerate references/requirements.md.
tools.summary_ar: يبيّن ما تحتاجه كل قدرة في الكتالوج من أدوات وحزم pip وnpm ومفاتيح ومنصات وخطوط ونماذج، وما المتوفر منها على هذا الجهاز، وأوامر التثبيت للقدرات المقترحة لمهمة ما. وتعيد أوامر الصيانة اشتقاق حقول requires وتوليد الملف references/requirements.md.
use_when: ايش لازم أثبت عشان أسوي ريلز بتعليق صوتي وترجمة متزامنة؟
القدرة GLOW-05 محتاجة ايه عشان تشتغل؟
What do I need to install before starting this task?
Which registered requirements are present on this machine?
Check that every power's requires field is up to date

commands.name: present
commands.does: Marks every registered requirement present, missing or unknown on this machine (read-only, about 1 s)

commands.name: for
commands.does: Checklist for one power: each requirement's state, kind and install command

commands.name: plan
commands.example: python3 scripts/requirements.py plan "Arabic reel with voice-over and synced captions" --limit 8 --json
commands.does: Suggests powers for a task, then merges their requirements into one checklist with install commands; ▶ marks powers whose requirements are all present

commands.name: derive-check
commands.does: Exits 1 if re-deriving `requires` from install/how text would change any record; read-only

commands.name: derive
commands.does: Rewrites the `requires` field in data/powers/*.json from the patterns in data/requirements.json

commands.name: index
commands.does: Regenerates references/requirements.md (requirement to powers unlocked); --probe adds present/missing marks for this machine

tools.inputs: A power id (for), a task sentence (plan, with --limit and --json), or nothing (present, derive, index). Reads data/requirements.json, data/powers/*.json and environment-variable names.
tools.outputs: Checklists with 🟢/📦/🔑/❔ marks and install commands, or JSON (plan --json, present --json), on stdout. derive rewrites data/powers/*.json; index rewrites references/requirements.md; derive --check exits 1 when stale.
tools.consent: `derive` (without --check) rewrites data/powers/*.json and `index` rewrites references/requirements.md inside the skill; both are maintainer actions. The install commands it prints need user approval before anyone runs them, especially paid or system-wide installs.
tools.limits: It detects presence only (shutil.which, importlib find_spec, env-var name set, font file exists), never version fit or output quality, and it treats a power with no listed requirement as ready.
tools.evidence_note: 6/6 passed (python3 -m unittest tests.test_requirements)

tools.summary_en: Picks an ordered subset of the 15 vendored obra/superpowers v7 process skills (brainstorming, debugging, TDD, verification and others) for a task, checks the vendored sources, and can install KOSIF plus those skills into ~/.claude/skills with backups.
tools.summary_ar: يختار للمهمة مجموعة مرتّبة من مهارات العمل الخمس عشرة المضمّنة من obra/superpowers الإصدار 7 (مثل العصف الذهني وتتبّع الأخطاء والتطوير المقاد بالاختبارات والتحقق)، ويفحص المصادر المضمّنة، ويستطيع تثبيت KOSIF مع تلك المهارات في ‎~/.claude/skills مع نسخ احتياطية.
use_when: أي مهارات عمل أستخدمها لإصلاح عطل في التطبيق؟
اعمل خطة لتطوير برنامج المونتاج، أي منهجية أتبع؟
Which process skills apply to 'Fix the crash in the montage app'?
Install KOSIF Superpowers and the obra process skills into my Claude skills folder
Check whether the vendored superpowers skills are complete

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Checks the vendored MIT LICENSE and the 15 process SKILL.md files, and reports whether KOSIF and how many process skills are installed under ~/.claude/skills. Exits with code 2 if sources are missing.

commands.name: plan
commands.example: python3 scripts/superpowers_unified.py plan "Fix the crash in the montage app"
commands.does: Uses a fixed keyword table (English and Arabic) to return an ordered list of process skills, starting with using-superpowers and ending with verification-before-completion, adding test-driven-development for code/app tasks.

commands.name: list
commands.does: Lists the 15 vendored process-skill names.

commands.name: install
commands.does: Copies the whole kosif-superpowers folder (~30 MB) and the 15 process skills into ~/.claude/skills; identical copies are reported already_current and differing existing ones are skipped unless --force is given, which backs them up to ~/.claude/backups/kosif-ultimate-<UTC stamp> before replacing. Without --no-global-instructions it also appends a marked policy block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (backing up an existing file first).

tools.inputs: A task text for plan. It reads vendor/obra-superpowers-v7/skills/*/SKILL.md and LICENSE. install targets the user's home directory (~/.claude).
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout. install also writes ~/.claude/skills/<name>/, ~/.claude/backups/kosif-ultimate-<stamp>/ and, unless --no-global-instructions, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.
tools.consent: install writes outside the repository: it copies 16 skill folders (about 30 MB) into ~/.claude/skills, replaces existing ones with --force (after backing them up), and appends to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md unless --no-global-instructions is given. Get explicit user approval before running install. doctor, plan and list are read-only.
tools.limits: plan is a fixed keyword-to-skill lookup and doctor checks only that files exist; neither one runs, verifies or tests any skill.
tools.evidence_note: 7/7 passed (6 exercise this script, including install twice in temporary home directories; 1 checks package_skill.py; the --force backup path is not tested)

tools.title_ar: أداة سطر أوامر لأطلس أنماط KOSIF
tools.summary_en: Searches, lists and shows records of the motion-graphics style atlas (289 records in catalog/styles.json). It also fills a ready-to-paste Claude Code request from templates/claude_request.<lang>.txt, scaffolds a project folder (STYLE.md, PLAN.md, TEST_REPORT.md, words.json, REQUEST.md and an optional starter copy), prints catalog statistics and runs the repository validator.
tools.summary_ar: يبحث في أطلس أنماط الموشن جرافيك (289 سجلًا في catalog/styles.json)، ويسرد سجلاته ويعرض أيًّا منها بالتفصيل. ويملأ كذلك طلبًا جاهزًا للصق في Claude Code من القالب templates/claude_request.<lang>.txt، وينشئ مجلد مشروع يضم STYLE.md وPLAN.md وTEST_REPORT.md وwords.json وREQUEST.md مع نسخة اختيارية من مشروع بداية، ويطبع إحصاءات الفهرس ويشغّل فاحص المستودع.
use_when: دوّر لي على استايل موشن عربي كينتك في الأطلس
أبغى طلب جاهز لـ Claude Code لاستايل معيّن بمقاس 9:16 ومدة 15 ثانية
جهّز لي مجلد مشروع فيديو من استايل kinetic-arabic مع ستارتر html-canvas
find a whiteboard or kinetic typography style in the atlas
scaffold a motion-graphics project from a catalog style
how many styles per category are in the catalog?

commands.name: list
commands.does: Shows a table of styles (id, name, categories, type, rank). Filters by category key or label, origin (PromptsMotion|KOSIF) and type; sorts by rank, name or published date; --json prints the full records.

commands.name: search
commands.does: Case-insensitive free-text search. Every word must match somewhere in the id, names, creator, keywords, summaries or category labels; words found in the id score higher.

commands.name: show
commands.does: Prints styles/<id>/STYLE.json, then BRIEF.md when present, then the category playbook paths (and whether each exists) and the SKILL.md path. An unknown id suggests close matches.

commands.name: prompt
commands.example: python3 tools/kosif.py prompt kinetic-arabic --lang en --aspect 9:16 --duration 15 --source "audio voice.mp3" --audio keep
commands.does: Fills the ar or en request template with the style, playbooks, aspect and resolution, fps, duration, source, stack, brand, audio policy and on-screen language. Prints the request, or writes it with --out FILE (parent folders are created).

commands.name: scaffold
commands.does: Creates a project folder with filled STYLE.md, PLAN.md and TEST_REPORT.md, a words.json copied from templates/words.example.json, and REQUEST.md; optionally copies starters/html-canvas or starters/remotion without node_modules. Refuses a non-empty folder unless --force is given.

commands.name: validate
commands.does: Runs tools/validate.py in a child Python process on the same --root, passes extra flags through (--quiet, --json) and exits with its code.

commands.name: stats
commands.does: Prints counts by origin, type, category and aspect_label, the top creators, BRIEF.md coverage and how many category playbooks exist.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Prints the bilingual usage text (exit 0). With no arguments it prints the same text and exits 2; `<command> --help` shows that subcommand's options.

tools.inputs: A style id (for example kinetic-arabic or pm-ror-fly-9950f1) or free-text search words. prompt and scaffold take --lang ar|en, --aspect (W:H, WxH or a name such as reel or cinema), --fps, --duration, --source "audio voice.mp3" | "video clip.mp4" | "text script.md" | free text, --stack auto|remotion|canvas|svg|three, --brand, --audio keep|music|sfx|silent|free text, --content-lang ar|en|both and --notes; scaffold also takes --starter html-canvas|remotion|none and --force. It reads catalog/styles.json, catalog/categories.json, styles/<id>/, templates/ and starters/ under --root or $KOSIF_ROOT (default: this checkout).
tools.outputs: Tables or JSON on stdout for list, search and stats; STYLE.json, BRIEF.md and playbook paths for show; request text on stdout or in the --out file for prompt; for scaffold, a project folder with STYLE.md, PLAN.md, TEST_REPORT.md, words.json, REQUEST.md and an optional <starter>/ copy; for validate, the validator's report and exit code. Exit 1 on user errors (unknown id or category, non-empty folder), 2 when no command is given or argparse rejects an argument.
tools.consent: scaffold writes into the chosen folder; with --force it overwrites STYLE.md, PLAN.md, TEST_REPORT.md, words.json, REQUEST.md and starter files already there, so confirm the destination first. prompt --out overwrites that file. validate only spawns the repo's own read-only tools/validate.py with the same Python.
tools.limits: It only searches and scaffolds from the motion style atlas (catalog/styles.json); it does not search the skill's 4,700-power catalog, render video or install starter dependencies (it only prints an npm install reminder).
tools.evidence_note: tests.test_cli 17/17 passed (fixture and real-repo cases); tests.test_aspects 4/4 passed (its CLI case runs `kosif.py prompt --aspect` for 2.35:1, 3:4 and cinema). Live: list, search, show, prompt, stats --json, validate --quiet (14/14 OK) and scaffold into a scratch folder all exited 0.

tools.title_ar: بوابة حفظ الحقائق عند إعادة الصياغة
tools.summary_en: Compares a text before and after a rewrite (English and Arabic) and reports every factual anchor that was dropped or added (quotes, numbers in digits or words, currencies, months, weekdays, emails, URLs, paths, @handles, versions, ratios/times and must-keep names), returning PASS or REVIEW_REQUIRED.
tools.summary_ar: يقارن النص قبل إعادة الصياغة وبعدها (بالعربية والإنجليزية) ويعرض كل مرتكز حقائقي حُذف أو أُضيف: الاقتباسات، والأرقام بالأرقام أو بالحروف، والعملات، والشهور، وأيام الأسبوع، وعناوين البريد، والروابط، والمسارات، والحسابات، والإصدارات، والنسب والأوقات، والأسماء التي يجب أن تبقى، ثم يعطي النتيجة PASS أو REVIEW_REQUIRED.
use_when: اتأكد إن إعادة الصياغة ما غيرتش أي رقم أو اسم أو تاريخ
تحقق أن البرومبت المحسّن ما ضيّع تفاصيل طلبي الأصلي
قارن النص الأصلي بالنسخة المعدلة وقل لي وش انحذف من الحقائق
check that my rewrite kept every number, name and link
verify the optimized prompt didn't drop any of the user's details
gate a humanized draft so no facts were invented or lost

commands.name: rewrite (files)
commands.does: Default rewrite mode: PASS only if nothing was dropped and nothing was added. --text prints a one-line summary instead of JSON. Exits 0 on PASS, 2 on REVIEW_REQUIRED.

commands.name: --keep (must-keep names file)
commands.does: Adds terms (one per line) that must survive; they are counted by presence, not by count. Prints the JSON report.

commands.name: inline text + --keep-term
commands.example: python3 scripts/anchor_gate.py --before-text "قابلنا أحمد يوم الخميس" --after-text "قابلنا محمود يوم الجمعة" --keep-term أحمد --text
commands.does: Compares inline strings; --keep-term can be repeated.

commands.name: --mode prompt
commands.does: Prompt mode: PASS when nothing was dropped; additions are listed for review (for checking an optimized prompt against the user's raw prompt).

commands.name: stdin
commands.does: Reads one side from stdin ('-'); giving '-' for both sides is a usage error (exit 64).

tools.inputs: Exactly one of --before/--before-text and one of --after/--after-text (UTF-8 files up to 5 MB, or '-' for stdin on one side), plus an optional --keep file, repeatable --keep-term, --mode rewrite|prompt and --text.
tools.outputs: JSON (status, mode, dropped, added, kept count, note) or a one-line --text summary on stdout. Exit 0 PASS, 2 REVIEW_REQUIRED, 64 usage or file error.
tools.limits: It only checks that surface anchors survived, so a PASS does not prove that meaning, tone, attribution or unlisted names were preserved.
tools.evidence_note: 62/62 checks passed (cd /home/user/kosif-tool && python3 -I .claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/proofs/general-writing/test_writing.py); shared with tell_scan; includes CLI exit codes 0/2/64.

tools.summary_en: Computes a deterministic back-of-envelope capacity estimate (average and peak RPS, minimum replicas, logical and replicated storage in bytes and GiB) from caller-supplied traffic and hardware assumptions, using exact decimal arithmetic.
tools.summary_ar: يحسب تقديرًا تقريبيًا حتميًا لسعة النظام (متوسط الطلبات في الثانية وذروتها، والحد الأدنى من النسخ المتماثلة، والتخزين المنطقي والمكرَّر بالبايت والجيبيبايت) انطلاقًا من افتراضات الحِمل والعتاد التي يقدّمها المستخدم، وبحساب عشري دقيق.
use_when: احسب لي كم سيرفر محتاج لو عندي مليون طلب في اليوم
قدّر مساحة التخزين المطلوبة لمدة الاحتفاظ دي
كم نسخة نحتاج للخدمة وقت الذروة؟
estimate replicas and storage for 10M requests per day
do a back-of-envelope system design sizing
how much storage for 30-day retention with 2 copies

commands.name: size
commands.does: Prints JSON with status, the echoed inputs, average_rps, peak_rps, peak_rps_ceiling, minimum_replicas, logical_storage_bytes, retained_storage_bytes, storage_gib, assumptions, exclusions, executed_benchmark=false and source_reference.

tools.inputs: Six required decimal assumptions, each finite and > 0: --daily-requests, --peak-factor (>= 1), --payload-bytes, --retention-days, --replica-rps and --target-utilization (<= 1); plus optional --copies (a positive integer, default 1).
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout (status deterministic_estimate_not_load_test, executed_benchmark false). It exits 2 with an argparse error on missing, non-numeric or out-of-range inputs.
tools.limits: Linear arithmetic on assumed numbers only; it runs no load test and leaves out indexes, log overhead, backups, compression, burst shape, network, CDN, failover headroom and regional placement.
tools.evidence_note: 9/9 ArchitectureSizerTests passed (cd /home/user/kosif-tool && python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/evals -p test_system_python.py; file total 15/15 including python_package_probe tests). The example command was also run here: 1 replica, 1,209,600,000 retained bytes, 1.127 GiB.

tools.summary_en: Turns one problem statement into a reproducible, ranked JSON list of falsifiable engineering ideas (16 TRIZ-style inventive methods × 4 lenses), each with a hypothesis, test, success metric and rejection threshold.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل وصف مشكلة واحدة إلى قائمة JSON مرتّبة وقابلة لإعادة الإنتاج من أفكار هندسية قابلة للتفنيد (16 طريقة ابتكار على نهج TRIZ × 4 زوايا)، لكل فكرة فرضية واختبار ومقياس نجاح وحدّ للرفض.
use_when: اقترح لي حلول مبتكرة لمشكلة بطء الترجمة على الموبايل
عايز أفكار جديدة لتحسين الأداة دي مع معايير نجاح واضحة
ابغى أفكار هندسية قابلة للاختبار لمشكلة عندي
brainstorm falsifiable engineering alternatives for this bottleneck
invent options to make our render pipeline more resilient
give me TRIZ-style ideas with kill criteria

commands.name: methods
commands.does: Prints the 16 inventive methods (method, technique, suggested experiment) as JSON.

commands.name: invent
commands.example: python3 scripts/invention_lab.py invent "Make Arabic captions render faster on mobile" --count 12 --constraint "no paid APIs"
commands.does: Prints schema kosif-invention-candidates-v1 JSON with up to --count (1-64, default 12) candidates sorted by a deterministic heuristic priority; --constraint is repeatable and the first six values are copied into every candidate's risk field.

tools.inputs: methods: nothing. invent: a problem statement of 8-2000 characters after whitespace normalization (positional), optional --count 1-64 (default 12) and repeatable --constraint strings.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout. For invent: schema kosif-invention-candidates-v1 with problem, constraints, disclaimer and candidates (id, method, lens, proposal, hypothesis, test, success_metric, failure_threshold, novelty_status, risk, cost_class, priority_score). Exit 2 with an argparse error for a missing/short problem or an out-of-range --count.
tools.limits: Fills fixed templates from the problem string and ranks them with a SHA-256-seeded heuristic, so it gives no real novelty, feasibility, cost or patent assessment.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed (cd /home/user/kosif-tool && python3 -m unittest tests.test_invention_lab); the tests call make_ideas() directly, not the CLI. CLI --help, methods and invent were also run here and parsed correctly.

tools.summary_en: Scans English and Arabic (MSA and Egyptian) prose for stock 'AI-sounding' writing habits and tool leftovers, and reports each hit with its line, strength and an overall verdict (EDIT/REVIEW/LOOK/LEAVE/CLEAN).

راجع المقال وطلّع العبارات الآلية قبل ما أنشره

scan this draft for AI writing tells before I publish

commands.name: scan
commands.does: Prints a human report per file: verdict, word and sentence stats, then each hit (strength, rule id, line, label, matched text), strongest first.

commands.name: scan --json
commands.does: Prints a machine-readable JSON report (a list when several files are given) with verdict, families, hits, rhythm stats and notes.

commands.name: stdin
commands.does: Scans text piped on stdin ('-').

commands.name: --fail-on
commands.does: Exits 1 when any file's verdict is at or above the given level (edit, review or look); useful as a gate.

commands.name: --include-code / --include-quotes
commands.does: Also scans fenced/inline code, URLs and blockquotes, and the inside of quotations (all masked by default).

commands.name: --list-rules
commands.does: Prints every rule id (pattern rules H1-H25, X1 and AR1-AR26, with gaps, plus computed rules H7, H8+, H20t, H20+, AR26d, AR26t), its strength and label, then exits.

tools.inputs: One or more UTF-8 text or Markdown files, or '-' for stdin.
tools.outputs: Human-readable report or JSON on stdout (file, verdict, verdict_text, words, sentences, mean_sentence_words, sentence_length_stdev, rhythm_note, tells_per_100_words, families, hits with id/strength/label/line/match, note). Exit 1 with --fail-on when the threshold is reached; exit 2 on usage or read errors.
tools.limits: A regex-based editing aid that shows where to look; it is not an authorship or AI detector, and it never rewrites text or judges meaning.
tools.evidence_note: 62/62 checks passed (cd /home/user/kosif-tool && python3 -I .claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/proofs/general-writing/test_writing.py); a script-style runner, not unittest, shared with anchor_gate; includes CLI exit-code checks for --fail-on and --list-rules.

tools.summary_en: Turns thinking procedures into checkable text scaffolds. It picks a reasoning level (L0–L6), writes a task contract, ranks 63 mental models, drafts a backcast plan, builds an idea matrix from catalog powers, scores a weighted decision with sensitivity, runs a Monte-Carlo Fermi estimate and flags weak wording in a draft.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل إجراءات التفكير إلى قوالب نصية قابلة للفحص. يختار مستوى التفكير (L0–L6)، ويكتب عقد المهمة، ويرتّب 63 نموذجًا ذهنيًا، ويصوغ خطة بالتخطيط العكسي، ويبني مصفوفة أفكار من قدرات الكتالوج، ويقيّم قرارًا موزونًا مع اختبار الحساسية، ويجري تقدير فيرمي بطريقة مونت كارلو، ويرصد الصياغات الضعيفة في المسودة.
use_when: فكّر بعمق في المهمة دي قبل ما تبدأ
اعطني أفكار مبتكرة لريل الجمعة
Which option should I choose? Run a weighted decision with sensitivity
Estimate the range for users × conversion × price
راجع المسودة وطلّع لي العبارات المبالغ فيها
Plan the course launch over 6 weeks

commands.name: ladder
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py ladder "design a 30-day plan for a course launch"
commands.does: Picks the reasoning level L0–L6 from keywords (default L2; tasks over 25 words go to at least L4), prints its steps, and from L4 up the models worth running

commands.name: frame
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py frame "a 15 s reel at 30 fps"
commands.does: Prints a contract template: goal, reader, done-criteria, constraints (numbers pulled from the task), non-goals, unknowns, first probe, plus the powers.py suggest and requirements.py plan commands for the task

commands.name: models
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py models "pricing a new subscription" -n 3 --json
commands.does: Ranks mental models from data/mental_models.json and prints each one's question, steps, output and pitfall

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Backcast plan template: end state, week milestones, WBS skeleton, critical path, pre-mortem, kill criteria

commands.name: ideas
commands.does: Idea matrix: creative operators paired with nearby and far-domain catalog powers, with each power's requirements

commands.name: decide
commands.does: Weighted decision matrix; JSON with totals, winner, margin, robust, and the flips under a ±1 weight change

commands.name: fermi
commands.example: python3 scripts/think.py fermi "a*b*c" --range a=1:3 b=10:20 c=0.1:0.3 --samples 2000
commands.does: Monte-Carlo range (log-uniform when lo>0, default 20,000 samples, --seed 7) for an arithmetic factor tree; JSON with p10, p50, p90, mean and samples

commands.name: critic
commands.does: Flags intensifiers, unverified claims, absolutes, vague lists, AI-tell words and bare completion claims, with file:line, and counts the digits in the text

tools.inputs: A task, problem, goal or seed sentence. decide takes a JSON file {"criteria": {name: weight}, "scores": {option: {criterion: score}}}. fermi takes an arithmetic expression plus --range name=lo:hi for every name. critic takes a text or Markdown file.
tools.outputs: Text templates on stdout (ladder, frame, plan, ideas, and critic flags), or JSON (models --json, decide, fermi). Nothing is written to disk.
tools.limits: It produces templates and keyword-based rankings to think with; the blanks (…) still have to be filled and tested, it does not reason about or verify claims by itself, and critic is a plain regex sweep that misses Arabic words written with tanween (جدًا، دائمًا).
tools.evidence_note: 9/9 passed (python3 -m unittest tests.test_think)

tools.title_en: Pro Council: five opposing members, three rounds, a scored verdict
tools.title_ar: مجلس البرو: خمسة أعضاء متعارضين وثلاث جولات وحكم بالدرجات
tools.summary_en: Plans a five-member adversarial council for a request (Visionary, Skeptic, Builder, Audience, Guardian, each with its own evidence lane and a specialisation from the brief's deliverable), writes every member's prompt for each round (independent positions, cross-examination, scored vote), validates and fingerprints each answer, refuses secrets, and computes a Borda verdict with recorded dissent, warnings and a SHA-256 receipt. It never calls a model: Claude runs the members as separate agents, or labels them COUNCIL_SIMULATED.
tools.summary_ar: يخطط لمجلس من خمسة أعضاء متعارضين (المبتكر، محامي الشيطان، المهندس العملي، صوت الجمهور، الحارس)، لكل منهم مسار أدلة مختلف وتخصص حسب مخرج الطلب، ويكتب مطالبة كل عضو في كل جولة (مواقف مستقلة، استجواب متبادل، تصويت بالدرجات)، ويتحقق من كل رد ويبصمه ويرفض الأسرار، ثم يحسب حكمًا بطريقة بوردا مع الرأي المخالف والتحذيرات وإيصال SHA-256. لا يستدعي أي نموذج: Claude يشغّل الأعضاء وكلاء منفصلين، أو يسميهم COUNCIL_SIMULATED.
use_when: اعمل مجلس خمسة يتناقشوا في الفكرة دي قبل ما تقرر
وضع البرو: عايز نقاش بين آراء متعارضة
Run a five-member adversarial council on these three plans
Debate this decision with opposing experts and give me the verdict and the dissent

commands.name: plan
commands.example: python3 scripts/council.py plan "اعمل ريلز دعاء" --dir out/demo/council --options A,B,C
commands.does: Writes council.json: five members with stances, evidence lanes and a specialisation, the options and the session rules.

commands.name: prompts
commands.does: Writes prompts_r<N>.json with one prompt per member; round 2 and 3 include the earlier rounds and refuse to run before the previous round is complete.

commands.name: ingest
commands.example: python3 scripts/council.py ingest --dir out/demo/council --round 1 --member M1 --file m1.json
commands.does: Validates one member's JSON answer for a round, refuses secrets, fingerprints it and records it (--simulated marks a voice written in Claude's own context).

commands.name: status
commands.does: Shows which members answered which rounds.

commands.name: verdict
commands.does: Sums round-3 scores per option, records the dissent and warnings (NO_DISSENT, CLOSE_CALL, WEAK_EVIDENCE), and writes verdict.json and minutes.md with a SHA-256 receipt.

tools.inputs: A request in the user's words, an optional USIP brief.json (options = its plans), and per-member JSON answers.
tools.outputs: council.json, prompts_r1..3.json, verdict.json and minutes.md in the --dir folder; JSON on stdout; exit 2 with one line on stderr on any refusal.
tools.consent: Writes only inside the --dir folder; it runs no model, spends nothing and publishes nothing.
tools.limits: The council's quality depends on the members Claude runs; the script checks structure, evidence fields and votes, not whether an argument is correct, and a council without separate agents is only COUNCIL_SIMULATED.
tools.evidence_note: evals/test_council.py 6/6 passed on this checkout; one real five-agent council run on 22-10 (proofs/pro-council-20261022: COUNCIL_RUN, B 25 / A 17 / C 10).

tools.summary_en: Standard-library Python module that turns any aspect spec (W:H ratio, WxH pixels, or an English/Arabic platform name such as reel, cinema or مربع) into a label and even pixel dimensions, plus ratio, resolution-string and validity helpers.
tools.summary_ar: وحدة بايثون لا تعتمد إلا على المكتبة القياسية، تحوّل أي صيغة لنسبة الأبعاد (نسبة W:H، أو أبعاد WxH بالبكسل، أو اسم منصة بالإنجليزية أو العربية مثل reel أو سينما أو مربع) إلى تسمية وأبعاد بكسل زوجية، مع دوال لحساب النسبة ونص الدقة والتحقق من الصحة.
use_when: What pixel size should a 2.35:1 cinema video be?
Resolve 'reel' or '21:9' to an even H.264-safe resolution
كم أبعاد فيديو مقاس سينمائي أو مربع؟
ابي أعرف الدقة المناسبة لمقاس تيك توك
Validate the aspect the user typed before scaffolding

commands.name: import
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import aspects; print(aspects.resolve('2.35:1'))"
commands.does: Imports the module from the skill root; prints ('2.35:1', 1920, 818).

commands.name: resolve
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import resolve; print(resolve('ريلز'))"
commands.does: Returns (label, width, height) with even dimensions; here ('9:16', 1080, 1920). Raises ValueError for unreadable specs or W:H ratios outside 1:5–5:1 (explicit WxH sizes are not range-checked).

commands.name: ratio_of
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import ratio_of; print(ratio_of('1920x816'))"
commands.does: Returns width/height as a float for any accepted spec (2.3529… here).

commands.name: resolution
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import resolution; print(resolution('cinema'))"
commands.does: Returns a 'WxH' string; cinema -> 1920x804.

commands.name: is_valid
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from aspects import is_valid; print(is_valid('foo'))"
commands.does: Returns True/False instead of raising (False here).

tools.inputs: An aspect spec string: integer or decimal W:H (9:16, 2.35:1), explicit WxH pixels (1920x816), or a name (reel, story, tiktok, shorts, youtube, square, feed, portrait, classic, cinema, scope, ultrawide, flat, or Arabic names such as ريلز، مربع، سينما، تيك توك).
tools.outputs: (label, width, height) tuple with even dimensions; float ratio; 'WxH' string; boolean validity.
tools.limits: Only maps aspect specs to even pixel sizes (1080 px short side for ratios between 9:16 and 16:9, otherwise a 1920 px long side; W:H limited to 1:5–5:1); it does not resize, crop or reframe media.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed (imports the byte-identical repo copy tools/aspects.py; evals/test_hub.py BundledCopiesTest, which passed, enforces that the copies match). Also imported the skill copy and ran all five examples: outputs as documented.

tools.summary_en: Turns a kosif.audio-cues.v1 JSON (measured onsets plus aligned words from audio_cue_mapper.py) into an editable motion_director storyboard with timed text, a draw-on path, a character and a camera zoom, plus a decision report that scores the doodle, kinetic and cinematic styles.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملف JSON بصيغة kosif.audio-cues.v1 (بدايات الأصوات المقيسة والكلمات المحاذاة الناتجة عن audio_cue_mapper.py) إلى لوحة قصة قابلة للتحرير بصيغة motion_director، فيها نص موقوت ومسار يُرسم تدريجيًا وشخصية وتقريب للكاميرا، مع تقرير قرار يقيّم أساليب doodle وkinetic وcinematic.

اعمل لي مشاهد متزامنة مع الصوت من ملف cues.json
أبغى لوحة قصة رأسية للريلز مبنية على توقيت كلماتي
turn my audio cues and word timings into an editable motion storyboard
pick a doodle, kinetic or cinematic style for this voiceover and build scenes
generate a 9:16 scene plan synced to the narration

commands.name: plan (auto style)
commands.does: Validates the cues, scores the three styles with a declared heuristic, cuts the audio into scenes (target 6 s, inside a 2-9 s window) at pauses or word ends, and writes a new 1080x1920 30 fps storyboard JSON and a decision/evidence report. commands.name: plan (forced style, landscape)

tools.title_ar: مُصرِّف حركة SVG المتزامنة مع الصوت
tools.summary_en: Validates a word-timed JSON scene spec (paths, circles, text, characters, rigged actors, morphs, camera) and compiles it into a self-contained seekable SVG/HTML animation, with an optional MP4 render through render_html.cjs.
tools.summary_ar: يتحقق من ملف مشاهد بصيغة JSON مُوقَّت على مستوى الكلمات (مسارات ودوائر ونصوص وشخصيات وممثلون بمفاصل وتحوّلات أشكال وحركة كاميرا)، ثم يحوّله إلى رسم متحرك SVG/HTML مستقل يمكن الانتقال فيه إلى أي لحظة، مع تصيير اختياري إلى MP4 عبر render_html.cjs.

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Probes for the motion engine asset, render_html.cjs, node, ffmpeg and ffprobe; renders nothing.

commands.name: sample
commands.does: Writes a valid 9-second, 3-scene 1080x1920 Arabic demo spec (refuses an existing path).

commands.name: compile
commands.does: Validates the spec and writes a new self-contained HTML/SVG animation exposing window.__kosif.seek(t); status html_compiled_not_rendered.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Runs node render_html.cjs --mode seek --offline (Playwright Chromium + ffmpeg, 20-minute timeout) to write a new MP4, optionally muxing the user's audio; result is marked verified:false.

tools.inputs: Motion Director spec JSON v1: even width/height 320–4096, fps 24/25/30/60, duration 0.1–120 s, 1–30 continuous scenes with monotonic word timings (≤240 words each), camera zoom/pan, ≤80 elements in total of type path|circle|text|character|actor|morph with hex colours; for render an existing HTML file, a new .mp4 path and an optional audio file.
tools.outputs: JSON status on stdout; sample spec JSON; self-contained seekable HTML animation; optional MP4 (unverified) from render. Exit 0 ok, 1 render_failed, 2 validation/IO error.
tools.consent: render launches node + headless Playwright Chromium + ffmpeg (timeout up to 20 min) and writes an MP4 muxed with the user's audio: confirm before rendering. sample/compile only create new files and never overwrite.
tools.limits: Compiles only its own validated vector primitives (≤80 elements, ≤120 s); it does not read words.json directly, transcribe or align audio, or verify the rendered MP4.
tools.evidence_note: test_motion_director.py 15/15 passed; test_creative_intelligence.py 6/6 passed (it only calls validate() on a generated storyboard). The MP4 path is tested only for refusal; no real render was run. Also ran doctor, sample and compile into scratch: OK (3 scenes, 7 elements, 270 frames); render to a non-.mp4 path was refused with exit 2.

tools.summary_en: A browser-side script (IIFE), inlined by motion_director.py compile, that reads scene JSON from <script id=kosif-data> and animates an SVG film deterministically: stroke draw-on, text fades, polygon morphs, a stick character, pivot-rigged actors (walk/run/wave/point/sit) with a moving pen tip, per-scene camera zoom/pan and word-timed RTL captions, all through window.__kosif.seek(t) for frame-exact rendering.
tools.summary_ar: سكربت يعمل في المتصفح يدمجه الأمر motion_director.py compile، يقرأ بيانات المشاهد بصيغة JSON من الوسم <script id=kosif-data> ويحرّك فيلم SVG بشكل حتمي: يرسم الخطوط تدريجيًا، ويُظهر النصوص بالتلاشي، ويحوّل المضلعات من شكل إلى آخر، ويحرّك شخصية خطية وممثلين بمفاصل محورية (مشي، جري، تلويح، إشارة، جلوس) مع رأس قلم متحرك، ويكبّر الكاميرا ويحرّكها لكل مشهد، ويعرض ترجمة عربية من اليمين إلى اليسار موقّتة بالكلمات، وكل ذلك عبر الدالة window.__kosif.seek(t) لرندر دقيق إطارًا بإطار.

اعمل فيلم SVG فيه ترجمة عربية كلمة بكلمة على توقيت الصوت
Animate my SVG scene with draw-on strokes, a walking character and word-timed captions
Build a seekable whiteboard animation I can render to MP4

commands.name: embed
commands.does: Validates the scene spec, escapes it into <script id=kosif-data> and inlines this engine into a new self-contained HTML film. It refuses an existing output and needs the folder to exist. For a demo spec, run `python3 scripts/motion_director.py sample --out ./out/scene.json`.

commands.name: seek
commands.example: window.__kosif.seek(2.5)  // in the compiled page: draws t=2.5 s, returns {time, scene, word}
commands.does: Draws the exact frame for time t (clamped to 0..duration) and returns the active scene id and caption word. render_html.cjs calls it for every frame in seek mode.

commands.name: check
commands.does: Syntax-checks the engine source, as documented in references/executable-creative-motion.md.

tools.inputs: Scene JSON (validated by motion_director.py): {width, height, fps, duration, scenes:[{id, start, end, background, camera{fromZoom, toZoom, fromX, toX, fromY, toY, start, end}, words[{text, start, end}], elements[{type: path|circle|text|character|actor|morph, start, end, move{fromX, toX, fromY, toY, start, end}, ...}]}]}. It must be embedded in a page that has #kosif-data, #background, #stage, #art and #captions; #scene is looked up but not used.
tools.outputs: Live SVG DOM state for each seek(t), plus window.__kosif = {duration, fps, seek, source} and window.__kosifReady (a fonts-ready promise). The engine writes no files; the embed command writes one new HTML file.
tools.limits: Draws simple SVG strokes, polygon morphs and stick-figure rigs only and shows one caption word at a time. It needs a host page and a separate renderer (render_html.cjs) to become MP4, and it is not a general animation editor.
tools.evidence_note: node --test test_motion_engine.mjs: 3/3 passed. node --test test_code_drawing_engine.mjs: 7/7 passed. unittest test_motion_director.py: 15/15 passed (it checks the engine's seek/draw contract and inlines it via compile). node --check passes.

tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملف توقيت الكلمات بصيغة motion-starter-kit (lines[].words[]) إلى لوحة قصة أصلية لـ KOSIF Motion Director بعد التحقق منها، مع معاينة HTML اختيارية يمكن الانتقال فيها إلى أي لحظة، بأنماط plotter وdoodle وwhiteboard وinfographic.

tools.summary_en: A dependency-free ES module that exports 12 deterministic, seekable animation primitives: clamp, easing, keyframe interpolation and timelines, SVG stroke reveal, camera pan/zoom, walk-cycle joint angles, parallax, seeded hand-drawn line jitter, HH:MM:SS:FF timecode, whole-word caption cue state and a render frame-contract check.
tools.summary_ar: وحدة ES بلا اعتماديات تصدّر 12 دالة حركة حتمية يمكن الانتقال بها إلى أي لحظة: حصر القيم ضمن مدى، ومنحنيات التسهيل، والاستيفاء بين الإطارات المفتاحية وخطوط الزمن، وكشف خطوط SVG تدريجيًا، وتحريك الكاميرا وتكبيرها، وزوايا مفاصل دورة المشي، واختلاف المنظر (البارالاكس)، واهتزاز الخط اليدوي ببذرة ثابتة، والرمز الزمني بصيغة HH:MM:SS:FF، وحالة الترجمة على مستوى الكلمة الكاملة، والتحقق من عقد الإطارات قبل الرندر.
use_when: أبي دوال جاهزة للـ easing والكي فريم في الأنيميشن بتاعي
اعمل لي خط مرسوم باليد بشكل ثابت يتكرر بنفس الشكل
احسب لي عدد الإطارات والتايم كود لفيديو 8 ثواني 30 فريم
Give me deterministic easing/keyframe helpers for a seekable SVG animation
I need walk-cycle and camera zoom math for my HTML film

commands.name: import
commands.does: Loads the module from the skill root and prints '0.5 00:00:02:15'. All 12 names (clamp, ease, interpolate, timeline, strokeReveal, camera, walkRig, parallax, seededSketchLine, timeCode, wordCueState, assertFrameContract) can be imported the same way in Node.js or an ES-module browser page; no npm packages are needed.

commands.name: ease
commands.example: ease(0.5, "cubic")  // 0.5; kinds: linear | smooth | in | out | cubic
commands.does: Clamps u to 0..1 and applies the named easing curve (default smooth). Throws on an unknown kind.

commands.name: interpolate
commands.does: Eases from `from` to `to` between times a and b. Throws if b<=a or any value is non-finite.

commands.name: timeline
commands.does: A multi-keyframe track with held endpoints. Keyframe times must strictly increase.

commands.name: strokeReveal
commands.does: Returns dasharray/dashoffset values that draw an SVG path of the given length like a pen between start and end.

commands.name: camera
commands.example: camera(4, {end:8, zoomEnd:1.1, panX:20, centerX:540, centerY:960})  // {zoom:1.05, x:-17, y:-48}
commands.does: Returns {zoom, x, y} for an eased zoom about the centre plus a pan.

commands.name: walkRig
commands.does: Returns leg and arm angles in degrees plus an `active` value that eases in over 0.5 s after onset.

commands.name: parallax
commands.does: Scales the camera offset by a layer depth from 0 to 1.

commands.name: seededSketchLine
commands.does: Returns steps+1 jittered points that look hand-drawn. The jitter fades to zero at both ends, so the endpoints stay on the line within floating-point error, and the same seed always gives the same line.

commands.name: timeCode
commands.does: Formats seconds as HH:MM:SS:FF (non-drop-frame) at an integer fps from 1 to 240.

commands.name: wordCueState
commands.does: Returns per-word active/progress state for caption timing without splitting Arabic words.

commands.name: assertFrameContract
commands.does: Checks the duration (0–3600 s), the integer fps (1–120) and an even width/height of at least 64 px before rendering, and returns the total frame count.

commands.name: clamp
commands.does: Clamps a number into [min, max], 0..1 by default.

tools.inputs: Plain numbers and objects passed as function arguments: times in seconds, keyframe arrays [{time, value}], word cues [{word, start, end}] and option objects.
tools.outputs: New plain values or objects (numbers, {strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}, {zoom, x, y}, point arrays, timecode strings). Invalid input throws an Error, and no files are written.
tools.limits: Supplies math primitives only: it draws, renders and edits nothing, and has just five easing curves and a single sine-based walk cycle.
tools.evidence_note: node --test evals/test_motion_toolkit.mjs: 10/10 passed. The node one-liner and all 12 function examples were also run here and returned the values shown.

tools.summary_en: The skill's bundled copy of KOSIF's deterministic HTML-to-MP4 renderer: it captures a local or http HTML film frame by frame in headless Chromium (through window.__kosif.seek(t) or Chromium virtual time), encodes H.264 with ffmpeg, optionally muxes untouched audio and checks fps, frames, duration, size and audio with ffprobe, or with --preview makes an 8-frame contact sheet instead.
tools.summary_ar: نسخة مضمّنة في المهارة من عارض KOSIF الحتمي لتحويل HTML إلى MP4: يلتقط فيلم HTML محليًا أو عبر رابط http إطارًا بإطار في Chromium بلا واجهة (عبر window.__kosif.seek(t) أو الزمن الافتراضي في Chromium)، ويرمّزه بصيغة H.264 عبر ffmpeg، ويدمج الصوت اختياريًا دون تعديله، ثم يتحقق بـ ffprobe من معدل الإطارات وعددها والمدة والأبعاد والصوت، أو يصنع بالخيار ‎--preview لوحة معاينة من 8 إطارات بدل الفيديو.
use_when: حوّل ملف film.html لفيديو MP4 مع التعليق الصوتي
اعمل لي معاينة سريعة للأنيميشن قبل الرندر النهائي
أبي أصدّر الموشن جرافيك بمقاس ريلز 9:16
Render this HTML animation to a 1080x1920 MP4 at 30 fps with my voiceover
Make a contact-sheet preview of my HTML film before the final render

commands.name: render
commands.does: Renders every frame (seek mode if window.__kosif exists, otherwise it relaunches in virtual mode), encodes libx264 CRF 18 yuv420p, muxes the audio as AAC 192k padded to the video length, then prints a 'VERIFY OK|FAIL' line from ffprobe. Exits 3 on a mismatch.

commands.name: preview
commands.does: Captures 8 evenly spaced frames and tiles them into a 4x2 contact sheet at ./out/film_preview.png. It always appends '_preview.png' to the --out stem. Tiles are labelled when ffmpeg has drawtext. Audio is ignored.

commands.name: virtual
commands.does: Renders any CSS/WAAPI/rAF/GSAP page under the paused Chromium virtual clock in exact 1000/fps steps. --offline aborts every http(s) request and --seed replaces Math.random with a seeded PRNG, for reproducible output.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Prints every option (--aspect, --width, --height, --fps, --duration, --start, --audio, --mode, --preview, --frames-dir, --keep-frames, --crf, --scale, --seed, --offline, --timeout, --settle) and the exit codes.

tools.inputs: A local .html file or an http(s) URL. In seek mode the page exposes window.__kosif = {duration, seek(t)} (and optionally window.__kosifReady); otherwise --duration is required. Optional audio file. Options: --aspect (9:16, 16:9, 4:5, 21:9, WxH or a name such as reel/square/cinema), --start for a partial render, fps, crf, scale, seed and others.
tools.outputs: An H.264 MP4 at --out (or <out-stem>_preview.png with --preview) and a VERIFY line with duration, fps, frames, size and audio. PNG frames go to --frames-dir if given, otherwise to a temp dir that is deleted unless --keep-frames is set. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage, 2 render/encode failure, 3 ffprobe mismatch.
tools.consent: An http(s) --in URL, or a page that loads remote assets, contacts the network (use --offline to block it). It runs the page's own scripts in headless Chromium, so render only pages the user trusts. It overwrites --out, and --frames-dir deletes existing frame_######.png, preview_raw_NN.png and preview_tile_NN.png files in that folder.
tools.limits: Verifies only container metrics (fps, frame count, duration, size, audio presence), not visual or creative correctness, and it installs nothing, so Playwright Chromium and ffmpeg/ffprobe must already be present.
tools.evidence_note: No test in evals/ or tests/ executes this bundled copy. evals/test_motion_runtime.py mocks the render and, in a full repo, points at tools/render_html.cjs. Checked here: --help exits 0, and a missing --in file gives a usage error with exit 1. No render was run.

tools.summary_en: Checks a rendered video with ffprobe/ffmpeg against the request (H.264/yuv420p, even size, aspect, fps, duration and frame count, AAC audio at ≥44.1 kHz, EBU R128 loudness and true peak, master-audio length) and prints PASS/FAIL lines with an optional JSON report.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص الفيديو المُصدَّر باستخدام ffprobe وffmpeg مقابل المطلوب (ترميز H.264 وyuv420p، والأبعاد الزوجية، ونسبة الأبعاد، ومعدل الإطارات، والمدة وعدد الإطارات، وصوت AAC بتردد 44.1 كيلوهرتز فأكثر، وجهارة الصوت وفق EBU R128 والذروة الحقيقية، وتطابق طوله مع الصوت الأصلي)، ثم يطبع نتيجة كل فحص بالنجاح أو الفشل مع تقرير JSON اختياري.
use_when: Verify this MP4 is 9:16, 30 fps and 15 seconds before delivery
Check the loudness and that the audio length matches my voice file
اتأكد إن الفيديو مقاس ريلز وإن الصوت مضبوط قبل ما أسلمه
افحص الفيديو النهائي: المدة والفريمات والصوت
Is my rendered film ready to upload?

commands.name: verify
commands.does: Runs the codec/size/aspect/fps/duration/frame-count/audio/loudness checks and writes a JSON report; exit 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail.

commands.name: verify source-preserved audio
commands.does: Requires the first audio stream's packet MD5 (ADTS-normalised for AAC) to equal the source's and no other audio stream; when both hold, loudness, true peak, a sample rate under 44.1 kHz and an MP3 codec are [INFO] 'source preserved … (not normalised by design)' instead of failures; JSON gains source_audio and a status on every check.

commands.name: verify with master audio
commands.does: Adds a check that the delivered audio length matches the master audio within 50 ms.

commands.name: verify silent
commands.does: Requires that the deliverable has no audio stream and skips the audio and loudness checks.

tools.inputs: A rendered video file; optional --aspect (W:H, WxH or a name such as reel/cinema/ريلز), --fps, --duration, --audio master file, --lufs target (default -14, ±1.5 LU), --no-audio, --json path, --source-audio <the untouched source audio>.
tools.outputs: [PASS]/[FAIL]/[INFO] lines and an 'N/M checks passed' summary (INFO is never scored) on stdout; an optional JSON report (codec, size, fps, frames, pix_fmt, audio, loudness, checks; with --source-audio a status on every check and source_audio {md5_match, video_md5, source_md5}). Exit 0 when all scored checks pass, 1 when any fails, 2 when ffmpeg/ffprobe is missing or an input cannot be read (missing video, --audio or --source-audio file, a source without audio, an unreadable --aspect).
tools.limits: Checks technical delivery specs only; it does not judge visual content, caption correctness or word-level audio sync. --source-audio compares the first audio stream only (an extra stream fails the separate one-stream check).
tools.evidence_note: tests/test_verify_source_audio.py 10/10 and tests.test_tools_extra VerifyVideoTests passed here (they run the byte-identical repo copy; evals/test_hub.py BundledCopiesTest enforces the match). Without --source-audio stdout and JSON were byte-identical to the previous version on 4 test files. On 22-10 a reel_factory build muxed with -c copy matched its AAC source (packet MD5) and scored 12/12.

tools.summary_en: A standard-library-only Python module, shared by kosif.py, verify_video.py and import_briefs.py, that turns any aspect spec (a W:H ratio, WxH pixels or an English or Arabic platform name such as reel, cinema or مربع) into a label and an even pixel size, with helpers for the numeric ratio, a 'WxH' string and validity.
tools.summary_ar: وحدة بايثون لا تعتمد إلا على المكتبة القياسية، تستخدمها kosif.py وverify_video.py وimport_briefs.py، وتحوّل أي صيغة لنسبة العرض إلى تسمية وأبعاد زوجية بالبكسل. تقبل نسبة W:H أو أبعادًا بصيغة WxH أو اسم منصة أو شكل بالإنجليزية أو العربية مثل reel وcinema ومربع، وتوفّر دوال لحساب النسبة العددية وإرجاع نص الأبعاد WxH والتحقق من صلاحية الصيغة.
use_when: كم أبعاد فيديو سينمائي 2.35:1 بالبكسل؟
حوّل ريلز أو مربع إلى عرض وارتفاع
what pixel size should a 21:9 render use?
check whether '1920x816' is a valid aspect spec
resolve 'cinema' to width and height in Python

commands.name: resolve
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from aspects import resolve; print(resolve('2.35:1'))"
commands.does: Returns (label, width, height) with even dimensions; here ('2.35:1', 1920, 818). Raises ValueError for unreadable specs.

commands.name: ratio_of
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from aspects import ratio_of; print(ratio_of('cinema'))"
commands.does: Returns width/height as a float for any accepted spec (cinema gives 2.388…).

commands.name: resolution
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from aspects import resolution; print(resolution('ريلز'))"
commands.does: Returns a 'WxH' string (ريلز gives 1080x1920).

commands.name: is_valid
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from aspects import is_valid; print(is_valid('10:1'), is_valid('1920x816'))"
commands.does: Returns True or False instead of raising (prints False True).

commands.name: import
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from aspects import PRESETS, NAMES; print(PRESETS); print(sorted(NAMES))"
commands.does: Shows the four classic pixel presets and the 35 English and Arabic platform and shape names.

tools.inputs: An aspect spec string: a W:H (or W/H) ratio with integers or decimals between 1:5 and 5:1, WxH pixels with 2 to 5 digits per side (x, × or *), or a name from NAMES (English or Arabic, such as reel, story, youtube, square, feed, cinema, ultrawide, ريلز, مربع, سينما).
tools.outputs: resolve returns (label, width, height) with even dimensions: presets keep 1080x1920, 1920x1080, 1080x1080 and 1080x1350; other ratios between 9:16 and 16:9 get a 1080 px short side and ratios outside that range a 1920 px long side. ratio_of returns a float, resolution a 'WxH' string and is_valid a bool; unreadable specs raise ValueError.
tools.limits: It only maps aspect specs to even pixel sizes; it does not resize, crop or reframe media, and it has no CLI.
tools.evidence_note: tests.test_aspects 4/4 passed: sizes and evenness for 15 specs, validation of bad specs, the kosif.py prompt --aspect path, and the web/generator.js mirror checked with node. All five import examples ran here with the stated output.

tools.title_ar: محوّل حتمي من HTML إلى فيديو MP4
tools.summary_en: Renders a local or http HTML film frame by frame in headless Chromium (Playwright), driving the page through window.__kosif.seek(t) or, for any CSS/WAAPI/rAF/GSAP page, through paused Chromium virtual time. It encodes H.264 yuv420p with ffmpeg, can mux a supplied audio track re-encoded as AAC 192k without resampling or retiming it, and checks fps, frame count, duration, size and audio presence with ffprobe. With --preview it writes an 8-frame contact-sheet PNG instead of a video.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل فيلم HTML محليًا أو عبر رابط http إلى فيديو إطارًا بإطار داخل متصفح Chromium بلا واجهة (Playwright)، إما بالدالة window.__kosif.seek(t) في الصفحة، وإما بإيقاف الزمن الافتراضي للمتصفح وتقديمه خطوة خطوة لأي صفحة تعتمد CSS أو WAAPI أو requestAnimationFrame أو GSAP. ثم يرمّز الإطارات بصيغة H.264 ‏yuv420p عبر ffmpeg، ويدمج الصوت المرفق بعد ترميزه AAC بمعدل 192k دون إعادة أخذ العينات أو تغيير توقيته، ويتحقق عبر ffprobe من معدل الإطارات وعددها والمدة والأبعاد ووجود الصوت. ومع ‎--preview يُخرج لوحة PNG من ثمانية إطارات بدلًا من الفيديو.
use_when: حوّل صفحة الأنيميشن HTML لفيديو MP4 مع الصوت الأصلي
اعمل لي معاينة إطارات قبل الرندر النهائي
رندر الستارتر html-canvas بمقاس ريلز 9:16 و30 فريم
render this GSAP/CSS animation page to a 30 fps MP4

commands.name: render
commands.does: Full render: seek mode when window.__kosif exists, otherwise it relaunches in virtual mode. Muxes the audio as AAC 192k (apad + -shortest, no retiming) and prints an ffprobe 'VERIFY OK/FAIL' line; exit 3 means the output disagrees with the request.

commands.name: preview
commands.does: Captures 8 evenly spaced frames into a 4x2 contact sheet written as <out-basename>_preview.png next to --out (here ./out/film_preview.png). No video is produced and --audio is ignored.

commands.name: virtual
commands.does: Forces the virtual-time driver for a page without a seek hook; here --aspect sets 1920x1080, --offline aborts every http(s) request and --seed replaces Math.random with a seeded PRNG for a reproducible render.

commands.name: segment
commands.does: Renders only part of the film (from film time --start for --duration seconds) at a custom viewport size, as a quick motion check.

commands.name: frames-dir
commands.does: Writes and keeps the PNG frames (frame_000000.png …) in the given folder after deleting older frame_NNNNNN.png and preview_raw/tile_NN.png files there; --keep-frames instead keeps the temporary folder.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Prints the options and exit codes (0 ok, 1 usage, 2 render or encode failure, 3 ffprobe disagrees). Note: `-h` is not recognised and exits 1 with a usage error.

tools.inputs: --in takes a local .html file or an http(s) URL; --out takes an output .mp4 path. Optional: --aspect (W:H, WxH or a limited set of English names), --width/--height in CSS px, --fps, --duration (seek mode can read window.__kosif.duration), --start, --audio <file>, --mode seek|virtual, --preview, --frames-dir, --keep-frames, --crf, --scale, --seed, --offline, --timeout and --settle. Seek-mode pages expose window.__kosif = {duration, seek(t)} and an optional window.__kosifReady promise.
tools.outputs: An H.264 yuv420p MP4 with +faststart (AAC 192k when --audio is given), or a contact-sheet PNG named <out-basename>_preview.png in preview mode. It prints progress, a 'VERIFY OK|FAIL duration= fps= frames= size= audio=' line and up to 10 page console errors. Temporary frames are deleted unless --frames-dir or --keep-frames is given.

optional: bin:ffmpeg built with the drawtext filter (time labels on preview tiles)

tools.consent: An http(s) --in URL, or a page that loads remote assets, contacts the network (the html-canvas starter loads Google Fonts); --offline blocks this. It runs the page's own scripts in headless Chromium with HTTPS errors ignored, so render only pages the user trusts. It overwrites --out, and --frames-dir deletes existing frame_NNNNNN.png and preview_raw/tile_NN.png files in that folder.
tools.limits: It verifies only container metrics (fps, frame count, duration, size, audio presence), not whether the visuals are right, and it installs nothing: Playwright, its Chromium and ffmpeg/ffprobe must already be present.
tools.evidence_note: Not run: no test renders with tools/render_html.cjs; skill evals test_hub.BundledCopiesTest only checks it is byte-identical to the skill copy (1/1 passed). Here --help (exit 0) and the usage-error paths were checked with a non-existent --in; every draft example's flags parse. No render was performed.

tools.summary_en: Probes a rendered video with ffprobe and ffmpeg and checks it against the request: H.264, yuv420p, even dimensions, aspect, fps, duration and frame count, AAC audio at 44.1 kHz or more, EBU R128 integrated loudness (default -14 LUFS ±1.5), true peak ≤ -1 dBFS and master-audio length (±50 ms). It prints PASS/FAIL lines and can write a JSON report.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص الفيديو المُصدَّر عبر ffprobe وffmpeg ويقارنه بالمطلوب: ترميز H.264 وصيغة yuv420p والأبعاد الزوجية ونسبة العرض ومعدل الإطارات والمدة وعدد الإطارات، وصوت AAC بتردد لا يقل عن 44.1 كيلوهرتز. ويقيس كذلك الجهارة المتكاملة وفق EBU R128 (الهدف الافتراضي ‎-14 LUFS بسماحية ±1.5) والذروة الحقيقية التي يجب ألا تتجاوز ‎-1 dBFS، ويتحقق من تطابق طول الصوت مع الملف الأصلي (±50 ملّي ثانية). ثم يطبع سطور نجاح أو فشل، ويكتب تقرير JSON عند الطلب.
use_when: افحص الفيديو النهائي قبل التسليم: المقاس والمدة والصوت
تأكد إن الريل 9:16 و30 فريم ومدته 15 ثانية بالضبط
هل جهارة الصوت في الفيلم -14 LUFS؟

commands.name: verify
commands.does: Runs every check (13 when all options are given), including that the delivered audio length matches the master file; prints PASS/FAIL lines and 'N/M checks passed' and writes the JSON report.

commands.name: verify source-preserved audio
commands.does: Requires the first audio stream's packet MD5 (ADTS-normalised for AAC) to equal the source's and no other audio stream; when both hold, loudness, true peak, a sample rate under 44.1 kHz and an MP3 codec are [INFO] 'source preserved … (not normalised by design)' instead of failures; JSON gains source_audio and a status on every check.

commands.name: silent
commands.does: Checks an intentionally silent deliverable: requires that there is no audio stream and skips the audio checks.

commands.name: loudness-target
commands.does: Runs the codec, size and audio checks with a different integrated-loudness target (±1.5 LU).

commands.name: help
commands.does: Shows usage and the list of checks.

tools.inputs: A video file path. Optional: --aspect (W:H, WxH or a name, resolved through tools/aspects.py), --fps, --duration in seconds, --audio <master audio file>, --lufs <target, default -14>, --no-audio and --json <report path>, --source-audio <the untouched source audio>.
tools.outputs: [PASS]/[FAIL]/[INFO] lines and an 'N/M checks passed' summary (INFO is never scored) on stdout; an optional JSON report (codec, size, fps, frames, pix_fmt, audio, loudness, checks; with --source-audio a status on every check and source_audio {md5_match, video_md5, source_md5}). Exit 0 when all scored checks pass, 1 when any fails, 2 when ffmpeg/ffprobe is missing or an input cannot be read (missing video, --audio or --source-audio file, a source without audio, an unreadable --aspect).
tools.consent: --json overwrites the named report file; otherwise it only reads the video and master audio with local ffprobe/ffmpeg.
tools.limits: Checks technical delivery specs only; it does not judge visual content, caption correctness or word-level audio sync. --source-audio compares the first audio stream only (an extra stream fails the separate one-stream check).
tools.evidence_note: tests/test_verify_source_audio.py 10/10 and tests.test_tools_extra 7/7 OK here (ffmpeg/ffprobe present). --source-audio: ADTS .aac and MP4 AAC sources muxed with -c copy match; an AAC re-encode, an extra audio stream or Opus/PCM fail; output without the flag is byte-identical to the previous version.

commands.name: live-preview
commands.does: Opens the page with play, scrub and safe-area controls. Space toggles play, ?t=3.2 jumps to a time and ?autoplay=1 starts playback. The controls hide under the renderer (navigator.webdriver).

commands.name: words
commands.does: Regenerates words.js (window.KOSIF_WORDS) from SRT, VTT, Whisper JSON, CSV/TSV or words.json. The page reads words.js, so it also works from file://.

commands.name: contact-sheet
commands.does: Renders 8 evenly spaced, labelled frames into ./out/film_preview.png for approval before the final render. --offline blocks the Google Fonts request, so a system font is used.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Seek-mode render of all 360 frames with headless Chromium, encoded with libx264 by ffmpeg. The user's audio is re-encoded to AAC 192k with its timing untouched, then padded or cut to the film's 12 s.

commands.name: verify
commands.does: Delivery gate that checks codecs, size, fps, frame count, audio and loudness against the request. --audio also requires the delivered audio to match the master's length (±50 ms).

commands.name: KOSIF.Timeline
commands.example: const tl = new KOSIF.Timeline({ duration: 12, fps: 30, scenes: [{ id: 'title', t0: 0, t1: 3, draw: (t, p, local) => {} }] }); window.__kosif = { duration: 12, fps: 30, seek: (t) => tl.seek(t) };
commands.does: The in-page API from timeline.js. It also exports Ease (linear, outCubic, inOutCubic, outExpo, outQuint, outBack, inBack, spring), prog, window01, lerp, clamp01, rng(seed), cameraAt/applyCamera, activeWord and phrases.

tools.inputs: Edits to index.html (the scenes array with t0/t1/draw, camKeys, the series data, title words), word timings in words.json or words.js, and optionally a voice or music file.
tools.outputs: A live preview page, a contact-sheet PNG (<out name>_preview.png) and a 1080x1920, 30 fps, 12 s H.264/AAC MP4 through tools/render_html.cjs.
tools.consent: Unless --offline is passed, the page fetches the Cairo webfont from fonts.googleapis.com, and opening it in a browser does too. Any --audio file must be one the user has rights to (it is re-encoded to AAC with its timing untouched).
tools.limits: It is one hand-coded 12 s sample film to copy and edit, with no visual editor, and it does not render itself (render_html.cjs with Playwright Chromium and ffmpeg does).
tools.evidence_note: No test file exercises the real starter. tests/test_cli.py (17/17 passed here) only scaffolds a fixture stand-in. Manual checks here: render_html.cjs --preview --offline wrote an 8-frame contact sheet to scratch (seek mode, 360 frames, 12 s, exit 0, one expected blocked-font console error), and the frames look correct. kosif.py scaffold kinetic-arabic --starter html-canvas copied the folder into scratch. words_convert wrote 19 words from the starter's words.json to a scratch words.js. The KOSIF.Timeline example ran in node and drew at t=1.5 with p=0.5.

tools.summary_en: Renders a real camera-motion B-roll video master with FFmpeg from a production-ready cinematic_cut_planner EDL and a licensed footage manifest (push-in, pull-back and pan per shot, exact frame counts), stream-copies the original audio and verifies frame count and audio bitstream hash.
tools.summary_ar: يصيّر فيديو B-roll حقيقيًا بحركة كاميرا (تقريب وابتعاد وتحريك جانبي) عبر FFmpeg، انطلاقًا من قائمة EDL جاهزة للإنتاج وبيان لقطات مرخّصة. ينسخ مسار الصوت الأصلي دون أي تعديل، ويتحقق من عدد الإطارات ومن تطابق بصمة الصوت.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Checks EDL coverage and readiness, verifies each clip's license evidence, sha256, dimensions and length, renders every scene with an ffmpeg zoompan camera move to its exact frame count, concatenates the shots, muxes the original audio with -c:a copy, verifies frames and an identical audio packet hash, and prints a JSON report. It refuses to overwrite --out.

tools.inputs: --edl: production_ready kosif.edl.v1 JSON from cinematic_cut_planner.py; --manifest: JSON array of clips (same fields as the planner plus sha256 and license_evidence_url or license_document; relative paths resolve against the manifest folder); --audio: the original audio master whose duration matches the EDL within 0.04 s; --out: new .mkv or .mp4; --width/--height: even values >=32 (default 1080x1920).
tools.outputs: A video file (H.264 yuv420p, CRF 19) with the original audio stream copied unchanged, plus a JSON report on stdout: path, video_frames, width, height, fps, audio_codec, audio_stream_copied, audio_original_sha256, audio_packet_sha256, audio_bitstream_verified_identical, scope. Temporary shots are deleted.
tools.consent: Renders the user's footage and audio with local ffmpeg: confirm each clip's license evidence and the user's rights to the audio before running.
tools.limits: Produces only a camera-motion B-roll master (every shot starts at its clip's first frame) with no captions, Arabic text, graphics, transitions or audio mix, and its rights checks trust the manifest's declared flags.
tools.evidence_note: 3/3 passed here, including test_real_render_and_bitstream_copy (real ffmpeg 6.1.1: 60-frame two-shot 180x320 MKV with an identical PCM packet hash; refuses an overwrite and a wrong sha256). Scratch repro: .mkv and .mp4 (PCM audio) masters both rendered 60 frames with verified audio; a .mov --out raised ValueError and left its newly created parent folder behind.

tools.summary_en: Builds a deterministic JSON edit decision list (kosif.edl.v1) from word timings and a reviewed, licensed footage manifest: splits scenes at speech pauses of 0.6 s or more or once a scene reaches 7 s, picks the best tag-matching clip per scene, assigns camera moves and lists blockers instead of inventing footage.
tools.summary_ar: يبني قائمة قرارات مونتاج (EDL) حتمية بصيغة JSON من توقيت الكلمات وبيان لقطات مرخّصة ومراجَعة: يقسّم المشاهد عند وقفات الكلام (0.6 ثانية فأكثر) أو حين يبلغ المشهد 7 ثوانٍ، ويختار لكل مشهد اللقطة الأنسب بحسب الوسوم، ويحدد حركة الكاميرا، ويسجّل النواقص بدل اختلاق لقطات.
use_when: عندي تعليق صوتي وتوقيت كلمات ولقطات مرخصة، اعمل لي خطة مونتاج
أبي EDL للفيديو مع حركة كاميرا لكل مشهد

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Validates the words, rejects clips without license_verified=true, reviewed_frames>=3, contains_text=false, contains_excluded_people=false and is_moving_video=true, builds frame-exact 1080x1920 scenes covering the whole audio, and writes the EDL (creating parent dirs, overwriting silently). It prints {file,scenes,blockers,ready} and exits 0 when production_ready, 2 when blockers remain.

tools.inputs: --words: a bare JSON array of {word|text,start,end,emphasis?} in seconds (the bare-list output of tools/words_convert.py works; a {"words":[...]} object does not); --clips: JSON array of clips with id, path, duration, width, height, license_verified, reviewed_frames, contains_text, contains_excluded_people, is_moving_video, and tags/description; --duration: audio seconds; --fps: 24/25/30/60 (default 30); --out: JSON path.
tools.outputs: EDL JSON (schema kosif.edl.v1) with video {fps,1080x1920,frame_count}, an audio lock policy, scenes (frames, spoken_text, word_ids, key_words, footage_id/path, video_trim, camera move + easing, rights_status), rejected_clips, blockers and production_ready; a one-line JSON summary on stdout.
tools.consent: Nothing to approve for running it, but the license_verified, reviewed_frames, contains_text and contains_excluded_people flags in clips.json must come from the user's real review of the footage; Claude must not set them by inference.
tools.limits: Plans only: it does not inspect footage pixels, transcribe, download or render anything, and matches clips purely by word/tag overlap.
tools.evidence_note: 14/14 passed here (test_cinematic_cut_planner 11/11; test_cinematic_broll_render 3/3, whose real-render test builds its EDL with this planner). Scratch runs: a 2-word bare list with one tagged clip gave 2 scenes, ready=true, exit 0; with no clips it still wrote the EDL with 1 blocker and exited 2; a {"words":[...]} template and --fps 29 crashed with raw tracebacks (exit 1).

tools.summary_en: Audits a KOSIF reference-edit plan.json (schema kosif.reference-edit.v1). It checks the fps/frame clock, gap-free and overlap-free shot frames, bounded pulse cues, that no aligned word crosses a hard cut, safe local media names (and, with an optional Remotion project, that those files exist), and honest evidence flags. It writes a new audit JSON whose status is structurally_verified_render_pending or blocked.
tools.summary_ar: يدقّق ملف خطة مونتاج مرجعي من KOSIF ‏(plan.json بمخطط kosif.reference-edit.v1). يتحقق من اتساق ساعة الإطارات، ومن تتابع اللقطات بلا فجوات ولا تداخل، ومن أن نبضات الإيقاع داخل حدود لقطاتها، ومن أنه لا توجد كلمة موقّتة تعبر قطعًا حادًا، ومن سلامة أسماء ملفات الوسائط المحلية (ومن وجودها فعلًا إن أُعطي مشروع Remotion)، ومن صدق مؤشرات الإثبات. ثم يكتب تقرير تدقيق JSON جديدًا حالته إما structurally_verified_render_pending (سليم بنيويًا وبانتظار التصيير) أو blocked (محجوب).
use_when: افحص خطة المونتاج دي قبل الريندر: فيه فجوات بين اللقطات؟
تأكد إن ما في كلمة مقطوعة بين لقطتين في plan.json
تحقّق من أن مشروع Remotion يحتوي كل المقاطع البديلة المذكورة في الخطة
Run the quality gate on my Remotion reference-edit plan
