commands.name: audit
commands.does: Validates the plan and writes a NEW audit JSON (exclusive create: an existing file is refused, and the --out parent folder must already exist). Prints {status, failures, audit} and exits 0 when all five gates pass, or 2 when any gate fails or the input/output path is invalid.

commands.name: audit-with-project
commands.does: Also requires every referenced clip_NNN.<ext> and audio.<ext> file to exist under <project>/public/assets.

commands.name: inspect_plan (import)
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import creative_quality_gate as q; print(q.inspect_plan(json.load(open('./plan.json')))['status'])"
commands.does: Runs the same checks in memory and returns the report dict without writing anything. scripts/reference_edit_engine.py calls this automatically before it finishes a project and writes quality-audit.json.

tools.inputs: plan.json of schema kosif.reference-edit.v1 (made by scripts/reference_edit_engine.py, stored at <project>/src/plan.json). It must be a regular file, not a symlink, ≤2 MB, with duration 0.1–300 s, fps 24/25/30/60, totalFrames ≤18000, 1–80 shots and an alignedWords list (it may be empty, but a missing list blocks the word gate; at most 1500 entries). Optionally the generated Remotion project directory.
tools.outputs: A new audit JSON (checks with pass/detail, failures, metrics such as shots/totalFrames/shortShotsUnderQuarterSecond/replacementAssetSlots, and an 'unverified' list) plus a one-line JSON summary on stdout. Exit 0 = structurally_verified_render_pending; exit 2 = blocked, invalid input or a bad --out path.
tools.limits: It checks only the plan's structure and timing logic; it never renders or inspects the MP4's visuals, audio sync, rights or aesthetic quality.
tools.evidence_note: 11/11 passed (0.004 s). In scratch the CLI passed a plan generated by reference_edit_engine (exit 0), refused to overwrite an existing --out (argparse error '[Errno 17] File exists', exit 2), and refused a --out whose parent folder is missing ('output parent missing', exit 2).

tools.summary_en: A Python engine that analyses a reference video (built for vertical reels) into spec.json: shots, transitions classified among 65 kinds with measured progress curves, animated Arabic text events with their style and font candidates, and the look (Lab grade, vignette, grain, letterbox, fades). It then rebuilds the same film from new replacement clips into one H.264 MP4 that copies the original audio stream untouched.
tools.summary_ar: محرك بايثون يحلّل فيديو مرجعيًا (مصمَّم للريلز العمودية) إلى ملف spec.json يضم: اللقطات، والانتقالات مصنّفةً ضمن 65 نوعًا مع منحنيات تقدّمها المقاسة، وأحداث النص العربي المتحرك مع أسلوبه ومرشحي الخط، والطابع اللوني (تدرج Lab، والتعتيم الطرفي، والحبيبات، والأشرطة السوداء، والتلاشي). ثم يعيد بناء الفيلم نفسه بلقطات بديلة جديدة في ملف MP4 واحد بترميز H.264 مع نسخ مسار الصوت الأصلي كما هو دون تعديل.

commands.name: analyze
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/mimic'); import mm_analyze; mm_analyze.analyze('./in.mp4','./work')"
commands.does: Writes work/spec.json, the Arabic work/analysis.md, review sheets in work/sheets (plus frames/text/cache folders), and copies the original audio stream into work/audio without re-encoding (plus a 48 kHz WAV for analysis). Optional arguments: text_color, sensitivity, skip_text, deep.

commands.name: match_fonts
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/mimic'); import mm_fonts; mm_fonts.match('./work')"
commands.does: Ranks Arabic font faces (shipped OFL fonts, the fetched cache, work/fonts and system fonts) against each text line's mask and updates spec.json plus font sheets. Each line's text must first be typed into spec.json (or come from OCR); otherwise the event gets a 'no line text yet' note. Optional arguments: families, top, engine, extra_dirs, include_system.

commands.name: build_preview
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/mimic'); import mm_build; mm_build.build('./work', preview=True)"
commands.does: Renders a half-size work/remake_preview.mp4 and work/build/preview/build_report.json. Every shots[].replacement.path must be set in spec.json.

commands.name: build_placeholder
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/mimic'); import mm_build; mm_build.build('./work', preview=True, placeholder=True)"
commands.does: Draft render that uses shot-coloured placeholder plates wherever replacement footage is missing.

commands.name: build
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/mimic'); import mm_build; mm_build.build('./work')"
commands.does: Full-size work/remake.mp4: H.264 bt709 CRF 17 (preset medium), same size and frame count, with the original audio stream copied (-c:a copy).

commands.name: make_reference
commands.does: Generates a synthetic 9:16 ground-truth reference (ref.mp4, truth.json, clips/*.mp4) with known transitions, text events and fonts. Options: --w, --h, --fonts (default proofs/_shared/fonts). Needs OpenCV.

commands.name: run_synthetic
commands.does: End-to-end regression: analyses the synthetic reference, fills each line's text from truth.json, matches fonts and prints the TRANSITIONS / TEXT EVENTS / FONTS scorecard. --skip-analyze reuses an existing work/spec.json.

commands.name: make_candidates
commands.does: Meant to write synthetic replacement-clip candidates and decoys plus candidates.json. Currently broken: the burned-in-text decoy loads scripts/mimic/assets/fonts/Cairo-700.ttf, which does not exist, so it fails after the first 8 clips. Takes a bare positional OUT_DIR (no argparse).

commands.name: fonts-list
commands.does: Lists the usable faces with Arabic coverage (core bundle from proofs/_shared/fonts and fonts/kosif-jumuah, the cache, and system fonts) with weight, style and source. Read-only.

commands.name: fonts-fetch
commands.does: NETWORK: sparse-clones github.com/google/fonts with git (or falls back to raw.githubusercontent.com) and copies or instances OFL Arabic families into --dest (default ~/.cache/kosif-mimic/fonts). --only takes google/fonts ofl directory names.

commands.name: fonts-build-ofl
commands.does: Copies or instances catalogue families from a local google/fonts 'ofl' checkout into --dest and writes fonts.json (offline). --ofl is required in practice: without it the script crashes with a TypeError.

tools.inputs: A reference video (e.g. ./in.mp4, usually vertical, with Arabic text and audio) and a work directory. Replacement clips that the user owns or has licensed, set per shot in spec.json shots[].replacement.path. Optionally the user's own font files in work/fonts. The text of each event is normally typed into spec.json by hand.
tools.outputs: work/spec.json, work/analysis.md, work/sheets/*.png (shots, transitions, texts, font candidates), work/audio (original stream copy plus analysis WAV), work/build/*/build_report.json, and work/remake_preview.mp4 or work/remake.mp4. The synthetic harness writes ref.mp4 and truth.json and prints a scorecard.
tools.consent: The user must confirm the right to analyse the reference video and must supply owned or licensed replacement footage (no platform scraping). mm_fonts_lib.py fetch downloads Google Fonts (OFL) from GitHub into ~/.cache/kosif-mimic/fonts, so confirm network use and that write location first.
tools.limits: OCR runs only when tesseract and assets/tessdata/ara.traineddata are present (neither is shipped), so event text is normally typed by hand; there are no stickers or emoji; commercial Thuluth/Diwani faces become the closest free font unless the user supplies the file; and accuracy on real footage is lower than the synthetic proof (6/6 transitions, 5/5 fonts, 3/5 text timing within ±2 frames).
tools.evidence_note: 2/2 passed in 155.9 s, including the heavy synthetic analyse + font-match scorecard (FONTS 5/5). numpy, Pillow with raqm, OpenCV, fontTools, ffmpeg and ffprobe are present here; scipy, imageio-ffmpeg and tesseract are absent. The test does not call mm_build.build, so the remake render was not exercised here (the proof README records a 570/570-frame placeholder preview build on 2026-10-18).

tools.summary_en: Reads an authorized local video with ffprobe (duration, size, fps, audio presence) and optionally runs ffmpeg scene-change detection, producing a JSON timing report of cut candidates and segments that downstream KOSIF edit tools require.
tools.summary_ar: يقرأ فيديو محليًا مصرّحًا به عبر ffprobe لاستخراج المدة والأبعاد ومعدل الإطارات ووجود الصوت، ويشغّل اختياريًا كشف تغيّر المشاهد عبر FFmpeg، ثم يخرج تقرير توقيت بصيغة JSON بنقاط القطع المرشّحة والمقاطع، وهو مُدخل تحتاجه أدوات المونتاج اللاحقة.
use_when: شوف الفيديو المرجعي ده فيه كام قطع وفين
أبي أعرف مدة وأبعاد ومعدل فريمات هالفيديو
Detect the cut points in this reference reel
Get duration, resolution and fps of my clip before editing
حلّل إيقاع القطعات في الفيديو المرجعي قبل ما نبني المونتاج

commands.name: metadata
commands.does: Runs ffprobe only and prints the full JSON report (width, height, fps_rational, duration_seconds, audio_present, one segment) to stdout; it writes nothing.

commands.name: cuts
commands.does: Also runs ffmpeg select=gt(scene,threshold),showinfo to list cut candidates (>=0.25 s apart, not within 0.2 s of the ends) and segments, saves them to a new JSON file (never overwrites) and prints {status,saved,cuts}.

tools.inputs: A local regular (non-symlink) video file of at most 300 s and 1 GB; --cuts to enable detection; --threshold strictly between 0 and 1, default 0.35; optional --out for a new JSON path whose parent exists.
tools.outputs: JSON report with status 'reference_timing_observed_not_animation_reconstructed', target (absolute input path), width, height, fps_rational, duration_seconds, audio_present, cut_detection_run, cut_candidates_seconds, segments, important_limitations and next, printed to stdout or saved to --out. Errors print {status:failed,error} to stderr with exit 2.
tools.consent: Reads a user-supplied local video with ffprobe/ffmpeg: confirm the user owns or is authorized to analyze it.
tools.limits: Cut candidates are heuristic scene-change detections that can miss dissolves or fire on flashes, and it does no object, motion, speech or semantic analysis.
tools.evidence_note: 14/14 passed here (test_motion_reference_probe 6/6 with mocked ffprobe/ffmpeg; test_reference_visual_style 8/8, whose real-ffmpeg test runs this probe's ffprobe metadata path on a synthetic clip). Scratch runs on a synthetic 4 s 160x90 25 fps red→blue clip: metadata reported duration 4.0 and no audio; --cuts found the cut at 2.0 s; a second --out to the same path was refused with exit 2.

tools.summary_en: Turns a motion_reference_probe cut report (plus optional audio cues, visual fingerprint and owned replacement clips) into a new, unrendered, editable Remotion React project with frame-exact shots, word-safe cuts and a quality-gate audit.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل تقرير القطعات المستخرج من فيديو مرجعي، مع إشارات الصوت والبصمة البصرية والمقاطع المملوكة اختياريًا، إلى مشروع Remotion جديد قابل للتعديل لم يُصيَّر بعد، بلقطات مضبوطة على مستوى الإطار وقطعات لا تقسم الكلمات، مع تقرير فحص من بوابة الجودة.
use_when: عايز أعمل مونتاج بنفس إيقاع قطعات الفيديو ده بس بلقطاتي أنا
أبي أعيد بناء مونتاج هالفيديو المرجعي كمشروع Remotion أقدر أعدّله
حوّل توقيت القطعات وألوان الفيديو المرجعي إلى مشروع مونتاج جديد
Rebuild this reference video's cut rhythm as an editable Remotion project
Match the cut timing of this reel to my voiceover without splitting words

commands.name: build-project
commands.does: Converts the probe's cut candidates into a 1080x1920 frame-exact shot plan and writes a new Remotion project (package.json, src/index.jsx, src/Root.jsx, src/Video.jsx, src/plan.json, decision-report.json, quality-audit.json, README.md); the reference duration is the clock and captions are placeholders ('مشهد N').

commands.name: build-project-with-audio-and-look
commands.does: Uses the kosif.audio-cues.v1 duration as master clock, scales the reference cuts to it, moves cuts off word interiors to the nearest word edge (fails if that is more than 0.5 s away), captions shots from the aligned words, adds per-shot pulse frames from onset candidates and applies measured per-shot palettes from the visual fingerprint.

commands.name: build-project-with-owned-media
commands.does: Also copies one user-owned clip per shot and/or an optional audio track (from {"clips":[...],"audio":"voice.wav"}) into public/assets/ as clip_NNN.ext / audio.ext after rejecting traversal, symlinks, bad extensions, empty files and files over 350 MB (800 MB total).

tools.inputs: --probe: JSON from motion_reference_probe.py --cuts (required; fewer than 80 cut candidates, reference up to 300 s); optional --cues: kosif.audio-cues.v1 JSON from audio_cue_mapper.py (up to 120 s, words keyed 'word' or 'text'); --visual: JSON from reference_visual_fingerprint.py of the same video; --manifest {clips:[...],audio:'...'} with --assets-dir holding owned .mp4/.mov/.webm/.m4v and .mp3/.wav/.m4a/.aac files; --fps 24/25/30/60 (default 30); --out: a new directory whose parent exists. Every JSON input must be a regular file under 2 MB.
tools.outputs: A new unrendered Remotion project directory: package.json (remotion ^4, @remotion/cli ^4, react ^19), src/index.jsx, src/Root.jsx, src/Video.jsx, src/plan.json (schema kosif.reference-edit.v1), decision-report.json (evidence flags), quality-audit.json (creative_quality_gate result), README.md, plus public/assets/ when owned media is given; prints a one-line JSON status.
tools.consent: Copies user-supplied replacement clips/audio into the new project: confirm the user owns or licensed them. Running npm install or a Remotion render on the generated project needs separate approval and a Remotion commercial-license review.
tools.limits: Generates source code only: it does not install Remotion, render an MP4, inspect replacement media durations or codecs, understand shot content or reproduce the reference's effects, and output is fixed at 1080x1920.
tools.evidence_note: 36/36 passed here (test_reference_edit_engine 11/11, test_reference_visual_style 8/8 incl. the real-ffmpeg test, test_creative_quality_gate 11/11, test_music_rhythm_engine 6/6). Scratch smoke runs: --visual on a synthetic 4 s red→blue clip gave 2 shots/120 frames; --cues (6 s, 25 fps) gave 150 frames and moved a word-splitting cut from frame 75 to 70; a 2-clip+audio manifest copied 3 assets; a 1-clip manifest and an existing --out were refused without creating anything.

tools.summary_en: Decodes an authorized local video at 64x36 and 2 fps with ffmpeg and measures per-shot palette, luma, contrast, saturation, frame change and coarse translation candidates, writing a JSON fingerprint that reference_edit_engine can apply as new shot colors.
tools.summary_ar: يفكّ ترميز فيديو محلي مصرّح به بدقة 64×36 وبمعدل إطارين في الثانية عبر FFmpeg، ويقيس لكل لقطة لوحة الألوان والإضاءة والتباين والتشبّع ومقدار التغيّر ومرشّحات الإزاحة التقريبية، ثم يكتب بصمة JSON يستطيع محرك المونتاج المرجعي تحويلها إلى ألوان مشاهد جديدة.
use_when: استخرج ألوان وإضاءة كل لقطة من الفيديو المرجعي
أبي ألوان مشاهدي تشبه ألوان هالفيديو
Measure the palette and brightness of each shot in this reference video
Is there camera panning in this reference? Give me motion candidates

commands.name: fingerprint-per-shot
commands.does: Validates that the probe report came from a --cuts run of the same video (duration within 0.25 s), samples frames at 64x36 and 2 fps, computes per-sample stats and per-shot sections (palette, luma, contrast, saturation, change ratio, horizontal/vertical translation candidate), and writes a new JSON file.

commands.name: fingerprint-whole
commands.does: Same measurement without a cut report, so the whole video is one section.

tools.inputs: A local regular (non-symlink) video of at most 120 s; optional --probe JSON from motion_reference_probe.py --cuts of the same video; --out: a new JSON path whose parent exists (never overwritten).
tools.outputs: JSON (schema kosif.reference-visual-fingerprint.v1) with duration, sample_fps 2, sample_dimensions [64,36], sample_count, per-sample rows (luma, contrast, saturation_proxy, mean_rgb, change_ratio, translation) and sections (start/end, palette hex list, mean_luma, mean_contrast, saturation_proxy, change_ratio_mean, possible_translation, motion_candidate_count), exclusions, source_name, cut_report_provided and source_video_unchanged; prints a one-line status.
tools.consent: Decodes a user-supplied local video with ffmpeg: confirm the user owns or is authorized to analyze it.
tools.limits: Measures coarse low-resolution pixel statistics only (3-bit-quantized palette, uncalibrated luma, sparse translation guesses), not accurate color grading, object or camera tracking, or semantic understanding.
tools.evidence_note: 20/20 passed here (test_reference_visual_fingerprint 12/12 with mocked decoding; test_reference_visual_style 8/8 including a real ffmpeg decode of a synthetic clip). Scratch runs on a synthetic red→blue clip: with its cut report, 8 samples and 2 sections with palettes ['#f01010'] and ['#1010f0'], translation 'none'; without it, 1 section; rerunning to an existing --out failed with '[Errno 17] File exists' only after the decode.

tools.summary_en: Generates deterministic, non-destructive JSON for two editor workflows: a text-based paper edit that turns selected word ranges into frame-bounded video-only segments, and frame-accurate review markers with timecodes and optional pixel anchors; it never reads, cuts or renders media.
tools.summary_ar: ينتج ملفات JSON حتمية وغير إتلافية لمسارين من مسارات المونتاج: خطة مونتاج نصية تحوّل نطاقات الكلمات المختارة إلى مقاطع فيديو محددة بالإطارات، وعلامات مراجعة دقيقة على مستوى الإطار مع رموز زمنية (timecode) وإحداثيات بكسل اختيارية، دون أن يقرأ الوسائط أو يقصّها أو يصيّرها.
use_when: عايز أقص الفيديو بالكلام: خلّي الكلمات من 1 لـ 3 ومن 7 لـ 9
حوّل ملاحظات المراجعة لعلامات على إطارات محددة بالتايم كود
Make a text-based paper edit from words.json
Convert review comments with x/y positions to frame-accurate markers

commands.name: paper-edit
commands.does: Reads words (list or {words:[...]}, each with word/start/end), keeps the 1-based word ranges, merges consecutive words into source frame runs (floor start, ceil end), lays them end-to-end on an output timeline and writes kosif.video-paper-edit.v1. Audio is never processed.

commands.name: review
commands.does: Converts [{time,comment,x?,y?}] notes into sorted markers (kosif.frame-review.v1), each with a stable 12-hex id, an exact frame, HH:MM:SS:FF timecode and an optional pixel point from normalized x/y.

tools.inputs: paper-edit: words.json (list or {words:[...]}) with 'word'/start/end seconds, non-overlapping; --keep ranges such as '1-3,7-9'; --fps (integer, default 30). review: notes JSON list of {time,comment,x?,y?} with 0 <= time < duration and x/y in 0..1; --duration seconds; --fps; --width/--height (default 1080x1920).
tools.outputs: A JSON file at --out (parent dirs created, existing file overwritten): kosif.video-paper-edit.v1 segments with source/output frames, word indices and text, or kosif.frame-review.v1 markers; prints {status,output,schema}.
tools.limits: Produces cut and review plans only: it never cuts, renders or plays media, and its paper-edit segments must not be applied to an audio master.
tools.evidence_note: 12/12 passed here. Scratch runs: paper-edit on templates/ik-wave-words.json --keep 1-3,5 gave 2 segments and 41 output frames; review of an Arabic anchored note and an unanchored note gave frames 45 and 6 (00:00:01:15, 00:00:00:06, point 270x1152); a second review run silently overwrote --out; a 'text'-keyed word file was rejected ('ERROR: word #1: missing word', exit 2).

tools.summary_en: Measures a 16-bit PCM WAV (up to 120 s) into a new kosif.audio-cues.v1 JSON with a 50 ms RMS energy envelope and rising-energy onset candidates, optionally importing validated WhisperX/KOSIF word timings, without ever inventing BPM, beats, words or emotion.
tools.summary_ar: يقيس ملف WAV بترميز PCM بعمق 16 بت (حتى 120 ثانية) ويُخرج ملف JSON جديدًا بصيغة kosif.audio-cues.v1 يضم غلاف طاقة RMS كل 50 ملي ثانية وبدايات صوتية مرشّحة عند ارتفاع الطاقة، ويستورد اختياريًا توقيتات كلمات جاهزة من WhisperX أو KOSIF بعد التحقق منها، دون أن يختلق سرعة إيقاع أو نبضات أو كلمات أو مشاعر.
use_when: حلّل الصوت ده وطلّع لي لحظات ارتفاع الطاقة عشان أركّب عليها القطعات
استورد توقيت الكلمات من WhisperX وتأكد إنه سليم ومرتب
أبي نقاط البداية في التعليق الصوتي عشان أزامن الأنيميشن عليها
Measure onsets and energy in my voiceover WAV for motion sync
Import my WhisperX word timings into a KOSIF cues file

commands.name: measure
commands.does: Reads the WAV in 50 ms windows and writes the RMS envelope and onset candidates (at least 0.12 s apart, at most 600) to a new JSON file. It then prints a one-line JSON summary.

commands.name: measure-with-words
commands.does: Does the same and also imports words[] or segments[].words[] timings. It rejects missing or non-numeric times, overlap, reversal and words that run past the audio.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Shows the arguments: audio, --aligned-words and the required --out.

tools.inputs: An uncompressed 16-bit PCM WAV, mono or stereo, 8–192 kHz, 0.1–120 s, under 64 MB. Optionally a JSON with words[] or segments[].words[], each {word|text, start, end} in seconds, in order and inside the audio (at most 1500 words, 120 characters each).
tools.outputs: A new JSON file with schema kosif.audio-cues.v1: source, duration, sample_rate, channels, window_seconds, energy_rms[], energy_median, onset_candidates_seconds[], words[{text, start, end}], word_alignment_source, bpm:null, emotion:null, verified_beats:false, scope and master_clock. It refuses to overwrite, and the parent folder must exist. A one-line JSON summary is printed on stdout; errors exit 2.
tools.limits: Detects amplitude jumps only: it does not estimate tempo or beats, does not transcribe, and does not read MP3/AAC or 8/24/32-bit WAV, which must first be converted to 16-bit PCM WAV elsewhere.
tools.evidence_note: unittest discover -p test_creative_intelligence.py: 6/6 passed; it covers measure_wav only, not the CLI or the word import. In the scratch folder, a 4 s synthetic WAV with segments[].words gave 8 onsets and 2 imported words. A second run on the same --out was refused with exit 2, as was a missing input. --help exits 0.

tools.summary_en: Turns a kosif.audio-cues.v1 file into a new JSON of up to three distinct tempo hypotheses (60–200 BPM scored against measured onsets), an estimated beat grid when the best match is at least 0.60, and per-second energy sections relative to the track median, all flagged as unverified.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملف kosif.audio-cues.v1 إلى ملف JSON جديد يضم حتى ثلاث فرضيات متمايزة لسرعة الإيقاع (يقيّم السرعات من 60 إلى 200 نبضة في الدقيقة مقابل البدايات المقيسة)، وشبكة نبضات تقديرية عندما يبلغ أفضل تطابق 0.60 أو أكثر، وأقسام طاقة لكل ثانية مقارنةً بوسيط المقطع، مع وسم كل النتائج بأنها غير مؤكدة.
use_when: طلّع لي البي بي إم التقريبي للمزيكا دي
أبي شبكة نبضات عشان أقصّ الفيديو على الإيقاع
اقترح سرعة الإيقاع للموسيقى من ملف cues.json
Estimate the tempo and a beat grid from my measured audio cues
Which seconds of the track are high energy so I can place the big cuts?

commands.name: estimate
commands.does: Scores every integer BPM from 60 to 200 against the onsets (±55 ms tolerance), keeps the top three hypotheses at least 6 BPM apart and builds a grid (at most 500 ticks) when the match is 0.60 or higher. It labels per-second RMS sections, writes a new JSON file and prints a summary.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Shows the arguments: the cues file and the required --out.

tools.inputs: A cues JSON from audio_cue_mapper.py (schema kosif.audio-cues.v1, at most 2 MB, not a symlink): duration 0.1–120 s, strictly increasing onset_candidates_seconds (at most 600), energy_rms values in 0..1 (at most 10,000) and window_seconds (0.001–1, default 0.05).
tools.outputs: A new JSON file with schema kosif.music-rhythm-hypotheses.v1: duration, source, tempo_hypotheses (up to 3, each {bpm, match, aligned_onsets, mean_error_seconds, phase_anchor_seconds}), candidate_tempo_bpm or null, estimated_grid_seconds[], measured_transients_seconds[], relative_energy_sections[{start, end, mean_rms, energy_label}], verified_bpm:false, lyric_understanding:false, emotion_detection:false and notes. It refuses to overwrite, and the parent folder must exist. A summary JSON is printed on stdout; errors exit 2.
tools.limits: Gives a heuristic tempo guess from onset alignment only: half- and double-time errors are common, fewer than 4 onsets gives no tempo, and it detects no chords, mood or lyrics.
tools.evidence_note: unittest discover -p test_music_rhythm_engine.py: 6/6 passed, including the reference_edit_engine pulse-frame integration. In the scratch folder, cues from a synthetic 120 BPM click gave candidate_tempo_bpm 120 (match 1.0) with a 9-tick grid. --help exits 0, and an invalid cues path fails cleanly with exit 2.

tools.summary_en: Converts SRT/VTT subtitles, Whisper-style JSON or word,start,end CSV/TSV into the atlas words.json timing list ([{word,start,end}] in seconds), with an optional global offset and minimum gap between words. When the destination ends in .js it writes a words.js file (window.KOSIF_WORDS) instead.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملفات الترجمة SRT وVTT ومخرجات JSON بأسلوب Whisper وملفات CSV/TSV ذات الأعمدة word,start,end إلى ملف توقيت الكلمات words.json الخاص بالأطلس (قائمة [{word,start,end}] بالثواني)، مع إزاحة زمنية عامة وحدّ أدنى للفجوة بين الكلمات عند الطلب. وإذا انتهى اسم الوجهة بـ ‎.js كتب ملف words.js ‏(window.KOSIF_WORDS) بدلًا من ذلك.
use_when: حوّل ملف الترجمة srt إلى words.json
عندي تفريغ Whisper وأبغى توقيت الكلمات للستارتر
قدّم توقيت كل الكلمات 80 ملّي ثانية
convert captions.vtt into words.json for word-synced kinetic text
turn whisper output into a words.js file for the html-canvas starter
shift all word timings earlier by 0.08 s

commands.name: srt
commands.does: Splits each subtitle cue into words and spreads the cue's time span across them, weighted by word length; inline <...> and {...} tags are stripped.

commands.name: whisper-json
commands.does: Reads segments[].words, {words:[...]} or a flat list (segments without words are spread from their text) and moves every timestamp by the offset (negative means earlier, clamped at 0).

commands.name: vtt
commands.does: Parses WebVTT (WEBVTT header, NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks and cue settings are skipped) and enforces a minimum gap between consecutive words.

commands.name: csv
commands.does: Reads word,start,end rows (header optional; times in seconds or [hh:]mm:ss.mmm). Use a .tsv file or --format tsv for tab-separated input.

commands.name: js
commands.does: Writes 'window.KOSIF_WORDS = [...]' for pages opened from file://, such as the html-canvas starter.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Shows the formats, options and examples.

tools.inputs: A source file: .srt, .vtt, Whisper-style .json, .csv or .tsv (word,start,end); --format srt|vtt|json|csv|tsv overrides the extension. A destination path (.json, or .js for window.KOSIF_WORDS) whose folder must already exist; --offset and --min-gap in seconds.
tools.outputs: A words.json array of {word,start,end} (seconds rounded to 3 decimals, sorted, end at least start+0.02), or a words.js file assigning window.KOSIF_WORDS; prints 'wrote N words … (start → end)'. Exit 1 when no words are found, 2 for an unsupported format; a missing source or destination folder, or invalid JSON, ends in a Python traceback.
tools.consent: Overwrites the destination file without asking; confirm before pointing it at an existing words.json or words.js (the docstring example targets the tracked starters/html-canvas/words.js).
tools.limits: For SRT/VTT, word times are estimated by spreading each cue's span by word length, not by real forced alignment, and only word/start/end are kept (emphasis or scene fields are dropped).
tools.evidence_note: tests.test_tools_extra.WordsConvertTests 3/3 passed (SRT spread with Arabic words, VTT with offset and min-gap, Whisper JSON); module 4/4 OK. Live in scratch: all five conversion examples exit 0; a missing destination folder gives FileNotFoundError.

tools.summary_en: Renders a layered 2D full-body character that walks, runs, waves, smiles, blinks and nods on time or word cues, using two-bone IK for legs and arms, and exports PNG/SVG stills or GIF/H.264 MP4 with optional packet-verified original AAC audio.
tools.summary_ar: يرسم شخصية ثنائية الأبعاد كاملة الجسم مكوّنة من طبقات، تمشي وتركض وتلوّح وتبتسم وترمش وتومئ برأسها وفق أزمنة أو كلمات محددة، مستخدمًا الحركية العكسية ذات العظمتين للساقين والذراعين، ويصدّرها صورًا ثابتة PNG أو SVG أو GIF أو MP4 بترميز H.264 مع إمكانية إرفاق الصوت الأصلي بصيغة AAC والتحقق من حزمه.
use_when: خلّي الشخصية تمشي وتلوّح وتبتسم على كلمات التعليق
عايز كاركتر يجري ويرمش في فيديو قصير
أبي شخصية كاملة تهزّ راسها على كلمة معينة
Animate a 2D character that walks, waves, smiles, blinks and nods
Render a full-body character animation to MP4 with my original AAC voice-over

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints JSON with the schema, ffmpeg availability (not ffprobe), export formats and the supported actions.

commands.name: render-still
commands.does: Draws the 5-layer character pose at t=1.55 s to a new PNG (use .svg for a vector still).

commands.name: render-gif
commands.does: Renders every frame of the scene (24 frames for the 3 s demo) to a looping GIF.

commands.name: render-mp4-audio
commands.does: Encodes an H.264 MP4 and stream-copies the user's AAC audio, failing unless the packet hashes match. --audio is optional.

tools.inputs: A kosif.fullbody.v1 scene JSON with: a 128-1280 px canvas; duration 0.1-30 s; character origin, scale 0.35-1.8 and colours; at most 100 actions (walk, run, wave, smile, blink, nod). Actions must be ordered by start across all channels. Each has exactly one of time or word (+occurrence), a duration of 0.05-30 s and an optional speed. Walk and run share one channel, and no two actions may overlap on the same channel. Optional --words JSON {words:[{word,start,end}]} from real alignment. Optional --audio must be AAC (MP4 only) with a length matching the duration. --fps 1-60; --time applies to stills.
tools.outputs: A new PNG or SVG still, or a GIF or H.264 MP4 (CRF 19, whole frame count, at most 600 frames). Images have five layers: ground, back limbs, torso and head, facial expression, front arm. The MP4 can include the original AAC by stream copy. stdout gets JSON with verified, the output path, frames, sha256, audio_packets_preserved and the format; errors go to stderr with exit 1.
tools.consent: --audio muxes the user's narration into the output: use only audio the user supplied and has rights to.
tools.limits: One stylized 2D figure with six preset actions and simple leg/arm IK; no 3D, mocap, lip sync, transcription, multiple characters or custom artwork.
tools.evidence_note: 14/14 passed, including the H.264 MP4 and AAC packet-copy tests (ffmpeg and ffprobe present, nothing skipped).

tools.summary_en: Animates a simple drawn character's arm with analytic two-bone inverse kinematics toward targets cued by time or verified word timestamps, exporting PNG/SVG stills or GIF/H.264 MP4, optionally with the original AAC narration stream-copied and checked by packet hashes.
tools.summary_ar: يحرّك ذراع شخصية مرسومة بسيطة بالحركية العكسية التحليلية ذات العظمتين نحو أهداف تحدّدها أزمنة أو توقيتات كلمات موثّقة، ويصدّر صورًا ثابتة PNG أو SVG أو GIF أو MP4 بترميز H.264، مع إمكانية نسخ التعليق الصوتي الأصلي بصيغة AAC دون إعادة ترميز والتحقق منه ببصمات الحزم.
use_when: حرّك ذراع الشخصية لما يقول كلمة ارفع
عايز الشخصية ترفع إيدها على كلمة معينة في التعليق الصوتي
أبي إشارة يد متزامنة مع الصوت وأحافظ على الصوت الأصلي
Make the character raise its arm on a specific word from my narration
Solve elbow and hand positions with inverse kinematics and export a GIF

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints JSON with the schema, Pillow version, ffmpeg availability (not ffprobe), formats and the 600-frame limit.

commands.name: render-still
commands.does: Resolves the word-cued targets, solves the arm IK at t=0.8 s and paints a new PNG (use .svg for a vector still).

commands.name: render-video
commands.does: Renders the full duration as frames and encodes an H.264 MP4 (or a GIF when the output ends in .gif), then checks the codec with ffprobe.

commands.name: render-with-audio
commands.does: Muxes the user's AAC narration by stream copy and fails unless every audio packet hash matches the source.

commands.name: library
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from character_ik import solve_ik; print(solve_ik((320,310),(400,190),120,115,-1))"
commands.does: Uses solve_ik, words_from_file, resolve, probe and packet_hashes as a library; character_fullbody.py reuses them.

tools.inputs: A kosif.ik.v1 scene JSON with: a 128-2048 px canvas; duration 0.1-30 s; a rig (shoulder, upper/lower bone lengths 5-1000, bend ±1, colours, widths); 1-100 targets, each with exactly one of time or word (+occurrence), a point and a travel time. The first target must sit at time 0 with travel 0. Optional --words JSON ({words:[{word,start,end}]} or a bare list, sorted by start, from real alignment). Optional --audio must be AAC and match the scene length (MP4 only). --fps 1-60; --time applies to stills only.
tools.outputs: A new PNG or SVG still at --time, or a GIF or H.264 MP4 of the whole scene (duration×fps must be a whole number of frames, at most 600). The MP4 can carry the original AAC by stream copy. stdout gets JSON with the output path, verified, sha256, frames, fps, cue_times and audio_packet_copy_verified; errors go to stderr with exit 1.
tools.consent: --audio muxes the user's narration into the output: use only audio the user supplied and has rights to.
tools.limits: Animates one two-bone arm on an otherwise static simple figure; it is not full-body rigging, lip sync, transcription or AI character generation.
tools.evidence_note: test_character_ik.py 18/18 passed, including the H.264 exact-frame and AAC packet-copy tests (ffmpeg and ffprobe present, nothing skipped). test_character_fullbody.py, which reuses its words_from_file/probe/packet_hashes, passed 14/14.

tools.summary_en: Generates an editable 1080x1920 Motion Director storyboard JSON, plus an optional self-contained seekable HTML preview, in which procedural vector human and/or cat characters draw on in a street or park with six actions, three moods and optional real word timestamps.
tools.summary_ar: يولّد لوحة قصصية (storyboard) قابلة للتحرير بصيغة JSON لأداة Motion Director بمقاس 1080×1920، مع معاينة HTML مستقلة اختيارية يمكن التنقّل فيها زمنيًا، تُرسم فيها تدريجيًا شخصيات متجهية لإنسان أو قطة أو كليهما في شارع أو حديقة، بست حركات وثلاثة تعابير وتوقيتات كلمات حقيقية اختيارية.
use_when: ارسم لي شخص وقطة يمشون في شارع كموشن جرافيك
عايز رسمة كرتون لراجل بيلوّح في حديقة
أبي ستوري بورد مرسوم بالكود لقطة تركض في الحديقة
Draw a hand-drawn style character walking down a street as an editable animation
Make a vertical draw-on storyboard of a person waving, synced to my word timestamps

commands.name: generate
commands.example: python3 scripts/code_drawing_master.py --cast human+cat --expression happy --location street --action walk --out ./story.json --html ./story.html
commands.does: Writes a new storyboard JSON and a self-contained seekable HTML preview of a human and a cat walking on a street. The HTML is compiled, not rendered to video.

commands.name: generate-with-words
commands.does: Embeds pre-aligned word timestamps (here the bundled synthetic demo words) as the scene's captions. Accepts words[{word|text,start,end}] or WhisperX segments[].words and fails on missing, overlapping or out-of-range timings instead of synthesizing them.

commands.name: generate-json-only
commands.example: python3 scripts/code_drawing_master.py --cast cat --expression determined --location park --action run --duration 12 --fps 30 --out ./cat-park.json
commands.does: Writes only the editable storyboard JSON (a cat running in a park, 12 s at 30 fps).

commands.name: library
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import code_drawing_master as d; print(len(d.human_parts('happy')), len(d.cat_parts('sad')))"
commands.does: Uses human_parts, cat_parts, scene_paths, load_words and make_story as a library (prints 20 14); motion_kit_bridge.py reuses human_parts this way.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Lists the allowed values for cast, expression, location, action and fps.

tools.inputs: CLI choices only: --cast human|cat|human+cat (default human+cat); --expression happy|sad|determined; --location street|park; --action idle|walk|run|wave|point|sit; --duration 4-120 s (default 9); --fps 24|25|30|60. Optional --words-json takes pre-aligned timestamps (words[] or WhisperX segments[].words, at most 240 words, UTF-8 without a BOM); they must be non-overlapping and inside the duration, and words without start/end are refused. --out (required) and --html must be new paths in existing directories.
tools.outputs: A new Motion Director v1 storyboard JSON at --out: one 1080x1920 scene with draw-on street or park paths, a fixed 'KOSIF DRAWING' title, a polygon morph, articulated actors (20-part human, 14-part cat) with post-draw movement, a camera zoom and the words. Optional --html adds a self-contained seekable HTML that embeds assets/motion_engine.js. A JSON report goes to stdout with rendered:false; failures print {status:failed} to stderr with exit 2.
tools.limits: Produces a fixed, stylized procedural storyboard (two locations, preset human/cat rigs, six actions) and only compiles HTML; it does not render MP4, transcribe speech, lip-sync or accept custom artwork.
tools.evidence_note: 14/14 passed (python3 -m unittest discover -p test_code_drawing_master.py). The related engine test evals/test_code_drawing_engine.mjs also passed 7/7 under node --test.

tools.summary_en: Paints a strict JSON layered scene (rectangles, ellipses, lines, polygons, pressure brush strokes, text) with Pillow into PNG/SVG stills, or animates whole layers with keyframes into a GIF or H.264 MP4.
tools.summary_ar: يرسم مشهدًا من طبقات معرّفًا بصيغة JSON صارمة (مستطيلات وأشكال بيضاوية وخطوط ومضلعات وضربات فرشاة حساسة للضغط ونصوص) باستخدام Pillow ويصدّره صورًا ثابتة PNG أو SVG، أو يحرّك الطبقات كاملةً بإطارات مفتاحية ويصدّرها GIF أو MP4 بترميز H.264.
use_when: ارسم لوحة بطبقات وصدّرها PNG وSVG
عايز أحرّك دائرة بكي فريمز وأطلّعها GIF
سوّ لي رسمة بسيطة بأشكال وفرشاة وطلّعها فيديو
Paint a layered illustration from JSON and export PNG and SVG
Animate a layer with keyframes and export an MP4

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints JSON with the schema, Pillow version, ffmpeg availability, frame limit and supported formats.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Validates the scene and paints one frame at the given time to a new PNG. Prints the path, sha256, byte count and verified flag.

commands.name: render-svg
commands.does: Writes an editable SVG with one <g data-layer> group per layer.

commands.name: animate-gif
commands.does: Renders the layer keyframes to a looping GIF (at most 300 frames).

commands.name: animate-mp4
commands.does: Renders the frames and encodes an H.264 yuv420p MP4 (CRF 18) with the local ffmpeg.

commands.name: library
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys,json; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import creative_paint as cp; print(cp.validate(json.load(open('templates/creative-paint-demo.json'))))"
commands.does: Uses the module as a library (validate, paint, svg, render, animate, pose); character_ik, character_fullbody and smart_draw build on it this way.

tools.inputs: A kosif.paint.v1 JSON scene (UTF-8 without a BOM) with: integer width/height 1-2048; background as #RRGGBB[AA] or 'transparent'; 1-150 layers (name, opacity, blend normal|multiply|screen, visible); at most 1500 shapes in total. Shape kinds are rectangle, ellipse, line, polygon, brush ([x,y,pressure] points, 2-1500) and text (optional font file path). Optional per-layer keyframes (up to 100) set x/y/angle/scale/opacity with linear or ease-in-out. render takes --time 0-3600 s; animate takes --fps 1-60 and --duration up to 30 s, with ceil(fps×duration) at most 300 frames.
tools.outputs: render writes a new .png or .svg; animate writes a new .gif, or a .mp4 (H.264, CRF 18) via ffmpeg. stdout gets JSON with the output path, sha256, bytes or fps/frames, and a verified flag; errors go to stderr as {verified:false,error} with exit 1. Existing outputs are never overwritten.
tools.limits: A simple 2D primitive painter with whole-layer keyframes only (no AI generation, per-shape animation or PSD); SVG drops brush pressure and blend modes, and rotated layers do not land in the same place in PNG and SVG.
tools.evidence_note: test_creative_paint.py 13/13 passed, including the MP4 render (ffmpeg present, nothing skipped). test_smart_draw.py (4/4) and test_character_fullbody.py (14/14), which call its paint/svg functions, also passed.

tools.summary_en: Turns freehand stroke JSON into a layered drawing, optionally snapping each stroke to a rectangle, ellipse or straight line with deterministic geometry, then reports the recognized shapes or renders the drawing to PNG/SVG.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ضربات الرسم الحر المعرّفة بصيغة JSON إلى رسمة من طبقات، ويطابق كل ضربة اختياريًا مع مستطيل أو شكل بيضاوي أو خط مستقيم بهندسة حتمية، ثم يعرض الأشكال المتعرَّف عليها أو يصدّر الرسمة بصيغة PNG أو SVG.
use_when: حوّل خربشاتي إلى مستطيل ودائرة وخط مستقيم
عايز أرسم بإيدي والأداة تظبّط الأشكال لوحدها
أبي أعرف وش الشكل اللي رسمته: دائرة ولا مستطيل؟
Snap my rough freehand strokes into clean shapes
Turn sketch strokes into a layered SVG with pen, marker and highlighter

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints JSON describing the engine, shape classes, brushes and output formats (is_ml:false).

commands.name: analyze
commands.does: Read-only. Prints each stroke's recognized shape and brush plus the layer count.

commands.name: render-svg
commands.does: Converts the strokes to Creative Paint layers (one per stroke) and writes a new SVG.

commands.name: render-png
commands.does: Writes a new raster PNG with pressure-aware brush strokes and the brush opacities.

commands.name: library
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import smart_draw as sd; print(sd.classify([[20,20],[130,20],[130,100],[20,100],[20,20]]))"
commands.does: Uses classify, simplify and to_scene as a library; this example prints 'rectangle'.

tools.inputs: A kosif.smartdraw.v1 JSON with: integer width/height 128-2048; background #RRGGBB[AA] or 'transparent'; 1-100 strokes. Each stroke has 2-1500 [x,y,pressure?] points inside the canvas (pressure 0.1-5), a color #RRGGBB[AA], a width of 1-80, a brush of pen, marker or highlighter, and assist true or false (default false). Only strokes with assist:true are classified.
tools.outputs: analyze prints JSON {recognized:[{stroke,recognized,brush}],layers} to stdout. render also writes a new .png or .svg, one layer per stroke (highlighter at opacity 0.32, marker at 0.9), and adds the output path and byte count. Existing files are never overwritten.
tools.limits: Heuristic geometric snapping into three shape classes plus freehand (rectangle, ellipse, line); no ML object recognition like AutoDraw, no eraser, collaboration or template library.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed. Three tests exercise smart_draw; the fourth covers blender_api_audit.py.

tools.summary_en: Statically parses every .py file under a Blender scripts, addon or source folder with Python's ast module, without importing or running anything. It counts bpy.types Operator, Panel, Menu, PropertyGroup and GizmoGroup classes, bpy.ops calls and topic groups by file name, and prints a JSON summary.
tools.summary_ar: يحلّل كل ملفات ‎.py في مجلد سكربتات Blender أو إضافاته أو شيفرته المصدرية تحليلًا ثابتًا بوحدة ast في بايثون، دون استيراد أي ملف أو تشغيله. يعدّ أصناف Operator وPanel وMenu وPropertyGroup وGizmoGroup من bpy.types واستدعاءات bpy.ops، ويصنّف الملفات في مجموعات موضوعية حسب أسمائها، ثم يطبع ملخصًا بصيغة JSON.
use_when: افحص سكربتات بايثون اللي مع Blender من غير ما تشغّلها
What bpy operators does this Blender addon folder call?
عدّ الـ Operators والـ Panels في مجلد إضافات بلندر
Statically audit Blender's bundled Python API usage before building a bridge

commands.name: --help
commands.does: Shows usage: one positional source folder and an optional --output.

commands.name: audit
commands.does: Parses all .py files under the folder (at most 3,000; files over 2 MB are skipped) and prints a JSON summary without the samples or bpy.ops lists.

commands.name: audit --output
commands.does: Also writes the full report (up to 45 samples and the top 120 bpy.ops calls) to a new file. It refuses an existing file or a path inside the scanned tree, and the output folder must already exist.

tools.inputs: A directory of Blender Python sources (an installed Blender's scripts folder, an addon folder or a source checkout). Optional --output path for the full JSON report.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout (schema kosif.blender-api-audit.v1): files found and parsed, skipped files, counts of operator class types, topic file counts, source_not_executed=true and a caveat. With --output, a JSON file that also holds samples and the bpy_ops_calls counts.
tools.consent: Reads every .py file under the folder given (confirm it is the user's Blender install, addon or source tree); it never imports or runs them, and --output writes one new JSON file without overwriting.
tools.limits: It produces static AST counts of bpy classes and bpy.ops calls in .py files only (at most 3,000 files); it does not run Blender, read C/C++ or prove runtime behaviour, and its topic counts are file-name substring heuristics.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed in evals/test_smart_draw.py; test_blender_ast_fixtures_without_execution covers this tool's audit() and the other three cover smart_draw. In scratch, --help, a fixture audit (one Operator, one Panel, one bpy.ops call, one SyntaxError file skipped) and --output all worked, and a second --output to the same file was refused. Blender itself is not installed here.

tools.summary_en: Validates a bounded kosif.blender.v1 JSON scene and, when the user already has Blender installed, runs it headless (factory startup, autoexec disabled) through blender_worker.py to produce a PNG still, an editable .blend or an animated .glb; doctor only detects Blender.
tools.summary_ar: يتحقق من مشهد JSON محدود بصيغة kosif.blender.v1، ثم يشغّل Blender المثبّت مسبقًا لدى المستخدم في الخلفية (بإعدادات المصنع ومع تعطيل التنفيذ التلقائي) عبر blender_worker.py لإنتاج صورة PNG أو ملف ‎.blend قابل للتعديل أو ملف ‎.glb متحرك، أما الأمر doctor فيكتفي باكتشاف Blender.
use_when: عندي Blender متثبت، اعمل منه رندر PNG للمشهد ده
أبي ملف .blend أقدر أعدّله من مشهد JSON
هل Blender موجود على هذا الجهاز؟
render this JSON scene with my installed Blender to a .blend or .glb
check whether Blender is installed before a 3D job

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Reports whether a `blender` executable is on PATH and the supported formats; never downloads or installs and does not render.

commands.name: render (GLB)
commands.does: Validates the scene, runs Blender in the background with blender_worker.py and exports an animated .glb; prints JSON with format, bytes, sha256 and object_count.

commands.name: render (.blend)
commands.does: Saves an editable Blender project of the same scene.

commands.name: render (PNG, explicit Blender)
commands.does: Renders a still with the Blender executable at the given file path instead of the one on PATH.

tools.inputs: kosif.blender.v1 JSON: size 128–1920, fps 1–60, frames 1–240, 1–12 objects (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) with location (±100), scale (±20), RGBA colour 0–1 and ≤24 ordered location keyframes; --output a new .png/.blend/.glb in an existing folder; optional --blender path to an existing executable file.
tools.outputs: The requested .png/.blend/.glb file plus one JSON line {executed, verified_file, engine, format, bytes, sha256, object_count, output}; doctor prints {blender_installed, path, formats, user_code_loaded:false, automatically_installs:false, render_verified:false}; errors as JSON {executed:false, error} on stderr with exit 1.
tools.consent: Installing Blender needs user approval (the tool never downloads it); render executes the user's local Blender binary, or the one passed with --blender.
tools.limits: Fixed camera, one area light and location-only keyframes on primitives; doctor only detects Blender, and the repo records no real Blender render through this bridge.
tools.evidence_note: 6/6 passed (Blender is mocked; a real render was not run: blender not installed here)

tools.summary_en: Drives a local Blender (or the pip bpy module) to render cinematic Cycles stills or animations from five presets (product-hero, golden-hour, noir-volumetric, neon-night, anamorphic-epic) with light rigs, depth of field, fog, AgX looks, compositor finishing and camera moves, optionally around the user's model, and can dump a live Blender capability inventory.
tools.summary_ar: يشغّل Blender المحلي (أو وحدة bpy المثبتة عبر pip) لرندر لقطات ثابتة أو متحركة بمحرك Cycles وفق خمسة أساليب سينمائية جاهزة (product-hero وgolden-hour وnoir-volumetric وneon-night وanamorphic-epic) تشمل منظومات الإضاءة وعمق الميدان والضباب ومظهر AgX واللمسات النهائية في المركّب وحركات الكاميرا، حول نموذج المستخدم اختياريًا، ويستطيع كذلك استخراج جرد حي لقدرات Blender.
use_when: اعمل لي لقطة منتج سينمائية بإضاءة استوديو في Blender
أبي رندر نيون ليلي لموديلي glb
سوّ فيديو دوران 360 حول المنتج بـCycles
cinematic Cycles render of my product model with golden-hour light
orbit turntable MP4 with depth of field and bloom
list what my installed Blender can do

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Finds Blender (KOSIF_BLENDER, PATH, ~/KOSIF-Tools/Blender*, Program Files, /Applications, /usr/bin, /snap/bin, ~/blender*) and runs it with -v to read its version, or else a Python that can import bpy (KOSIF_BPY_PYTHON or the current one), plus ffmpeg; prints ready and an install hint. Does not install anything.

commands.name: presets
commands.does: Lists the five cinematic presets with lens, f-stop, AgX look and an Arabic description; no Blender needed.

commands.name: inventory
commands.does: Runs Blender to write a JSON inventory of operators, node types, sky/lens/codec enums, Cycles settings, add-ons and compute devices into an existing folder; without Blender it currently stops with a Python traceback.

commands.name: render (still)
commands.does: Builds the preset set, lights, placeholder subject (Suzanne), camera and compositor, then renders one PNG with Cycles and measures it.

commands.name: render (own model, final, editable)
commands.does: Imports the user's model, fits it into a 2 m box on the floor, renders at 512 samples and also saves the editable compressed .blend.

commands.name: render (camera move animation)
commands.does: Renders an animated camera move (orbit, dolly-in, crane-up, vertigo, handheld) with motion blur and encodes it to H.264 MP4 with ffmpeg, or copies the frames to a folder when ffmpeg is missing.

tools.inputs: A preset name; optional --model (.glb .gltf .fbx .obj .stl .ply .usd/.usdz .abc or .blend, otherwise a Suzanne placeholder); --res WxH (default 1920x1080), --quality draft|preview|final, --samples, --frames/--fps, --move none|orbit|dolly-in|crane-up|vertigo|handheld, --device auto|cpu|gpu, --lens, --fstop, --seed, --save-blend; -o output path.
tools.outputs: A PNG still, an H.264 MP4 (or a folder of frame PNGs), an optional compressed .blend, and one JSON line {op, output, metrics (engine, device, samples, resolution, look, render_seconds, warnings, image stats), verified} with exit 1 when not verified; failures print {op, status:error, error} on stdout with exit 1; inventory writes a JSON capability file.
tools.consent: Installing Blender or running `pip install bpy` (what doctor suggests) needs user approval; --model loads a user 3D file into Blender, so use only files the user owns or trusts; final quality or long animations can keep the CPU/GPU busy for a long time.
tools.limits: The look comes from five fixed presets around a placeholder or imported model, so it does not create characters, rigs or story animation, and nothing renders without Blender or bpy.
tools.evidence_note: 3 passed, 4 skipped (doctor, inventory, preset renders and orbit animation need Blender or bpy, which are not installed)

tools.title_ar: رندر Cycles إلى فيديو مُتحقَّق منه
tools.summary_en: Renders an existing .blend/.glb/.gltf scene with Blender Cycles (denoised, AgX) to PNG frames, encodes them to an H.264 MP4/MKV with FFmpeg, checks size and frame count with FFprobe and writes a render-report.json; plan prints the job and the source SHA-256 without rendering.
tools.summary_ar: يُجري رندرًا لمشهد موجود (‎.blend أو ‎.glb أو ‎.gltf) بمحرك Cycles في Blender مع إزالة الضوضاء ومظهر AgX إلى إطارات PNG، ثم يرمّزها فيديو H.264 بصيغة MP4 أو MKV عبر FFmpeg، ويتحقق من الأبعاد وعدد الإطارات بـFFprobe ويكتب تقرير render-report.json؛ أما الأمر plan فيطبع خطة العمل وبصمة SHA-256 للمصدر دون رندر.
use_when: رندر ملف .blend بتاعي لفيديو MP4 بـCycles واتأكد من عدد الفريمات
أبي أحوّل مشهد glb إلى فيديو بـCycles
خطط لي مدة ودقة الرندر قبل ما أبدأ
render my .blend scene to a verified MP4 with Cycles
plan a 5-second 540x960 Cycles render first

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints the paths found for blender, ffmpeg and ffprobe and whether all are ready; read-only, spawns nothing.

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Validates bounds, hashes the existing scene file (here the repo's shipped cat-rescue .blend) and prints the job (resolution, fps, frames, duration, samples, device, tools) with status PLAN_ONLY; writes nothing.

commands.name: render
commands.does: Renders frames with Cycles in headless Blender (autoexec disabled, camera and light added if missing), encodes H.264, verifies width/height/frame count with ffprobe and writes <stem>.render-report.json.

tools.inputs: --scene an existing .blend/.glb/.gltf (glTF is imported into an emptied factory scene), --out a new .mp4/.mkv path, --frames 1–3600 (default 150), --fps 1–120 (default 30), --width/--height even 64–4096 (default 640x360), --samples 4–512 (default 24), --device CPU|GPU, optional --blender/--ffmpeg/--ffprobe paths or names.
tools.outputs: Verified video at --out plus <stem>.render-report.json (source and video SHA-256, probe data, settings); stdout {video, report, status:VERIFIED_VIDEO}; doctor and plan print JSON only; failures print {error, status:FAILED} on stderr with exit 2 (argparse errors also exit 2).
tools.consent: Installing Blender needs user approval; render opens the user's .blend/.glb in local Blender (autoexec disabled), so use scenes the user owns; long CPU renders can take a long time.
tools.limits: Renders only what the scene already contains (adding at most a default camera and one area light), so it cannot make a scene realistic, and its frame-count check is skipped for .mkv output.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed in the file; the 2 tests for this script (test_render_cli_doctor, test_render_plan_and_bounds) passed, the other 2 cover atlas_external_bridge; render not run: blender not installed

tools.summary_en: Blender-side script, run only inside a local Blender (normally by blender_bridge.py), that re-validates the kosif.blender.v1 JSON and builds primitive meshes, Principled materials, location keyframes, a camera and an area light, then saves a PNG still, a .blend or an animated .glb.
tools.summary_ar: سكربت يعمل داخل Blender المحلي فقط ويستدعيه blender_bridge.py عادةً، فيعيد التحقق من مشهد kosif.blender.v1 ويبني الأشكال الأساسية وخامات Principled والإطارات المفتاحية للموضع والكاميرا والإضاءة، ثم يحفظ صورة PNG أو ملف ‎.blend أو ملف ‎.glb متحركًا.
use_when: إيه السكربت اللي بيشتغل جوّه Blender لبناء المشهد؟
شغّل مشهد kosif.blender.v1 داخل Blender مباشرة
what script does Blender execute for the KOSIF bridge
run the KOSIF scene builder inside blender --background

commands.name: run inside Blender
commands.does: Blender runs the worker with the scene JSON and output path after '--'; it builds the scene and writes .png/.blend/.glb, printing KOSIF_BLENDER_OUTPUT <bytes>.

commands.name: via bridge (preferred)
commands.does: The bridge validates the scene, refuses overwrite and launches Blender with this worker and the safe flags.

tools.inputs: Two positional paths after '--' in Blender's argv: a kosif.blender.v1 scene JSON and an output path ending in .png, .blend or .glb.
tools.outputs: The output file (PNG still via Blender's default engine, saved .blend, or GLB with animations) and a stdout line KOSIF_BLENDER_OUTPUT <bytes>; raises inside Blender on invalid input or missing output.
tools.consent: Runs inside the user's own Blender install; installing Blender needs user approval.
tools.limits: Only works inside Blender (bpy/mathutils), with a fixed camera at (8,-12,9), one area light and location-only keyframes, and it has never been executed in this repo's recorded tests.
tools.evidence_note: Only a py_compile syntax check (test_worker_compiles_without_bpy, part of 6/6) ran and passed; execution not run: Blender not installed

tools.title_ar: رندر ثلاثي الأبعاد مستقل عن Blender
tools.summary_en: Renders a bounded kosif.native3d.v1 JSON scene of flat-shaded primitives (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus) with location/yaw keyframes and an orthographic camera to a PNG frame or an H.264 MP4, using pure Python + Pillow (FFmpeg for MP4) and no Blender.
tools.summary_ar: يرسم مشهدًا ثلاثي الأبعاد مكتوبًا بصيغة JSON ‏(kosif.native3d.v1) ضمن حدود ثابتة، مؤلفًا من أشكال أساسية بتظليل مسطح (مكعب وكرة وأسطوانة ومخروط وحلقة) مع إطارات مفتاحية للموضع والدوران حول المحور الرأسي وكاميرا بإسقاط متعامد، ويُخرجه صورة PNG أو فيديو MP4 بترميز H.264 باستخدام Python وPillow (وFFmpeg للفيديو) دون Blender.
use_when: اعمل لي أنيميشن 3D بسيط لمكعب وكرة من غير Blender
أبي فيديو MP4 قصير لأشكال ثلاثية الأبعاد تتحرك
ارسم مشهدًا ثلاثي الأبعاد بسيطًا وصدّره صورة PNG
render a simple 3D primitives animation to MP4 without Blender
quick 3D cube/torus still with zero installs

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints JSON: schema id, whether FFmpeg is on PATH, supported shapes and render modes (painter, zbuffer); no Blender needed.

commands.name: render (PNG still)
commands.does: Renders one frame (--frame, default 1, must lie within the scene's frame count) to a new PNG in an existing folder and prints JSON with bytes and sha256.

commands.name: render (MP4)
commands.does: Renders every frame and pipes them to FFmpeg as H.264 yuv420p MP4 at the scene fps (--frame is ignored for video).

commands.name: render (z-buffer mode)
commands.does: Uses a scene with "render_mode":"zbuffer" for per-pixel depth (correct overlaps) instead of the default painter sort.

tools.inputs: kosif.native3d.v1 JSON scene: width/height 128–1280, fps 1–60, frames 1–240, background hex colour, render_mode painter|zbuffer, camera {position, target, ortho_scale 1–50}, 1–60 objects {shape cube|sphere|cylinder|cone|torus, location, scale, hex color, yaw, ≤32 strictly ordered keyframes with frame/location/yaw}; --output a new .png or .mp4 in an existing folder.
tools.outputs: A new .png (one frame) or .mp4 (H.264, all frames) at --output; refuses to overwrite and the folder must already exist; stdout JSON {renderer, uses_blender:false, output, frames, bytes, sha256}; errors as JSON {ok:false, error} on stderr with exit 1.
tools.limits: Flat-shaded orthographic primitives only: no perspective camera, textures, materials, shadows, imported meshes or Blender parity, and the pure-Python z-buffer slows down at large sizes.
tools.evidence_note: 17/17 passed (7 native_3d incl. the FFmpeg H.264 24-frame ffprobe check, 5 zbuffer, 5 primitives)

tools.summary_en: Writes a bounded kosif.blender.v1 JSON scene (cube/sphere, RGBA colour, location, scale, linear position keyframes) to a binary glTF 2.0 .glb file using only the Python standard library, with no Blender.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل مشهد JSON محدودًا بصيغة kosif.blender.v1 (مكعب أو كرة بلون RGBA وموضع وحجم وإطارات مفتاحية خطية للموضع) إلى ملف glTF 2.0 ثنائي بامتداد ‎.glb باستخدام مكتبة Python القياسية وحدها ودون Blender.
use_when: عايز أصدّر مشهد 3D بسيط كملف GLB من غير ما أنزّل Blender
أبي ملف glb فيه مكعب وكرة يتحركون
صدّر المشهد إلى glTF لأفتحه في عارض ثلاثي الأبعاد
export a simple animated cube/sphere scene to .glb without Blender
make a glTF file I can load in three.js or a web viewer

commands.name: export
commands.does: Validates the scene and writes a new deterministic .glb (meshes, PBR base-colour materials, LINEAR translation animation) into an existing folder; prints JSON {engine, path, bytes, sha256}.

tools.inputs: kosif.blender.v1 JSON (same schema as blender_bridge): 1–12 objects with shape cube or sphere, color RGBA 0–1, location (±100), scale (±20), ≤24 ordered keyframes each with frame and location; fps 1–60, frames 1–240, size metadata 128–1920; --output a new .glb path in an existing folder.
tools.outputs: A new .glb file (glTF 2.0 binary with JSON + BIN chunks) at --output; stdout JSON {engine, path, bytes, sha256}; byte-identical output for identical input; a non-.glb or existing output is an argparse error (exit 2), other failures are Python tracebacks (exit 1).
tools.limits: Exports cube and sphere geometry with translation animation only (no normals/UVs/textures, rotation or scale animation, cameras, lights or rendering) and copies the scene's Blender-style Z-up coordinates into Y-up glTF without conversion.
tools.evidence_note: 5/5 passed (tests call glb() directly; the CLI wrapper is not exercised by tests)

tools.summary_en: One command line with 104 photo, design, font, procedural and download operations modelled on desktop apps (DxO, Lightroom, Capture One, ACDSee, JPEGmini, Affinity, Xara, FontLab, Houdini, Animate, IDM, Canva, plus the 43-op painting batch). Most ops write an output file, and every run prints one JSON line with the op, output, metrics and a verified flag.
tools.summary_ar: أداة سطر أوامر واحدة تضم 104 عمليات للصور والتصميم والخطوط والتوليد الإجرائي والتنزيل، مستوحاة من برامج سطح المكتب مثل DxO وLightroom وCapture One وACDSee وJPEGmini وAffinity وXara وFontLab وHoudini وAnimate وIDM وCanva، إضافة إلى حزمة الرسم (43 عملية). تكتب معظم العمليات ملف ناتج، وتطبع كل عملية سطر JSON واحدًا فيه اسم العملية والناتج والمقاييس وعلامة التحقق.
use_when: نضّف الصورة دي من الضباب وظبّط الإضاءة والألوان
أبي أضغط صور المتجر كلها بدون ما تخرب الجودة
Add an Arabic watermark to every photo in this folder
اعمل لي بوست إنستغرام بنص عربي من قالب JSON وبعدين كبّره لكل المنصات
Check this font's Arabic coverage and subset it to WOFF2
Animate this Arabic title into a GIF or MP4

commands.name: --help
commands.does: Prints the usage docstring with examples.

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Lists every op as ready or missing, the pip install lines for what is missing, and whether Arabic shaping (raqm or reshaper fallback) is available.

commands.name: ops
commands.does: Lists the ops (name, APPX id, source app, params, Arabic name), filtered by an optional word.

commands.name: develop
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py develop ./in.jpg -o ./out/out.jpg --set wb=grey exposure=0.3 curve=s vibrance=0.25
commands.does: Applies white balance, exposure, tone curve and vibrance (Lightroom Basic style).

commands.name: dehaze
commands.does: Removes haze with the dark-channel prior and reports contrast before and after.

commands.name: jpegmini
commands.does: Finds the smallest JPEG quality whose SSIM stays within delta of q95; marked verified when the SSIM target is met.

commands.name: watermark
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py watermark ./in.jpg -o ./out/wm.jpg --set text="© كسيف" opacity=0.4 pos=br
commands.does: Stamps a text watermark (Arabic shaped) or a logo with the given opacity and position.

commands.name: design
commands.does: Renders a Canva-style JSON template (size, background, text/image/rect/ellipse/line elements, Arabic text effects) to PNG, JPG or PDF and checks that each text fits.

commands.name: resize-design
commands.does: Magic resize: writes one file per platform size (16 presets, or sizes=all) with smart, pad-blur or pad-color mode.

commands.name: text-anim
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py text-anim "مرحبا بكم" -o ./out/title.gif --set style=rise seconds=2 fps=24
commands.does: Animates a text line (rise, typewriter, fade or pop) to a GIF, or to MP4 by piping frames into ffmpeg.

commands.name: font-inspect
commands.does: Reports a font's family, style, glyph and code-point counts, Arabic letter coverage, GSUB/GPOS feature tags and whether it is variable (no kerning-pair list despite the ops text).

commands.name: font-subset
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py font-subset proofs/_shared/fonts/Amiri-Regular.ttf -o ./out/amiri-sub.woff --set text="مرحبا بكم" flavor=woff
commands.does: Subsets a font to the given text or code points and saves TTF, WOFF or WOFF2 (flavor=woff2 also needs the brotli package, which doctor does not check).

commands.name: catalog
commands.does: Indexes a photo folder into SQLite (path, size, EXIF, GPS, rating, keywords, dhash).

commands.name: search
commands.does: Searches a catalog database by word, minimum rating or camera.

commands.name: rename
commands.does: Plans a batch rename from EXIF dates; it renames files only when dry=0.

commands.name: remove-bg
commands.does: Cuts the subject out with GrabCut around an optional box and saves a transparent PNG.

commands.name: xmp
commands.does: Writes or merges an XMP sidecar (rating, label, keywords); without -o it writes <image>.xmp next to the photo, and read=1 only reads it.

commands.name: batch
commands.does: Runs one op on every image in a folder (searched recursively) and prints one JSON summary with a failure count.

commands.name: download
commands.does: Downloads a file in resumable parallel byte ranges with an optional sha256 check. This is the only op that uses the network.

commands.name: <any op>
commands.does: Every one of the 104 ops (dehaze, denoise, keystone, lens, hdr, faces, dedupe, trace, boolean, scatter, lsystem, font-build, tween, lottie, ik, collage, mockup, qr, palette, chart, pptx, print-pdf and the painting batch) runs with the same form: <op> IN [IN…] -o OUT [--set key=value …]; 'ops' prints them all with their parameters.

tools.inputs: Image files or folders (jpg, png, tif, bmp, webp); JSON specs for design, preset, layers and strokes; a folder of SVG glyphs for font-build; font files; a URL for download; op parameters as --set key=value.
tools.outputs: The output file (image, PDF, SVG, SQLite DB, TTF/WOFF/WOFF2, GIF/MP4, Lottie JSON, PPTX, .cube or an XMP sidecar) plus one JSON line on stdout: {op, output, metrics, verified}; read-only ops (font-inspect, exif, search, rename dry=1) print the JSON only. batch prints a single summary JSON with a failure count.
tools.consent: download fetches a user-supplied URL over the network (confirm the user has rights to the file). rename with dry=0 renames the user's files in place, and xmp without -o writes a sidecar next to the user's photo. text-anim to .mp4 runs ffmpeg. Installing missing pip packages (doctor prints the install lines) needs approval.
tools.limits: It uses classical OpenCV, Pillow and fontTools approximations of the named apps' features, with no AI models, no RAW decoding and no vendor parity; 'verified' is true only when an op measured its own postcondition, and doctor's 'ready' does not check brotli (WOFF2) or the YuNet model faces needs on OpenCV 5.
tools.evidence_note: test_app_studio.py: 45 tests, 42 passed and 3 skipped (shapely, matplotlib, segno not installed; the download test uses a localhost server only). test_app_studio_paint.py: 12/12 passed. Spot runs in scratch: doctor (101/104 ready), develop, dehaze, jpegmini, watermark, design, resize-design, text-anim (.gif and .mp4 via ffmpeg), font-inspect, font-subset to .woff, remove-bg, xmp, catalog, search, rename dry=1 and batch all succeeded; font-subset with flavor=woff2 failed (brotli not installed).

tools.summary_en: A Python module that registers 43 painting ops in app_studio.py: 30 Paint.NET effects, Julia and Mandelbrot fractals, 24 blend modes, layer stacks to PNG or OpenRaster, .cube LUT making and applying, sky replacement, liquify, depth lens blur, MS Paint style brushes, bucket fill, coloring book pages and stickers.
tools.summary_ar: وحدة بايثون تسجّل 43 عملية رسم داخل app_studio.py: ثلاثين مؤثرًا من Paint.NET، وصورًا كسيرية (فراكتال) لمجموعتي جوليا وماندلبروت، وأربعةً وعشرين وضعًا للمزج، وتسطيح مكدس الطبقات إلى PNG أو تصديره بصيغة OpenRaster، وصناعة جداول LUT بصيغة ‎.cube وتطبيقها، واستبدال السماء، والتسييل، وتمويه العدسة حسب العمق، وفرش برنامج الرسّام (MS Paint)، والتعبئة بالدلو، وصفحات التلوين، والملصقات.
use_when: حوّل الصورة دي لرسم زيتي أو رسم بالرصاص
ابغى فلتر سينمائي LUT تيل وأورنج وأطبّقه على صوري
Replace the sky in this photo with a sunset
Blend these two images with soft-light at 80% opacity
اعمل صفحة تلوين للأطفال من الصورة دي
Paint watercolor brush strokes from a JSON file into a PNG

commands.name: import
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import app_studio; print(app_studio.PAINT_BATCH['effects'])"
commands.does: app_studio.py loads the module and calls register(globals()). The return value {effects, blend_modes, brushes} is exposed as app_studio.PAINT_BATCH.

commands.name: ops paint
commands.does: Lists the painting ops with their APPX ids, parameters and Arabic names. Use the filter 'Paint.NET' for only the effects and fractals, or 'Photoshop' for the 7 Photoshop ops.

commands.name: oil-paint
commands.does: Applies one Paint.NET effect. The same form runs all 30 effects (ink-sketch, twist, zoom-blur, crystallize, levels and the rest).

commands.name: blend
commands.does: Composites a top image over a base with one of 24 Photoshop-style blend modes.

commands.name: layers
commands.does: Flattens a JSON layer stack (image or colour layers with opacity, mode and offset) to PNG, or writes an OpenRaster .ora that GIMP and Krita open.

commands.name: lut-make
commands.does: Writes a 3D .cube LUT for one of 10 looks and checks it with a round trip.

commands.name: lut
commands.does: Applies any 3D .cube LUT to an image with an amount control.

commands.name: sky-replace
commands.does: Detects the sky region and replaces it with a preset gradient or a sky image, with feathering and colour harmonizing.

commands.name: liquify
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py liquify ./in.jpg -o ./out/liq.jpg --set mode=twirl cx=0.5 cy=0.5 radius=0.3 strength=0.6
commands.does: Warps the image with push, pinch, bloat or twirl, or with a list of steps from ops=liquify.json.

commands.name: lens-blur
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py lens-blur ./in.jpg -o ./out/lensblur.jpg --set depth=auto focus=0.8 radius=14
commands.does: Blurs by depth with polygonal bokeh, using a depth map or an automatic bottom-near ramp.

commands.name: paint
commands.does: Draws JSON strokes with 11 brushes (pencil, calligraphy, airbrush, oil, crayon, marker, watercolor, eraser and others).

commands.name: fill
commands.example: python3 scripts/app_studio.py fill ./in.jpg -o ./out/fill.png --set x=10 y=10 color=#ff0000 tolerance=10
commands.does: Bucket fill from a seed point, contiguous or global, with a tolerance.

commands.name: coloring-book
commands.does: Turns a photo into a clean black-and-white line page for colouring.

commands.name: sticker
commands.does: Cuts out the subject (or uses the PNG alpha) and adds a white border and a drop shadow, saved as a transparent PNG.

commands.name: julia
commands.does: Renders a Julia set fractal. mandelbrot works the same way.

tools.inputs: Images (jpg, png and other common formats); a second image for blend; JSON specs for layers, strokes and liquify steps; a .cube file or a sky image path; parameters as --set key=value through app_studio.py.
tools.outputs: The processed image (JPG or PNG), a .ora OpenRaster file, a .cube LUT or a transparent PNG sticker, plus app_studio's JSON line {op, output, metrics, verified} with each op's measured checks.
tools.consent: None beyond installing numpy, opencv-python-headless or pillow if they are missing: each op only reads its inputs and writes its -o output (sticker also writes and deletes a temporary <name>_cutout.png beside it).
tools.limits: It uses classical numpy and OpenCV re-implementations of Paint.NET, Photoshop and MS Paint features (sky and subject masks are heuristics, not AI), the results are not pixel-identical to those apps, and the module cannot run without app_studio.py.
tools.evidence_note: 12/12 passed. Spot runs in scratch through app_studio.py of oil-paint, blend, layers to .ora, lut-make, lut, sky-replace, liquify, lens-blur, paint, fill, coloring-book, sticker and julia all succeeded with the exact example parameters, and the import example printed the 30 effect names.

tools.summary_en: Inspects a licensed font's OpenType facts: cmap coverage of a phrase, GSUB/GPOS, variable axes and family name. It also ranks a folder of TTF/OTF fonts against a tight crop of reference text by rendering the same phrase with libraqm shaping and scoring normalized mask IoU. The output is JSON candidates, never a claimed identification.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص خصائص OpenType لخط مرخّص: تغطية أحرف العبارة، وجداول GSUB وGPOS، والمحاور المتغيرة، واسم العائلة. ويرتّب مجلدًا من خطوط TTF/OTF مقارنةً بقصاصة دقيقة لنص مرجعي، إذ يرسم العبارة نفسها بتشكيل libraqm ويحسب نسبة تقاطع الأقنعة إلى اتحادها (IoU) بعد توحيد المقاس. والناتج قائمة مرشحين بصيغة JSON، لا ادعاء بتحديد الخط.
use_when: إيه أقرب خط للكتابة اللي في الصورة دي؟
افحص ملف الخط ده: يدعم كل حروف «جمعة مباركة»؟
أبي أطابق خط العنوان العربي من لقطة الشاشة مع خطوطي
Rank my licensed fonts against this cropped Arabic title
Inspect this TTF for Arabic coverage, GSUB/GPOS and variable axes

commands.name: inspect
commands.does: Prints font_fidelity_inspection_v1 JSON with file size, missing codepoints for --text (default «جمعة مباركة»), cmap size, GSUB/GPOS presence, fvar axes and family. Accepts .ttf/.otf/.woff/.woff2 (WOFF2 also needs brotli).

commands.name: rank
commands.does: Renders --text in every .ttf/.otf found recursively under --fonts at 5 sizes (48–128) and compares it with the crop in both polarities. Prints font_fidelity_ranking_v1 with candidates sorted by IoU, best_size and status candidate_only or unsupported:<reason>; --top is clamped to 1–50.

tools.inputs: inspect: a font file the user is licensed to use, plus a phrase. rank: a tightly cropped image of the reference text, the exact phrase, and a folder of licensed .ttf/.otf fonts.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout only (inspection, or ranking with metric and limitations notes). Exit 2 with 'FONT FIDELITY ERROR' on a wrong extension or missing file/folder.
tools.limits: It ranks how closely each candidate renders one phrase (binary mask IoU at 5 fixed sizes) and does not identify an unknown proprietary typeface or prove an exact match.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed (Pillow 12.3 with raqm and fontTools 4.67 present). I also ran inspect on proofs/_shared/fonts/Amiri-Regular.ttf (no missing codepoints, GSUB and GPOS present) and rank on a scratch crop rendered in Amiri: Amiri-Regular ranked first with IoU 0.843, then Amiri-Bold at 0.715.

tools.summary_en: Renders text samples in candidate font files through headless Chromium (HarfBuzz shaping) and saves one tightly cropped PNG per item plus a renders.json of box sizes, so the candidates can be compared side by side against a reference typeface.
tools.summary_ar: يعرض عينات نصية بملفات خطوط مرشّحة عبر متصفح Chromium بلا واجهة (بتشكيل HarfBuzz)، ويحفظ صورة PNG مقصوصة بإحكام لكل عنصر مع ملف renders.json بأبعاد صناديق النص، لمقارنة المرشّحين جنبًا إلى جنب مع خط المرجع.
use_when: طابق لي الخط اللي في الفيديو ده بأقرب خط مفتوح
اعرض الجملة دي بخطوط Amiri ونوتو نسخ عشان أقارن بينهم
أبي أعرف وش أقرب خط لخط هالتصميم
Render this Arabic line in several candidate fonts so I can compare them
Which open font matches the typeface in my reference frame?

commands.name: render
commands.does: Takes two positional arguments (spec file, output folder). Embeds each item's font as a data URL, shapes the text in Chromium, screenshots the text box plus 12 px padding to ./out/<id>.png, writes ./out/renders.json and prints 'id: WxH' per item. --help prints usage; a wrong argument count prints usage and exits 2.

tools.inputs: spec.json: {width (default 1200), height (default 400), background (default #000), scale, items:[{id, text, font (path to .ttf/.otf; omit to use the CSS 'family'), family, weight, size (px; no default), color, direction rtl|ltr (default rtl), letterSpacing, wordSpacing, features ("'liga' 1"), variation ("'wght' 600")}]} plus the font files it names.
tools.outputs: outdir/<id>.png for each item, outdir/renders.json [{id, png, width, height}] and one 'id: WxH' line per item on stdout; 'font not loaded' warnings go to stderr.
tools.consent: Launches headless Chromium and writes or overwrites <id>.png and renders.json in the chosen outdir (ids are limited to letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', so they cannot leave it). Item text is set as plain text; an item's optional html field is inserted as markup, so use it only with trusted specs, and use font files the user is licensed to use.
tools.limits: Produces render crops for side-by-side comparison only; it does not identify or score a matching font.
tools.evidence_note: No test executes it: tests/test_superpowers_catalog.py (25/25 passed here) only checks that the file exists and that SKILL.md names it. `node --check` passes; running with no arguments or with --help crashes with exit 1. No render was run here under the safety rules.

tools.summary_en: Reads a local KOSIF Atlas index of third-party skills (plus an optional copyleft index) and prints stats or keyword-ranked matches with licence scope, risk flags and verdicts; with --skill-root it also reads each match's SKILL.md headings. It never executes anything.
tools.summary_ar: يقرأ فهرس KOSIF Atlas المحلي لمهارات الجهات الخارجية (مع فهرس اختياري للمهارات ذات تراخيص الحقوق المتروكة copyleft)، ويطبع إحصاءات أو نتائج مرتبة بالكلمات المفتاحية مع نطاق الترخيص وعلامات الخطر وحكم المراجعة؛ ومع الخيار --skill-root يقرأ أيضًا عناوين ملف SKILL.md لكل نتيجة. ولا يشغّل أي شيء.
use_when: دوّر في أطلس المهارات على مهارة رندر بلندر
search the Atlas index for Blender rendering skills
كم مهارة في الأطلس عليها علامات خطر؟
which Atlas skills are copyleft and reference-only?

commands.name: stats
commands.does: Counts entries by licence scope, licence label, verdict and heuristic domain, plus how many are risk-flagged.

commands.name: search
commands.does: Ranks entries by query words found in the skill name (x5) or else in description/plugin (x1), keeping only positive scores. With --skill-root it reads the matching SKILL.md read-only (≤256 KB, paths that resolve outside the root return INVALID_PATH) and reports its line count and up to 12 headings.
