tools.inputs: stats|search; --index path to an Atlas index JSON (a list or {"skills":[...]}), or the KOSIF_ATLAS_INDEX env var; optional --copyleft-index; --query (required for search); --top (1–100, default 20); optional --skill-root folder holding the skills' files.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: entry/scope/licence/verdict/domain counts and a risk-flag count, or matches with licence_scope, risk_flags, verdict, heuristic category, inspection (NOT_READ, READ_ONLY+headings, INVALID_PATH, SKILL_MD_MISSING, SKILL_MD_TOO_LARGE) and execution NOT_EXECUTED. An unreadable or malformed index exits 2 with {"error": ...} on stderr.
tools.consent: Reads a private local Atlas index the user supplies; keep its contents out of public commits. Installing or running any listed skill needs separate user approval and review.
tools.limits: Needs an external Atlas index JSON that this repo does not ship. It only ranks metadata (optionally reading SKILL.md headings) and never runs, installs or vets the listed skills.
tools.evidence_note: 2/2 bridge tests passed (test_atlas_index_shape, test_atlas_path_traversal_blocked); the whole file passed 4/4

tools.summary_en: Picks a bounded, topic-stratified sample of skills from a KOSIF Atlas index (plus an optional copyleft index), fetches each raw SKILL.md and up to N of its script files from the kosif-atlas repository, and scans them for review indicators (remote script execution, destructive shell, secret collection, prompt override, installs). It never executes anything and writes the fetched text, records.json and summary.json only to a private --out directory.
tools.summary_ar: يختار عيّنة محدودة موزّعة على المواضيع من فهرس أطلس KOSIF (ومن فهرس copyleft اختياري)، ويجلب نص SKILL.md لكل مهارة وحتى N من ملفات سكربتاتها من مستودع kosif-atlas، ويفحصها بحثًا عن مؤشرات مراجعة (تنفيذ سكربت عن بُعد، أوامر حذف، جمع أسرار، تجاوز التعليمات، تثبيت حزم). لا ينفّذ شيئًا، ويكتب النصوص المجلوبة وrecords.json وsummary.json في مجلد --out خاص فقط.
use_when: راجع لي نصوص مهارات الأطلس قبل ما نستخدمها
افحص عيّنة من مهارات Atlas بحثًا عن أوامر خطرة
statically review a sample of Atlas skill bodies before using them
audit the next 200 Atlas skills for risky instructions

commands.name: audit
commands.does: Fetches the selected skills' SKILL.md and up to --scripts-per-skill code files (default 2), scans them for indicators, and writes source/, records.json and summary.json under --out; prints the summary.

tools.inputs: --index an Atlas index JSON with a skills list (id, skill, path, files, license, source); optional --copyleft-index; --out a private directory; --limit 1–1000 (default 200), --workers 1–16, --max-bytes per file (default 180000), --scripts-per-skill (default 2).
tools.outputs: Under --out: source/<id>/<kind>/<file> (fetched text), records.json (one record per file with status, SHA-256 and indicators) and summary.json; the summary is also printed.
tools.consent: Downloads third-party text from raw.githubusercontent.com into a private folder; keep it out of the repository and do not run or merge any fetched code without the owner's task-specific approval.
tools.limits: A sample, not full coverage, and static only: an indicator is a prompt for human review, not a malware verdict, and nothing proves a skill works; fetching needs network access to the kosif-atlas repository.
tools.evidence_note: tests/test_atlas_body_audit.py 4/4 passed offline on 2026-10-23 (path validation, indicator detection, sample selection, bridge annotation); the live fetch was not run here.

tools.title_ar: تحويل مراجعة الأطلس إلى بيان مُراجَع
tools.summary_en: Turns the private records.json from atlas_body_audit.py and a folder of REA static-analysis results into a metadata-only reviewed manifest (per skill: SKILL.md SHA-256, code files read, indicators, licence claim) and a short findings report. No third-party text is copied into the outputs, so the manifest can be committed as data/atlas-reviewed/manifest.json, which atlas_external_bridge.py reads to annotate search results.
tools.summary_ar: يحوّل ملف records.json الخاص الناتج من atlas_body_audit.py ومجلد نتائج تحليل REA الساكن إلى بيان مُراجَع من البيانات الوصفية فقط (لكل مهارة: بصمة SHA-256 لـSKILL.md، وعدد ملفات الكود المقروءة، والمؤشرات، وادعاء الرخصة) وتقرير نتائج قصير. لا يُنسخ أي نص لطرف ثالث، فيمكن حفظ البيان في data/atlas-reviewed/manifest.json ليقرأه atlas_external_bridge.py ويعلّم نتائج البحث.
use_when: حوّل نتائج مراجعة الأطلس إلى بيان نقدر نحفظه في الريبو
اعمل تقرير ملخص لمراجعة مهارات الأطلس
build the committed reviewed manifest from my private Atlas audit records
summarise the Atlas audit and REA results without copying third-party text

commands.name: synthesize
commands.does: Groups the records by skill, attaches REA results from --rea-dir, and writes the metadata-only manifest and the Markdown findings report.

tools.inputs: --records the records.json from atlas_body_audit.py, --rea-dir a folder of REA JSON results, --manifest-out and --report-out output paths (all four required).
tools.outputs: A metadata-only manifest JSON (schema kosif.atlas.reviewed-manifest.v1) and a Markdown findings report.
tools.consent: Writes only the two output paths given; review the manifest for private paths before committing it.
tools.limits: Only summarises what the audit and REA already recorded, so it adds no new verification; the counts describe the sample, not the whole Atlas.
tools.evidence_note: No direct test; its committed output data/atlas-reviewed/manifest.json is read by atlas_external_bridge.py, which tests/test_atlas_body_audit.py covers.

tools.summary_en: Statically audits a KOSIF Atlas skill index and its copyleft companion for schema, count, ID and required-field problems, and counts records whose source is not an https URL. It prints a JSON report of licence labels, verdicts, source hosts and structural errors, and can also save it to a new file.
tools.summary_ar: يدقّق، دون تشغيل أي كود، فهرس مهارات KOSIF Atlas وفهرسه المرافق للمهارات ذات تراخيص الحقوق المتروكة (copyleft)، بحثًا عن مشكلات البنية والعدد والمعرّفات والحقول الإلزامية، ويعدّ السجلات التي لا يكون مصدرها رابط https. ويطبع تقرير JSON عن تسميات التراخيص والأحكام ونطاقات المصادر والأخطاء البنيوية، ويمكنه أيضًا حفظه في ملف جديد.
use_when: افحص فهرس الأطلس وتأكد إن مفيش أخطاء في البنية
audit the Atlas index metadata before importing any skills
كم سجل في الأطلس حكمه REVIEW_BEFORE_INSTALL؟
validate atlas_index.json counts, IDs and source URLs

commands.name: audit
commands.does: Checks both indexes (count field matches, unique non-empty IDs per index, required plugin/skill/description/license/source/path/verdict fields) and tallies licences, verdicts, risk flags, REVIEW_BEFORE_INSTALL/READ_ONLY_OK records and source hosts; non-https sources are counted, not treated as structural errors. Prints the report and, with --output, also writes it to a new file (refuses to overwrite or to create folders).

tools.inputs: --index and --copyleft: Atlas JSON files shaped {"count": N, "skills": [...]}, both required; optional --output path to a new file in an existing folder.
tools.outputs: JSON report on stdout (and in --output if given) with record counts, licence labels, verdicts, inventory counts (including missing_verified_source_url), top-15 source hosts, up to 40 structural errors and up to 12 source-URL problem samples; exit 1 if there are structural errors, the input is invalid, or --output already exists.
tools.consent: --output writes a new report file (it never overwrites). The Atlas indexes are the user's private local files: keep them and the report out of public commits.
tools.limits: Checks index structure, labels, source URLs and verdict counts only; it does not read skill source code or verify licences, safety or behaviour.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed

tools.summary_en: Lists and inspects 26 curated HTTPS targets (web drawing apps, 3D and animation tools, AI and browser products) from data/integration-target-atlas.json. It can take a read-only viewport screenshot of one target in a fresh headless Playwright context that blocks off-host requests, downloads, service workers and saved cookies.
tools.summary_ar: يعرض 26 هدفًا منتقًى عبر HTTPS ويفحص سجلاتها، منها تطبيقات رسم على الويب وأدوات ثلاثية الأبعاد ورسوم متحركة ومنتجات ذكاء اصطناعي ومتصفحات، من الملف data/integration-target-atlas.json. ويستطيع أن يلتقط، دون أي تفاعل، صورةً لإطار العرض في هدف واحد داخل سياق Playwright جديد بلا واجهة، يحجب الطلبات إلى النطاقات الأخرى والتنزيلات وعمّال الخدمة (service workers) ولا يحفظ ملفات تعريف الارتباط.
use_when: صوّر لي واجهة Photopea عشان أدرس ميزاتها
Which web drawing apps are in the integration target atlas?
Take a read-only screenshot of the AutoDraw homepage
وش المواقع المعتمدة لدراسة ميزات تطبيقات الرسم؟
Show me the approach recorded for the canva-draw target

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Reports the target count, whether Playwright is installed, the supported engines and the flags for local prototype, no cloud browser and no auth. Uses no network.

commands.name: list
commands.does: Prints every target's id, category and feature as JSON.

commands.name: inspect
commands.does: Prints one target's full record: URL, category, feature and the recommended lawful approach.

commands.name: capture
commands.does: Opens the target in a fresh headless context with a 20 s timeout and saves one viewport PNG. The output must be an unused .png in an existing folder. Prints status, title, sha256 and bytes.

tools.inputs: A target id from data/integration-target-atlas.json. For capture: --output, the path of an unused .png in an existing folder, and --engine chromium, firefox or webkit.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: doctor status, the target list or one target record. capture writes one PNG screenshot and prints its metadata (HTTP status, title, sha256, bytes, cookies_saved=false).
tools.consent: capture visits the target website and needs 'pip install playwright' plus a separately installed browser engine ('playwright install chromium'). Ask before installing either and before visiting the site.
tools.limits: It captures only a viewport screenshot of one of 26 curated HTTPS targets (no arbitrary URLs, logins, clicks or crawling), and because off-host requests are blocked, pages that load assets from CDNs may render incomplete.
tools.evidence_note: 9/9 passed. The tests cover the atlas, the URL guard and the output and engine refusals, and use no network. doctor, list, inspect and the capture refusal paths ran here; a live capture was not run because Playwright is not installed.

tools.summary_en: Keyword-searches an offline index of 1,000 public GitHub repositories (video editing and processing, motion graphics, image and photo tools, computer vision, creative coding) and 1,000 creative websites extracted from curated awesome lists (design tools, motion graphics, AI image tools, creative coding, video production), and prints ranked JSON matches labelled metadata-only.
tools.summary_ar: يبحث بالكلمات المفتاحية في فهرس محلي يضم 1,000 مستودع عام على GitHub (تحرير الفيديو ومعالجته، والموشن جرافيك، وأدوات الصور، والرؤية الحاسوبية، والبرمجة الإبداعية) و1,000 موقع إبداعي مستخرَج من قوائم awesome منتقاة (أدوات التصميم، والموشن جرافيك، وأدوات الصور بالذكاء الاصطناعي، والبرمجة الإبداعية، وإنتاج الفيديو)، ويطبع نتائج JSON مرتبة موسومة بأنها بيانات وصفية فقط.
use_when: دورلي على أدوات مفتوحة المصدر للمونتاج وإزالة الخلفية
find open-source repos for kinetic typography
أبغى مواقع تساعدني في تصحيح الألوان والتلوين
list creative websites for motion graphics inspiration
how many creative repos and sites are in the discovery index?

commands.name: search
commands.does: Scores repos and/or sites by query terms found in the name (x6) and in description/category/topic (x2), plus a star bonus of at most 1.2; Arabic words such as مونتاج/صور/تلوين and topic names such as image-editing are expanded to English terms; --top is clamped to 1–100.

commands.name: stats
commands.does: Prints repo and website counts, repo category counts, and flags stating no REA analysis or implemented features.

tools.inputs: search|stats, a query in English or Arabic (required for search), --kind all|repo|site, --top; reads data/rea-creative-research/public_repos.json and creative_websites.json.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout with ensure_ascii (non-Latin text appears as \u escapes). Repo items carry name, url, summary, category, stars, SPDX licence metadata and discovery query; site items carry hostname, sample url, topic and source list; every item has rea_analysis, feature_status (DISCOVERED_METADATA_ONLY / CURATED_LINK_ONLY) and relevance_score. stats prints repo/site counts and repo category counts.
tools.limits: Plain substring keyword scoring over a frozen offline index of public metadata and curated links; no entry was code-analysed, licence-verified, checked for availability or tested, and nothing is fetched live.
tools.evidence_note: 8/8 passed

tools.summary_en: Discovers media URLs on a public web page (video and source tags, Open Graph and Twitter tags, JSON-LD, script text) or takes a direct file or an unencrypted HLS playlist. It downloads the media within a size cap into a git-ignored cache and measures it with ffmpeg (probe, contact sheet, scene cuts and dominant palette), plus a bilingual REPORT.md for STYLE.md.
tools.summary_ar: يكتشف روابط الوسائط في صفحة ويب عامة (وسوم video وsource، ووسوم Open Graph وTwitter، وJSON-LD، ونصوص السكربت)، أو يأخذ رابط ملف مباشرًا أو قائمة HLS غير مشفّرة. ثم ينزّل الوسيط ضمن حدّ أقصى للحجم إلى ذاكرة مؤقتة مستثناة من git، ويقيسه بأداة ffmpeg: خصائص الملف، ولوحة إطارات، والقطعات المشهدية، والألوان الغالبة، مع تقرير REPORT.md ثنائي اللغة يُستخدم في STYLE.md.
use_when: هات الفيديو المرجعي من الرابط ده وقيس القطعات والألوان
شوف الصفحة دي فيها روابط فيديو إيه
حمّل المرجع من رابط m3u8 وحلّل مدته وأبعاده
Fetch this reference video and give me a contact sheet, cuts and palette
List the media URLs on this page before downloading

commands.name: list
commands.does: Fetches the page and lists the discovered media URLs (direct first, then HLS, then untyped) without downloading media. The list goes to stderr and, with --json, also to stdout as a JSON array. A direct media or .m3u8 URL is echoed back without any network access.

commands.name: fetch-and-analyse
commands.does: Downloads (cap --max-mb, default 400), remuxes to reference.mp4 and writes probe.json, contact.png, cuts.json, palette.json and REPORT.md. Prints the output directory.

commands.name: pick
commands.does: Fetches the Nth media URL found on a page (default 1) and prints a JSON summary (probe, cuts_s, colors, files).

commands.name: hls
commands.does: Takes the highest-bandwidth variant (plus a separate audio rendition if present), fetches its segments one by one within the size cap, and refuses EXT-X-KEY encrypted streams.

commands.name: download-only
commands.does: Downloads without the ffmpeg measurements. The same happens automatically when ffmpeg or ffprobe is missing.

tools.inputs: A public HTTP(S) page URL, a direct .mp4/.webm/.mov/.m4v/.ogv URL, or an unencrypted .m3u8 playlist. blob:/data: URLs, URLs with embedded credentials, and private, loopback or reserved hosts (also on redirects) are refused.
tools.outputs: DIR/download.<ext> or stream.(mp4|ts) [+ stream-audio.(mp4|ts)], reference.mp4, probe.json, contact.png, cuts.json, palette.json and REPORT.md. DIR defaults to ./.kosif-cache/reference/<slug>/ relative to the cwd. Exit 0 ok, 1 nothing found or refused, 2 network or ffprobe failure.
tools.consent: Downloads third-party media: confirm the user has the right to analyse it. The output is working material in a git-ignored cache and must never be committed, rehosted or cut into the deliverable.
tools.limits: It cannot reach media behind logins, JavaScript-only players, DRM or encrypted HLS, and it measures only technical facts (duration, fps, size, cuts, palette, contact sheet), not easing, camera motion or typography.
tools.evidence_note: tests.test_reference_fetch_security 5/5 and tests.test_superpowers_catalog.FetchReferenceTest 5/5 passed (10 tests, 0.18 s). They cover offline parsers, SSRF and size guards, and CLI help/refusal; real downloads were not exercised. --list on a direct .mp4 and on a .m3u8 URL echoed the URL here with no network access.

tools.summary_en: Wraps yt-dlp to download one or many video or audio links for editing, with a format fallback chain, optional browser impersonation, a user cookies file and a quality cap. It can add an edit-safe H.264/AAC .safe.mp4 copy and writes a manifest.json with the file, duration, dimensions, frame rate, codecs, title, uploader and any license the site exposes.
tools.summary_ar: غلاف لأداة yt-dlp ينزّل رابطًا أو عدة روابط فيديو أو صوت لاستخدامها في المونتاج، مع سلسلة بدائل للصيغ، ومحاكاة متصفح اختيارية، وملف كوكيز من المستخدم، وحدّ أقصى للجودة. ويمكنه إنشاء نسخة ‎.safe.mp4‎ بترميز H.264/AAC تقبلها برامج التحرير، ويكتب ملف manifest.json فيه الملف والمدة والأبعاد ومعدل الإطارات والترميز والعنوان والناشر والترخيص إن كشفه الموقع.
use_when: نزّل الفيديوهات دي من الروابط عشان المونتاج
حمّل لي الصوت بس من هالرابط
Download these video links at 1080p with an edit-safe MP4 copy
Batch-download the URLs in links.txt into clips/
Check whether yt-dlp and ffmpeg are ready for downloading

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Reports the yt-dlp version, ffmpeg presence and impersonation support (runs yt-dlp locally; no download). Exits 1 if yt-dlp is missing.

commands.name: download
commands.does: Downloads each URL (requested format, then a fallback format, then an impersonation retry if available), probes it, optionally writes <name>.safe.mp4, and writes ./out/clips/manifest.json.

commands.name: batch
commands.does: Reads one URL per line (blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped) and downloads all of them. Non-HTTP(S) entries are skipped with a warning.

commands.name: audio
commands.does: Extracts the best audio track as m4a (--safe is ignored).

commands.name: cookies
commands.does: Passes a Netscape cookies.txt exported from the user's own browser, for private or age-gated posts the user can access.

commands.name: update
commands.does: Runs pip install --upgrade yt-dlp curl_cffi (network plus package install).

tools.inputs: One or more HTTP(S) video URLs, or a text file of URLs (--urls). Optional --quality (best|audio|a height, aliases 4k/2k/uhd/fhd/hd, or e.g. 1080p; default 1080), --cookies, --proxy, --connections (default 8) and -o (default ./downloads relative to the cwd).
tools.outputs: <out>/<title> [<id>].<ext>, .info.json sidecars, optional <name>.safe.mp4, and <out>/manifest.json (overwritten each run). Exit 0 only when every URL succeeded; 1 on any failure or missing yt-dlp; 2 when no valid URL was given.
tools.consent: It downloads third-party media, so confirm the user has the right to use it. --cookies uses the user's own session (never store, print or commit it). --update pip-installs yt-dlp and curl_cffi.
tools.limits: It is only a yt-dlp wrapper: it does not bypass DRM or paywalls, does not verify licenses, and many platforms (YouTube 403, Vimeo login, Wikimedia 403) failed from cloud hosts.
tools.evidence_note: No test executes this script. --doctor ran here and reported 'yt-dlp: MISSING' and 'ffmpeg: ok' (exit 1); --help parsed fine and an invalid --quality 8k was rejected by the parser. tests/test_media_sources_gateway.py (8/8 passed) only asserts that the media_sources dry-run command names fetch_video.py.

tools.title_ar: تحميل لقطات مجانية بلا مفتاح (Pexels وMixkit)
tools.summary_en: Downloads free stock clips by id or page URL without an API key: Pexels through its public download endpoint (a 302 to videos.pexels.com) and Mixkit through its free 720p file. It writes manifest.json with the page, file URL, licence name, link and terms, size, dimensions, frame rate and duration, can skip oversized files, and has a probe that reports which stock sources answer from the current machine.
tools.summary_ar: ينزّل لقطات مجانية برقم المقطع أو رابط صفحته بلا مفتاح API: من Pexels عبر رابط التحميل العام (تحويل 302 إلى videos.pexels.com)، ومن Mixkit عبر ملف 720p المجاني. ويكتب manifest.json فيه الصفحة ورابط الملف واسم الرخصة ورابطها وشروطها والحجم والأبعاد ومعدل الإطارات والمدة، ويتخطى الملفات الضخمة، وفيه فحص يبيّن أي مصادر اللقطات تستجيب من الجهاز الحالي.
use_when: هات لقطات مجانية للحرم من Pexels من غير مفتاح
مفتاح Pexels مش متاح، نزّل الفيديوهات دي بأرقامها
Download these Pexels clips by id without an API key
Which stock footage sites can this cloud machine reach?

commands.name: probe
commands.does: Prints the HTTP status of Mixkit pages and files, the Pexels search page, download endpoint and API, the Pixabay API, the Wikimedia API and Coverr from this machine.

commands.name: pexels
commands.does: Resolves each id through https://www.pexels.com/download/video/<id>/ (302), downloads the file, probes it and merges the rows into ./stock/manifest.json. --dry-run only resolves and sizes.

commands.name: mixkit
commands.does: Downloads https://assets.mixkit.co/videos/<id>/<id>-720.mp4 (the free size; 1080 and 2160 return 403) and records it in the manifest.

tools.inputs: Clip ids or page URLs (the id is the trailing number), -o output folder (default ./stock), --max-mb (default 120, 0 = no limit), --dry-run.
tools.outputs: <out>/<id>.mp4 and <out>/manifest.json (rows merged by source and id). Exit 0 when every clip resolved, 1 when any failed, 2 on a usage error.
tools.consent: It downloads third-party stock media; keep the manifest with the project and follow each licence (no resale of unaltered clips, no implied endorsement). Find ids with a web search restricted to pexels.com or mixkit.co; the tool does not search or log in.
tools.limits: It works only while the Pexels download endpoint keeps answering with a 302 and Mixkit keeps its 720p file public; it cannot search Pexels (search pages return 403 to scripts and new API keys were paused on 2026-10-21) and gives Mixkit clips at 720p only.
tools.evidence_note: tests/test_stock_fetch.py 5/5 passed offline; on 2026-10-21 the probe and live downloads ran from a cloud session: 17 Pexels clips (Kaaba, Masjid al-Haram, rain) fetched by id with no key, and Mixkit 720p files were used in three delivered films.

tools.summary_en: Lists and searches a fixed catalog of 100 stock, open-collection and texture websites and prints the legal prerequisites for a URL. It downloads a single asset through fetch_video.py only after explicit per-asset rights evidence is supplied, and records each download with its SHA-256 and rights in asset_rights.jsonl.
tools.summary_ar: يعرض فهرسًا ثابتًا من 100 موقع للوسائط الجاهزة والمجموعات المفتوحة والخامات ويبحث فيه، ويطبع المتطلبات القانونية لأي رابط. ولا ينزّل أي ملف عبر fetch_video.py إلا بعد تقديم إثبات صريح لحقوق ذلك الملف بعينه، ويسجّل كل تنزيل مع بصمته SHA-256 وحقوقه في ملف asset_rights.jsonl.
use_when: فين ألاقي لقطات ستوك مجانية للمونتاج؟
ابحث في مواقع الصور والفيديو المرخّصة عن pexels
أبي أنزّل مقطع من Pixabay وأسجّل ترخيصه
Find free stock video sites for B-roll
Download this licensed clip and record its rights and SHA-256

commands.name: list
commands.does: Prints all 100 catalog sites (id, name, type, URL). Offline.

commands.name: search
commands.does: Filters by an optional term (matched against name, domain and license hint) and --type (video_image, image, open_collections, graphics_texture). Exits 1 when nothing matches. Offline.

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Prints JSON with the matched catalog entry (domain, license_url, license_hint, policy) or null, the requirement, the accepted --rights values and restrictions. Offline.

commands.name: download-dry-run
commands.example: python3 scripts/media_sources.py download https://www.pexels.com/video/123/ --rights stock-license --evidence-url https://www.pexels.com/license/ --credit "Pexels" -o ./out/media --dry-run
commands.does: Validates the rights fields and prints the fetch_video.py command it would run, with no network, download or folder creation.

commands.name: download
commands.does: Runs fetch_video.py (default --quality 1080 --safe), checks that the file arrived via its manifest.json, and appends a record (sha256, rights, evidence, creator, credit) to ./out/media/asset_rights.jsonl.

tools.inputs: The built-in catalog data/media_sources_100.json. For plan or download: a media or page URL. For download: --rights (owned|cc0|public-domain|cc-by|cc-by-sa|stock-license|direct-permission). An HTTPS --evidence-url is required unless the rights are owned, --creator and --credit are required for CC BY/SA, and --credit is required for stock-license. Optional --site (catalog domain for CDN URLs), --quality (best/2160/1080/720/480/audio) and -o (default ./media_assets).
tools.outputs: Text lists, plan JSON or dry-run JSON on stdout. download writes the media plus manifest.json via fetch_video.py into --out, then appends asset_rights.jsonl. Exit 2 means a rights or --site check failed; a failed download returns fetch_video's exit code or 1.
tools.consent: download fetches media through fetch_video.py/yt-dlp. The user must assert per-asset rights with evidence; a site being in the catalog is never a license.
tools.limits: The rights check only confirms that evidence fields were supplied in the right shape; it does not open or verify the license page, grants no license, and real downloads need yt-dlp, which is missing here.
tools.evidence_note: 8/8 passed. I also ran list, search pexels --type video_image (1 result), plan and a download --dry-run here (exit 0, nothing written); a cc-by dry-run without evidence or credit was rejected with exit 2.

tools.summary_en: Builds the creative discovery catalogs by querying GitHub through the gh CLI: topic searches for repos, outbound links extracted from curated awesome-list READMEs for sites, and the owner's repo inventory and git-tree metadata. Each run prints a JSON summary; only `report` works offline, counting the existing catalogs.
tools.summary_ar: يبني فهارس الاكتشاف الإبداعي باستعلام GitHub عبر أداة gh: بحث المستودعات حسب الموضوع، واستخراج روابط المواقع من ملفات README لقوائم awesome منتقاة، وجرد مستودعات المالك وبيانات أشجارها في git. ويطبع ملخصًا بصيغة JSON في كل تشغيل، والأمر report وحده يعمل دون اتصال فيكتفي بعدّ الفهارس الموجودة.
use_when: حدّث فهرس المستودعات الإبداعية من GitHub
rebuild the 1,000 creative websites list from the awesome lists
show how many creative repos and sites are cataloged
اعمل جرد لمستودعاتي على GitHub واحفظه في مجلد خاص

commands.name: report
commands.does: Offline: counts cataloged repos and sites and how many were REA-inspected (currently 1,000 / 1,000 and 0 / 0).

commands.name: repos
commands.does: Runs up to 21 GitHub topic searches via gh (up to --pages pages of 100 each, ~2.1 s sleeps), stops at --limit unique public non-archived repos, and overwrites data/rea-creative-research/public_repos.json and repository_discovery_errors.json. When discovery errors would shrink the catalog it writes nothing and exits 1 unless --force is given.

commands.name: sites
commands.does: Fetches up to 15 curated awesome-list READMEs via gh until --limit unique hosts are found (the current catalog came from the first 9), keeps outbound links near creative keywords (dropping GitHub, social, Wikipedia, badge/CI hosts, image files and licence/donate/privacy links) and overwrites creative_websites.json and website_discovery_errors.json. When discovery errors would shrink the catalog it writes nothing and exits 1 unless --force is given.

commands.name: own
commands.does: Lists up to 100 of the authenticated user's own repos (private ones included) plus up to 100 public repos of the hard-coded elkosif0-cmd account, and writes owner_repositories_PRIVATE_LOCAL.json into the private folder (created if missing).

commands.name: trees
commands.does: Needs the inventory written by own. For each listed repo it fetches metadata and the recursive git tree via gh and writes extension counts and media-related path examples to owner_tree_inspection_PRIVATE_LOCAL.json (rewritten after each repo).

tools.inputs: An action (own|repos|sites|trees|report); --limit (default 1000); --pages (default 2, repos only); --private-output folder (required for own and trees). Every action except report needs network access and an authenticated gh CLI.
tools.outputs: repos and sites overwrite the tracked catalogs in data/rea-creative-research/ (public_repos.json, creative_websites.json, *_discovery_errors.json). own and trees write *_PRIVATE_LOCAL.json files into --private-output. Every action prints a JSON summary.
tools.consent: Contacts GitHub through the user's authenticated gh CLI. repos and sites overwrite tracked catalog files in data/rea-creative-research/ (no backup; review the git diff), but refuse to shrink a catalog after discovery errors unless --force is given. own and trees read the user's private repository metadata, and --private-output must be outside every git repository (the script refuses otherwise).
tools.limits: Collects GitHub search metadata and links scraped from awesome-list READMEs only; despite its name it does not run REA, analyse code, or verify licences or site availability, and only `report` works offline.
tools.evidence_note: 8/8 passed in tests/test_creative_external_research.py, but only test_site_extraction_filters_badges calls this script's code (extract_sites); the other 7 check the catalogs it produced and creative_external_search.py. report and --help ran here; repos, sites, own and trees were not run (network).

commands.name: run
commands.does: Merges the existing catalog with 8 GitHub topic searches, filters out 'fable/opus/claude 5.5' marketing rows, applies the quotas (video-film 380, motion-vfx 260, image-photo 320, computer-vision-creative 40, speech-typography 40), fills up to 1,000 rows by stars and cuts anything beyond 1,000. It overwrites public_repos.json and rebalance_errors.json, and writes nothing when every GitHub query fails. --help (or no argument) only prints usage.

tools.inputs: None (no arguments). It reads data/rea-creative-research/public_repos.json and needs an authenticated gh CLI.
tools.outputs: Overwrites data/rea-creative-research/public_repos.json (1,000 rows) and rebalance_errors.json, and prints JSON with the unique count, category counts, excluded-marketing count and query errors.
tools.consent: Contacts GitHub through the user's authenticated gh CLI and overwrites the tracked data/rea-creative-research/public_repos.json and rebalance_errors.json. Run it only when the user wants the catalog regenerated: there is no dry-run or backup (review the git diff).
tools.limits: Rewrites the catalog from GitHub search metadata using fixed quotas. It has no dry-run, no backup and no tests, and it analyses no code.

tools.summary_en: Searches a curated offline registry of 31 reviewed GitHub repositories (plus a dated top-10 Python star snapshot) and returns ranked reference sources with licence, caution and code-reuse gates as JSON.
tools.summary_ar: يبحث في سجلٍّ محلي منسَّق يضم 31 مستودعًا على GitHub جرت مراجعتها (مع لقطة مؤرَّخة لأعلى عشرة مستودعات Python من حيث عدد النجوم)، ويعيد بصيغة JSON مصادر مرجعية مرتبة مع ترخيص كلٍّ منها وتحذيراته وضوابط إعادة استخدام الكود.

وش أفضل مصادر GitHub لتصميم الأنظمة والتوسع؟
can I reuse code from GraphiteEditor/Graphite? check the licence gate
اعرض أعلى عشرة مستودعات بايثون حسب النجوم

commands.name: check
commands.does: Validates data/community_sources.json (schema, exactly 31 sources, URL = github.com/<repo>, 13 known domains, reference_only status, a sorted top-10 Python snapshot) and prints counts and domains. Every other command runs the same validation first.

commands.name: list
commands.does: Lists sources (id, repo, domain, licence), optionally filtered to one of 13 domains.

commands.name: show
commands.does: Prints the full registry record for one source by id or owner/repo (case-insensitive); an unknown id exits 2 with the same catalog_error message as an invalid registry.

commands.name: suggest
commands.does: Ranks sources by keyword overlap with each source's signals (Arabic-normalised) or an exact repo name, optionally within one --domain; --limit is clamped to 1–10. With --code-reuse the reuse_gate is check_rights_first for licences other than MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause and check_file_and_dependency_licenses for those three; without it, reference_only.

commands.name: python-top
commands.does: Prints the dated (2026-10-17) top-10 Python-repos-by-stars snapshot, flagged live_star_counts=false.

tools.inputs: Free-text query in English or Arabic (suggest), a source id like SRC-16 or owner/repo (show), optional --domain (agents, architecture, collaboration, creative, data, engineering, finance, learning, media, operations, prompts, python, research), --limit, --code-reuse; reads data/community_sources.json.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: registry validation status, source lists, one source record, ranked suggestions with url/licence/why (Arabic)/reuse_gate/caution, or the Python top-10 snapshot. On an invalid registry or a `show` id that is not found it exits 2 and prints only {status: catalog_error, error_type} on stderr.

إيه الأدوات المتسطبة على الجهاز ده قبل ما أوعد بالرندر؟
List the voice repositories in the KOSIF tool map
Show the record for ggml-org/whisper.cpp with its license note

commands.name: list
commands.does: Lists repositories, optionally filtered by --capability, --domain or a --license-note substring, as a table or as JSON.

commands.name: show

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Probes 21 tools on PATH, in node_modules folders, under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and by Python import spec, printing install hints for missing ones. With --strict it exits 1 if a core render tool (node, ffmpeg, ffprobe, playwright or chromium) is missing.

commands.name: stats
commands.does: Counts repositories and total stars by superpower, domain and license note.

commands.name: check
commands.does: Validates repos.json (125 entries, required fields, GitHub URLs, Arabic text, existing playbooks) and verifies that references/repos.md is up to date. Read-only, suitable for CI.

commands.name: build
commands.does: Without --check it validates repos.json and rewrites references/repos.md. With --check it only verifies the file is current (exit 1 if stale).

tools.outputs: Text tables or JSON on stdout. build without --check writes references/repos.md.

tools.summary_en: An interactive POSIX-sh app for a-Shell on iPhone. It downloads video or audio with yt-dlp (single links, batches, part of a video, subtitles, best-effort Facebook profiles), makes Photos-safe H.264/AAC MP4 copies, and offers an offline ffmpeg Studio (trim, compress to 16/25/50 MB, 9:16 reels with blurred fill, GIF, cover JPG, -14 LUFS loudness, cut pauses, mute, audio only) and an Audio Lab for separating voice and music.
tools.summary_ar: تطبيق تفاعلي مكتوب بلغة sh يعمل في a-Shell على الآيفون. ينزّل الفيديو أو الصوت عبر yt-dlp (رابط مفرد، أو دفعة روابط، أو جزء من فيديو، أو مع الترجمة، أو من صفحات فيسبوك بأفضل جهد ممكن)، وينشئ نسخ MP4 بترميز H.264/AAC متوافقة مع تطبيق الصور. ويوفّر استوديو ffmpeg يعمل دون اتصال (قص، وضغط إلى 16 أو 25 أو 50 ميغابايت، ومقاطع ريلز 9:16 بخلفية مموّهة، وGIF، وصورة غلاف، وضبط الجهارة على ‎-14 LUFS، وحذف فترات الصمت، وكتم الصوت، واستخراج الصوت وحده)، ومعملًا صوتيًا لفصل الصوت البشري عن الموسيقى.
use_when: نزّل الفيديو ده على الآيفون من a-Shell
أبي أحمّل ريل إنستغرام وأحفظه في الصور
افصل صوت المتكلم عن الموسيقى من فيديو على الجوال
Download a TikTok on my iPhone with a-Shell and save it to Photos
Trim and compress a downloaded video to 16 MB on iPhone
Make a 9:16 reel with a blurred background from a file on my iPhone

commands.name: download (interactive)
commands.does: Takes a URL or a whole share text (an empty Enter uses the clipboard), then shows a menu: best, 2160p to 480p, fast MP4, M4A or MP3, exact site formats (10), Audio Lab (11), part start-end (12), with subtitles (13) and Studio (14). Saves to Photos SAFE or Files and offers a yt-dlp update and one retry when a download fails.

commands.name: --photos/--files/-N/--output
commands.does: Presets the destination (photos or files), sets 1-16 parallel connections (default 8 or CINEMA_CONNECTIONS) and chooses the download folder.

commands.name: --batch
commands.does: Downloads many links in one go and saves the failed ones for a retry. Without a file it reads pasted links until an empty line.

commands.name: --studio
commands.does: Opens the offline ffmpeg Studio menu on a local file (or a file picked from Cinema_Downloads): fast or exact trim, compress to 16/25/50 MB or a custom size, 9:16 reels, GIF up to 15 MB, cover JPG, two-pass -14 LUFS, cut pauses, mute, audio only and Audio Lab. Results go to Cinema_Downloads/Studio.

commands.name: --safe
commands.does: Builds a Photos-safe H.264/AAC yuv420p +faststart MP4 from a file already downloaded. It remuxes losslessly when the video is already H.264 or HEVC, and otherwise re-encodes with the first encoder that works.

commands.name: --lab
commands.does: Opens the Audio Lab on a local file: voice only, music only, both, video with the music or the voice muted, AI STEMS (online Demucs on Replicate) or the original audio. Voice isolation may download the arnndn model once.

commands.name: --doctor
commands.does: Reports yt-dlp (and its impersonation targets, checked locally), the clipboard and ffmpeg, lists the encoders present, runs a 1-second synthetic encode test for each video encoder present and lists the Studio filters. It writes only to ~/Documents/.cinema.

commands.name: --lab-doctor
commands.does: Checks the Audio Lab ffmpeg filters, the Replicate token and curl. If the arnndn voice model is missing, it downloads it from GitHub with curl.

commands.name: --update
commands.does: Runs pip install --upgrade yt-dlp (or python3 -m pip).

commands.name: --setup-ai
commands.does: Prompts for a Replicate API token and saves it to ~/Documents/replicate_token.txt (chmod 600). An empty answer saves nothing.

commands.name: --install
commands.does: Copies the script to ~/Documents/bin/c and makes it executable, so typing 'c' runs it.

commands.name: --history
commands.does: Prints the last 20 lines of Cinema_Downloads/history.txt, or 'No downloads recorded yet.'

commands.name: --setup-facebook-cookies
commands.does: Prints instructions for providing a Netscape-format cookies file for Facebook profiles.

commands.name: --cookies
commands.does: Passes the user's Netscape cookies file to yt-dlp for the download. It exits 1 at parse time if the file is missing or lacks the Netscape header. Without this flag, Facebook profile URLs use ~/Documents/facebook_cookies.txt automatically when it is valid. Profile enumeration is best-effort.

commands.name: --fb-doctor/--fb-debug
commands.does: --fb-doctor diagnoses Facebook profile access (impersonation targets, login redirects). --fb-debug runs the normal flow with verbose logs. Both need yt-dlp.

commands.name: --version/--help
commands.does: Prints the version (Cinema C 34.0-Studio-iPhone) or the usage text.

tools.inputs: A video or reel URL, or a whole share text (or the clipboard via pbpaste). Optionally a links.txt file, local media files (from ~/Documents/Cinema_Downloads or a path), a Netscape cookies file and a Replicate token. Interactive menu choices are read from stdin.
tools.outputs: Media files in ~/Documents/Cinema_Downloads (override with CINEMA_DOWNLOAD_DIR or --output), Photos-safe copies, Studio results in Cinema_Downloads/Studio (mp4, gif, jpg, m4a), Audio Lab results in Cinema_Downloads/Audio_Lab, history.txt, and state, cache and models in ~/Documents/.cinema.
tools.consent: Downloads third-party media, so confirm the user owns it or has the rights first. It uses the user's cookies file, which is a login credential. --update runs pip install --upgrade yt-dlp. AI STEMS uploads the audio to api.replicate.com with the user's paid token. The Audio Lab and --lab-doctor may download an arnndn model from GitHub. --install copies the script to ~/Documents/bin/c, and --setup-ai stores a secret token in ~/Documents.
tools.limits: It is built for a-Shell on iPhone and has never been run on a real iPhone (only container simulations are recorded); most flows are interactive menus rather than scriptable flags, and Facebook profile enumeration is best-effort.
tools.evidence_note: No test file exercises it. Run here with HOME set to a scratch folder. sh -n syntax OK. --help, --version, --history and --setup-facebook-cookies exit 0. --setup-ai with empty stdin saved nothing. --install copied the script to the scratch ~/Documents/bin/c. --doctor exit 0: libx264 and MPEG-4 encode tests WORK, VideoToolbox absent, pbpaste missing, yt-dlp not found. An unknown option and -N 99 exit 1, and a cookies file without the Netscape header exits 1 at parse time. The download, --batch, --cookies and --fb-* examples parse and then stop with 'yt-dlp not found' (exit 1). --studio, --safe and --lab on a missing ./in.mp4 exit 1 with 'File not found'. --lab-doctor, --update, real downloads and the Studio and Lab menus were not run (network or interactive).

tools.summary_en: Standard-library triage of Windows installers and desktop apps before REA. It identifies the installer family (NSIS, Inno, WiX Burn, Squirrel, InstallShield, MSI), UPX packing, Electron, .NET and the signature slot, and finds payloads hidden in PE resources. It also lists and fingerprints Electron asar bundles, unpacks payloads with 7-Zip or innoextract on request and maps each artifact to the matching REA command.
tools.summary_ar: فرز لمثبّتات ويندوز وتطبيقات سطح المكتب بالمكتبة القياسية قبل استخدام REA. يتعرّف على نوع المثبّت (NSIS وInno وWiX Burn وSquirrel وInstallShield وMSI) وضغط UPX وElectron و‎.NET وخانة التوقيع، ويكشف الحمولات المخبّأة في موارد PE. ويسرد كذلك محتوى حزم asar في Electron ويستخرج بصمة قدراتها، ويستخرج الحمولة بـ 7-Zip أو innoextract عند الإذن، ويحدّد لكل عنصر أمر REA المناسب.
use_when: افحص ملف setup.exe قبل الهندسة العكسية
إيه المزايا اللي جوّه تطبيق Electron ده من ملف app.asar؟
ما نوع هذا المثبّت وهل هو موقّع؟
unpack this NSIS installer safely before analysis
fingerprint an app.asar for its Electron features
which REA command fits each file in this unpacked folder?

commands.name: scan
commands.does: Classifies a file, or the top-level .exe/.msi/.dll/.asar/.zip/.7z/.rar files in a folder. It reports installer family, packer, Electron, .NET, signature slot, version strings, embedded PE-resource payloads, encrypted RAR and Adobe offline packages, then proposes next steps (unpack or REA commands). Read-only.

commands.name: unpack
commands.does: Extracts the payload into a folder that must not exist yet, using 7-Zip (innoextract for Inno Setup), and goes up to two nested archive levels deep. It never runs the target, needs --authorized and a 7-Zip binary, and returns a file manifest plus the target's sha256.

commands.name: asar
commands.does: Lists an Electron asar archive (files, largest entries, package.json, renderers) or prints one small text entry.

commands.name: fingerprint
commands.does: Counts Electron capability anchors (screen capture, auto-update, deep links, safeStorage and more) in the main and preload bundles, plus file associations, renderer windows and RTL UI, as evidence that features exist.

commands.name: route
commands.does: Walks an unpacked folder and maps each asar, large exe, managed dll, msi, zip/nupkg and sqlite file to the REA or triage commands that fit it. Nothing is run.

tools.inputs: A file (.exe, .msi, .dll, .asar, .zip, .7z or .rar) or a folder. unpack takes --to <absent folder> and --authorized; asar takes an optional entry path. The SEVEN_ZIP env var can point to the 7-Zip binary.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: findings and proposed routes, an asar listing or entry text, a fingerprint, or a route plan. unpack writes the extracted tree under --to and returns a file manifest with the target's sha256.
tools.consent: unpack runs a third-party extractor (7-Zip, or innoextract for Inno Setup) on a binary the user supplies and writes its contents into a new folder. It needs --authorized and the user's confirmation that they may inspect the binary; the target itself is never run. An encrypted RAR is refused: ask the owner for the password and never guess it. scan, asar, fingerprint and route are read-only.
tools.limits: Reports installer, packer and Electron structure and counts Electron API anchors. That shows code is present, not that a feature is reachable or enabled (verified is always false). It never runs the installer.
tools.evidence_note: evals/test_installer_triage.py: 23/23 passed. The CLI scan, asar, fingerprint and route commands were also run here on synthetic PE and asar files. unpack stopped at authorization_required, or at seven_zip_missing with --authorized, because no 7z or innoextract is installed.

tools.summary_en: Performs a read-only static inventory of a local folder without executing anything and returns a JSON report of file counts, extensions, routes (source review, Ghidra/REA binary candidates, archives, media), regex indicators, SHA-256 hashes and zip-safety stats.
tools.summary_ar: يجري جردًا ساكنًا للقراءة فقط لمجلد محلي دون تشغيل أي شيء، ويعيد تقرير JSON يتضمّن أعداد الملفات وامتداداتها وتصنيف وجهتها (مراجعة الشيفرة، أو ملفات ثنائية مرشّحة للتحليل بـ Ghidra أو REA، أو أرشيفات، أو وسائط) ومؤشرات مطابقة الأنماط وبصمات SHA-256 وإحصاءات أمان ملفات zip.
use_when: افحص مجلد المشروع هذا وقل لي محتواه بدون تشغيل أي شيء
عايز جرد سريع للملفات وأي ملفات تنفيذية في الفولدر ده
أبي تقرير عن امتدادات الملفات والمؤشرات الثابتة في المشروع
Do a read-only triage of this local project folder
Which files in this repo are binaries worth looking at with Ghidra or REA?
Check this folder for zip files with path traversal entries

commands.name: scan
commands.does: Walks the folder read-only and prints a JSON summary: file and byte counts, extensions, routes, indicator counts and the unreadable count.

commands.name: scan-with-report
commands.does: Also writes the full report (per-file samples with sha256, indicators and zip stats, plus skipped items) to a path outside the audited folder, creating parent folders. It caps the walk at 20000 files.

commands.name: library
commands.example: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import local_project_audit as a; print(a.scan('templates')['routes'])"
commands.does: Calls scan(root, limit) directly and returns the full report dict without writing anything.

commands.name: help
commands.does: Shows the positional root and the --output and --limit options.

tools.inputs: A local directory path (positional root). Optional --output gives a report path outside that directory. Optional --limit sets the maximum number of files, 1-1,000,000 (default 100000).
tools.outputs: A one-line JSON summary on stdout (schema kosif.local-project-audit.v1, without samples or skipped items). With --output, the full report also holds up to 120 sample records: the first 80 files plus every Ghidra/REA candidate. Each record has the path, bytes, route, sha256 for files up to 4 MB, regex indicators for source files up to 2 MB, and zip entries, uncompressed bytes, ratio and unsafe_path_count. The report also lists up to 30 skipped entries.
tools.consent: Reads and hashes every file under the chosen folder, which may hold private data: confirm the user wants that folder inspected. --output creates parent folders and silently overwrites an existing report file.
tools.limits: Static, file-level triage by extension and regex signatures only; it never executes or extracts anything and cannot prove runtime behavior, malware status or licensing.
tools.evidence_note: 4/4 passed.

tools.summary_en: Opt-in bridge to the REA reverse-engineering CLI that stays within what the evidence shows. It checks Node and REA readiness, lists the 241 REA power records in the catalog (153 CLI commands, 76 MCP tools, 6 prompts and 6 KOSIF installer-triage additions) and plans an inspection without running it. Only with --authorized does it run one of 14 static local REA inspectors, saving the output to a new JSON file named by the caller.
tools.summary_ar: جسر اختياري إلى أداة REA للهندسة العكسية لا يتجاوز ما تثبته الأدلة. يفحص جاهزية Node وREA، ويسرد سجلات REA الـ241 في الكتالوج (153 أمرًا سطريًا و76 أداة MCP و6 قوالب أوامر و6 إضافات فرز من KOSIF)، ويخطّط للفحص دون تنفيذه. ولا يشغّل أحد فاحصات REA الساكنة المحلية الأربعة عشر إلا مع ‎--authorized، ويحفظ الناتج في ملف JSON جديد يسمّيه المستخدم.
use_when: شغّل فحص REA ساكنًا على تطبيق JavaScript واحفظ النتيجة في ملف
اعرض قائمة أوامر REA المتاحة وحالة كل أمر
هو REA متسطّب عندي ولا لأ؟ ونسخة Node مناسبة؟
check if REA and Node are installed and compatible
plan a .NET assembly inspection before running it
run REA on this extracted Electron app and save the JSON evidence

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Reports whether a REA launcher is found (REA_BIN or `rea` on PATH) and runs `node --version` to check against REA's supported range (22.19+, 24.11+ or 26+). Prints the result as a JSON report.

commands.name: catalog
commands.does: Lists the 241 REA power records from data/powers/software-investigation.json with their status, section and extra requirement. An optional text query filters the list. Nothing is run.

commands.name: plan
commands.does: Builds the exact REA argv for an existing target without running it. Kinds with no static command return a REA docs link (provider or manual workflow), and the 'installer' kind redirects to installer_triage.py scan.

commands.name: run
commands.does: Runs one of 14 static REA inspectors. It needs --authorized, an installed REA and a compatible Node. REA's JSON stdout goes to a new --output file (exclusive create, in an existing folder), and the tool returns the file's sha256 and byte count with verified=false.

tools.inputs: An action. plan and run also take a kind and a target path: plan accepts 32 kinds, including documented-only ones and 'installer'; run accepts 14 static kinds (javascript, dotnet, dotnet-members, dotnet-boundaries, sqlite, go, rust, artifact, electron-fuses, android-package, flutter, dart-aot, pe-resources, recorded-crash). run also takes --output, --authorized, --timeout (default 600 s) and --source-path (javascript only, repeatable). The REA_BIN env var overrides the REA launcher.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: an environment probe, a catalog listing or a plan. run also writes a caller-named JSON result file (it never overwrites and never echoes the contents) and reports its sha256 and byte count.
tools.consent: run executes the third-party REA CLI (npm package rea-agents, which the user installs separately with approval) against a target the user names. It needs --authorized and the user's confirmation that they own the target or may inspect it. doctor only runs `node --version`, and catalog and plan run nothing, so they need no approval.
tools.limits: Runs only REA's 14 static local inspectors. It never installs REA, never runs native, dynamic or provider workflows (plan only links their docs) and never validates findings (verified is always false). Its Node gate does not account for per-command needs, such as Node 24.15+ for inspect-sqlite-database.
tools.evidence_note: evals/test_rea_bridge.py: 10/10 passed (run is exercised with a stubbed REA; doctor here reports rea_installed=false and node v22.22.0 compatible=true)

tools.title_en: Web app study (public frontend, REA, facts only)
tools.title_ar: دراسة تطبيق ويب عام بـ REA (حقائق فقط)
tools.summary_en: Studies one public web page read-only: a logged-out headless Chromium with a fresh profile and background networking off (fresh profile, deleted afterwards), then REA captures the page, page-declared WebMCP tools, a screenshot and the public scripts, with SHA-256 receipts; optional bounded static JavaScript analysis. report turns a study folder into facts only: framework and versions, canvas/editor/realtime libraries, services inferred from storage key NAMES, WebMCP tools and page metrics, each with file-and-identifier evidence and never code. Written for the MagicPath study; runs on any desktop OS.
tools.summary_ar: يدرس صفحة ويب عامة للقراءة فقط: متصفح بلا تسجيل دخول وملف شخصي جديد يُحذف بعد التشغيل، ثم يلتقط REA الصفحة وأدوات WebMCP المعلنة ولقطة شاشة والسكربتات العامة ببصمات SHA-256. التقرير حقائق فقط: الإطار وإصداره، ومكتبات اللوحة والمحرر والتزامن، والخدمات المستنتجة من أسماء مفاتيح التخزين، بدليل اسم ملف ومعرّف، وبلا أي كود.
use_when: حلل واجهة موقع MagicPath العامة بـ REA واعرف مبني بإيه
Study a public web app's frontend stack and declared WebMCP tools without logging in
اعمل تقرير تقني عن تطبيق ويب عشان نستلهم أفكاره بدون نسخ كوده

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Finds REA and a Chromium/Chrome/Edge binary.

commands.name: run (plan only)
commands.does: Prints the isolated browser command and every REA step without starting anything.

commands.name: run
commands.does: Isolated logged-out capture: targets, page (scripts, storage key names), WebMCP tools, screenshot, script export, receipts, then the report. Add --deep for REA's bounded static JavaScript analysis.

commands.name: report
commands.does: Facts-only report.json and report.md from a study folder.

tools.inputs: One public http(s) URL the user may study, plus optional extra exact origins
tools.outputs: A study folder outside any git checkout: REA JSON artifacts, screenshot.png, exported public scripts (never commit them), receipts.json with SHA-256, report.json and report.md (facts only)
tools.consent: Visits the given public URL in a fresh, logged-out browser and saves its public scripts to a folder outside the repo. Only for sites the user may study; never log in, never commit the exported scripts, borrow ideas in your own words.
tools.limits: One page per run, logged out, so features behind sign-in are not observed; storage values, cookies and request bodies are never kept; library detection is identifier-based (a name can appear without the library being used — confidence is shown); the unbounded REA bundle analyzer is not used because it ran out of memory (about 8 GB, observed, not receipted) on MagicPath's 5.8 MB bundle. Exit code 2 when a required step failed or the profile could not be deleted.
tools.evidence_note: Tests in evals/test_web_app_study.py run here, one a live end-to-end study of a local page with REA 6.7.0 and Chromium 141 (DevToolsActivePort verified, profile deleted and checked, receipts, screenshot); real run on https://www.magicpath.ai on 2026-10-20.

tools.summary_en: Read-only router that maps one target keyword from a fixed 29-word list (dotnet, apk, har, firmware, sqlite and others) to one of 16 REA capability families, giving the upstream tool name and availability status. It also reports whether rea and node are on PATH.
tools.summary_ar: موجّه للقراءة فقط يربط كلمة واحدة تصف الهدف من قائمة ثابتة فيها 29 كلمة (مثل dotnet وapk وhar وfirmware وsqlite) بواحدة من 16 عائلة قدرات في REA، ويذكر اسم الأداة الأصلية وحالة توفّرها. ويبيّن كذلك هل rea وnode موجودان في PATH.
use_when: أي أمر في REA يناسب ملف APK؟
وجّه هدف dotnet إلى عائلة REA الصحيحة
هو REA موجود على الجهاز ده؟
which REA tool handles a HAR network capture?
list the REA capability families

commands.name: list
commands.does: Prints all 16 REA capability families with examples, availability status and the upstream tool name.

commands.name: route
commands.does: Maps one exact intent keyword (case-insensitive) to its REA family and tool name without running anything. An unknown word returns not_an_rea_target.

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Reports whether rea and node are on PATH (shutil.which only) and prints a suggested dry-run setup command, which it never runs.

tools.inputs: An action (list, route or doctor). route also takes a single intent keyword from the built-in map: application-binary, native, binary, dotnet, c#, javascript, asar, source-map, apk, android, zip, ios-package, chrome, website, electron, v8, node, har, saz, qlog, network-capture, process, firmware, sqlite, go, rust, plist, app-graph or evidence.
tools.outputs: JSON on stdout: the full family map, one routing record or an environment probe.
tools.limits: Maps one exact keyword from a fixed list to a REA family and tool name. It does not understand free text, never runs or installs REA and never confirms the tool exists in the installed version (verified is always false; provider_version is always 'unknown').
tools.evidence_note: tests/test_rea_family_router.py: 4/4 passed

tools.title_ar: تحليل REA لمستودعات المالك دفعةً واحدة
tools.summary_en: Batch static REA analysis of the user's own JavaScript, TypeScript and HTML GitHub repositories. It reads a private inventory (made by rea_creative_research_atlas.py own), shallow-clones the smallest eligible repos under a size cap with git (depth 1, blob:none) and runs REA's analyze-javascript-application on each through node. Clones and evidence stay in a local private folder, and only counts are printed.
tools.summary_ar: تحليل REA ساكن على دفعات لمستودعات المستخدم على GitHub المكتوبة بـ JavaScript أو TypeScript أو HTML. يقرأ جردًا خاصًا يُنشئه الأمر rea_creative_research_atlas.py own، ثم يستنسخ بـ git أصغر المستودعات المؤهَّلة ضمن حدّ الحجم استنساخًا سطحيًا (عمق 1 وblob:none)، ويشغّل عليها أمر REA analyze-javascript-application عبر node. تبقى النسخ والأدلة في مجلد خاص محلي، ولا يطبع إلا الأعداد.
use_when: حلّل مستودعاتي على GitHub بـ REA دفعة واحدة
استخرج أدلة REA من مشاريع JavaScript اللي أملكها
افحص شيفرة مستودعاتي الخاصة محليًا من غير ما تشغّلها
run REA statically over all my owned JS repos
batch-analyze the source of my GitHub repositories with REA

commands.name: run
commands.does: Picks JS, TS and HTML repos from the private inventory that are at or under --max-size-kb. It shallow-clones up to --max-repos of them over HTTPS, runs `node <rea-cli> analyze-javascript-application` on each, writes per-repo evidence and a results file, and prints a counts-only summary.

tools.inputs: --private-output <existing local folder holding owner_repositories_PRIVATE_LOCAL.json; it must not itself contain .git> and --rea-cli <path to the installed REA CLI .mjs>. Optional: --max-size-kb (default 8000) and --max-repos (default 16).
tools.outputs: Clones go to <private-output>/source_clones/, per-repo REA JSON to <private-output>/rea_evidence/, and a running rea_owned_repo_results_PRIVATE_LOCAL.json is kept. stdout gets START/RESULT progress lines and a public counts-only summary.
tools.consent: It clones the user's GitHub repositories over the network, using git with the user's credentials for private repos, and runs the third-party REA CLI on each clone. It needs the user's confirmation that they own or may analyze every repo in the inventory, a prepared private inventory and an output folder outside any git checkout (the script refuses a folder inside a git repository).
tools.limits: Analyzes only JS, TS and HTML repos under the size cap, using REA's static JavaScript analyzer. It does not verify runtime features, build the inventory or install REA.
tools.evidence_note: No test file exercises it. Here only --help ran, plus an empty-inventory run inside the scratch folder (0 repos, no clone, no node, no network).

tools.summary_en: Inspects a local repository folder or source ZIP for languages, capability signals, license files and a per-file SHA-256 manifest. It packs a deterministic, filtered source ZIP plus a JSON capability-transfer report, leaving out build caches, archives, executables, audio and video, keys, databases and files whose names suggest secrets. Nothing is run, imported or installed.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص مجلد مستودع محليًا أو ملف ZIP للشيفرة المصدرية بحثًا عن اللغات وإشارات القدرات وملفات التراخيص، ويبني بصمة SHA-256 لكل ملف. ثم يحزم الشيفرة في ملف ZIP مُرشَّح يتكرّر ناتجه حرفيًا، ويرفق به تقرير JSON لنقل القدرات. يستبعد مجلدات البناء والأرشيفات والملفات التنفيذية والصوت والفيديو والمفاتيح وقواعد البيانات والملفات التي توحي أسماؤها بأسرار، ولا يشغّل أي شيفرة ولا يستوردها ولا يثبّتها.
use_when: جهّز نسخة نظيفة من هذا المستودع لنقل قدراته
احزم كود المشروع من غير أسرار ولا ملفات تنفيذية
ما لغات هذا المستودع وما ملفات تراخيصه؟
inspect a repo for reusable capabilities and licenses
pack a downloaded GitHub ZIP into a sanitized source archive

commands.name: inspect
commands.does: Reports languages, capability signals, license files and excluded files on stdout, without the manifest. With --out it also writes the full report, including the sha256 manifest, to that path; the parent folder must already exist.

commands.name: pack
commands.does: Writes a deterministic filtered source ZIP (fixed timestamps, sorted entries) outside the input folder, creating parent folders as needed. With --report it also writes the capability-transfer report with package_sha256.

tools.inputs: A local source folder or an existing ZIP archive; for a GitHub source ZIP the single top folder is stripped. inspect takes an optional --out <json>; pack needs --out <zip> outside the input folder and takes an optional --report <json>.
tools.outputs: A summary JSON report on stdout. inspect --out writes the full report with the sha256 manifest. pack writes the ZIP, overwriting any file already at --out, and with --report writes the report. Blocked inputs print 'repository pack blocked: …' to stderr and exit with code 2.
tools.consent: pack and inspect --out write files to paths the user names. pack overwrites an existing --out file, and inspect --out is not stopped from writing inside the input folder, so choose fresh paths. Before reusing or sharing the ZIP, review licenses and any secrets inside files, because filtering goes by file name only (reuse_allowed is always false).
tools.limits: Infers candidate capabilities from file names and extensions only, and filters secrets by file name, not content. Images, fonts and PDFs stay in the ZIP. It never runs, imports, clones or licenses the code.
tools.evidence_note: evals/test_repository_capability_packer.py: 4/4 passed. inspect and pack were also run on a synthetic repo in the scratch folder: .env and .mp4 were excluded, while .png, .woff2 and a config.py holding an API key were kept.

tools.summary_en: A self-contained stdio MCP server (standard library only) that gives an MCP client 11 tools scoped to one approved workspace: health, system info, list, file info, read, search, plus create, write, replace, move and an allowlisted command runner. Writes and commands stay off until the user sets an environment flag.
tools.summary_ar: خادم MCP مستقل يعمل عبر stdio بالمكتبة القياسية وحدها، ويمنح عميل MCP إحدى عشرة أداة محصورة في مساحة عمل واحدة يوافق عليها المستخدم: الحالة، ومعلومات النظام، وسرد المجلد، وبيانات الملف، والقراءة، والبحث، ثم الإنشاء والكتابة والاستبدال والنقل وتشغيل أوامر من قائمة مسموحة. وتبقى الكتابة وتشغيل الأوامر معطّلين حتى يفعّلهما المستخدم بمتغيرات بيئة.
use_when: خلّي كلاود يقرأ ملفات مجلد مشروعي على جهازي
Give my MCP client read-only access to one project folder
ابحث في ملفات المشروع عن كلمة معيّنة عن طريق MCP محلي
Run git status in my workspace through a local MCP server
وصّل كلاود بمجلد على اللابتوب بدون ما يقدر يعدّل إلا بإذني

commands.name: doctor
commands.does: Prints the name, version, tool count, transport and current permissions (workspace, allow_writes, allow_exec) as one JSON line. It is also the default when no mode is given.

commands.name: demo
commands.does: In a temporary folder, shows that writes are denied by default, enables them there only, then writes, searches and reads a sample. Prints PASS or FAIL and exits.

commands.name: serve
commands.does: Serves MCP over stdio with newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call) until stdin closes. Add KOSIF_ALLOW_WRITES=1 or KOSIF_ALLOW_EXEC=1 only with the user's approval.

commands.name: tools/list (one-shot)
commands.does: Pipes one JSON-RPC request into the server, prints the 11 tool schemas and exits.

tools.inputs: JSON-RPC 2.0 lines on stdin. Environment: KOSIF_REMOTE_ROOT (the workspace; defaults to the current directory), KOSIF_ALLOW_WRITES=1 and KOSIF_ALLOW_EXEC=1 (opt-in).
tools.outputs: JSON-RPC responses on stdout whose tool results are JSON text. doctor and demo print one JSON line. The write tools change files only inside the workspace, with atomic writes and a 512 KB cap.
tools.consent: The user must approve the folder set as KOSIF_REMOTE_ROOT. Setting KOSIF_ALLOW_WRITES=1 (create, write, replace, move inside it) and KOSIF_ALLOW_EXEC=1 (git status/diff/rev-parse with a few read-only flags, and exactly python/node/npm --version with no other arguments) each needs separate approval, as does adding the server to an MCP client config; do not enable exec on an untrusted repository, because git honours that repository's own config.
tools.limits: It gives bounded local stdio access to one workspace (UTF-8 text files up to 512 KB, 300 lines per read, 150 listed entries, 500 files and 35 hits per search) plus six allowlisted status and version commands, with no remote relay, pairing, desktop or UI control, or arbitrary shell.
tools.evidence_note: 7/7 passed (python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/scripts -p test_kosif_remote_superpowers.py). --help, doctor, demo (PASS) and the tools/list one-shot worked here; a piped serve session on a scratch workspace answered initialize, run_command python --version and search_text, and refused python3 (not allowlisted) and a ../ path.

tools.summary_en: Regenerates the bilingual Markdown chapter references/powers/<family>.md for every general (non-motion) power family from data/powers/<family>.json. Output is deterministic, and it never touches the 30 hand-made motion chapters. --check reports stale, missing or orphaned chapters without writing.
tools.summary_ar: يعيد توليد الفصل ثنائي اللغة references/powers/<family>.md لكل عائلة قدرات عامة (غير عائلات الموشن) من ملف data/powers/<family>.json. ناتجه حتمي، ولا يمس فصول الموشن الثلاثين المكتوبة يدويًا. أما الخيار --check فيبلغ عن الفصول القديمة أو المفقودة أو اليتيمة دون أن يكتب شيئًا.
use_when: ولّد فصول العائلات من ملفات JSON بعد ما عدّلت القدرات
وش فيها الفصول طالعة قديمة في check_skill؟ حدّثها
حدّث ملف references/powers/thinking-core.md بس
regenerate the general family chapters after editing data/powers
check whether the generated power chapters are stale

commands.name: build
commands.does: Writes every general chapter whose rendered text changed. A chapter without the generated marker is refused, never overwritten. Prints 'wrote …' lines and a summary, and exits 1 if any chapter was refused or any family JSON failed to parse.

commands.name: --check
commands.does: Writes nothing. Lists missing, stale or orphaned generated chapters and exits 1 if there is any problem; otherwise prints 'N general chapter(s) up to date'.

commands.name: --family
commands.does: Limits the run (build or check) to one family stem; orphan detection and pruning are off. Exits 2 if no general family has that name.

commands.name: --out
commands.does: Writes the chapters into another folder instead of references/powers/ (for tests and previews).

commands.name: --force
commands.does: Overwrites a chapter even when it lacks the generated marker, which replaces a hand-written chapter.

commands.name: --prune
commands.does: Also deletes generated chapters whose family JSON no longer exists. Off with --family; with --check orphans are only reported.

commands.name: --quiet
commands.does: Suppresses the 'wrote …' lines and the summary in build mode, and the 'up to date' line in --check mode; problems are still printed.

tools.inputs: data/powers/*.json (general families only); references/*.md except the generated INDEX.md, which are scanned for the family stem or ID prefix to build 'related references'; FAMILY_META in scripts/powers.py. Options: --family STEM, --out DIR.
tools.outputs: references/powers/<family>.md for each general family (or DIR/<family>.md with --out), plus stdout 'wrote …' lines and a summary. --check exits 1 and lists stale, missing or orphaned chapters. An unknown --family exits 2.
tools.consent: A plain run rewrites the tracked generated chapters in references/powers/; --force overwrites hand-written chapters and --prune deletes files, so confirm before using either.
tools.limits: It only formats existing JSON records into Markdown, without checking the claims inside them, and it never regenerates the 30 motion chapters.
tools.evidence_note: Not run: no test file in tests/ or evals/ exercises it (CI runs --check; check_skill.py imports it for its chapters check). Manual runs on HEAD 524e22a: --help exit 0; --check exit 1 with 2 problems (runnable-tools missing, software-investigation stale); --family thinking-core --check exit 0; --family thinking-core --out <scratch> wrote 1 chapter byte-identical to the tracked one, exit 0; --family nope exit 2.

tools.summary_en: Statically audits every power record in data/powers/*.json for duplicate ids, malformed records and proof-link coverage. It checks only whether local 'kosif-tool/...' references exist and counts the claimed statuses and proof scopes.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص كل سجل قدرة في data/powers/*.json دون تشغيل أي شيء، بحثًا عن المعرّفات المكررة والسجلات المعطوبة ومدى تغطية روابط الإثبات. ويكتفي بالتحقق من وجود المراجع المحلية 'kosif-tool/...'، ويُحصي الحالات ونطاقات الإثبات المعلنة.
use_when: افحص كتالوج القدرات وشوف فيه سجلات مكررة أو روابط إثبات ناقصة
كم قدرة في الكتالوج ليها دليل محلي فعلًا؟
راجع صحة بيانات القدرات قبل ما ندمج الفرع
audit the powers catalog for duplicate ids and broken proof links
how many catalog entries have local evidence vs unverified links
run a catalog health check before release

commands.name: audit
commands.does: Prints kosif.catalog.evidence-audit.v1 JSON for the skill that contains the script: records_examined, unique_ids, families_examined, statuses_claimed, proof_scopes_claimed, proof_links counts, record_integrity_errors (first 30), missing_local_samples (first 12), assessment, executes_external_code=false and downloads=false. Exits 1 if there are integrity errors, otherwise 0.

commands.name: --skill
commands.does: Audits the skill folder at the given path (the repo root is taken as three levels above, i.e. skill.parents[2]).

tools.inputs: Optional --skill path to a skill folder that contains data/powers/*.json (defaults to this skill).
tools.outputs: JSON report on stdout. Exit 0 when there are no record integrity errors, 1 otherwise (a missing local reference does not change the exit code). A folder with no catalog crashes with a ValueError traceback, also exit 1.
tools.limits: Checks only that local reference paths exist, never runs a capability, and leaves every URL, sibling-repo or archive reference unverified, so a clean report does not prove that anything works.
tools.evidence_note: 4/5 passed in the current working tree (cd /home/user/kosif-tool && python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude/skills/kosif-superpowers/evals -p test_catalog_evidence_audit.py): test_catalog_all_records_unique fails with 'AssertionError: 53 != 52' because the untracked, in-progress data/powers/runnable-tools.json adds a 53rd family. A clean 'git archive HEAD' export run in scratch passed 5/5.

tools.summary_en: Validates the kosif-superpowers skill with 13 read-only checks: SKILL.md frontmatter, power records, proof paths, relative Markdown links, contents headings, generated chapters, the counts marker, model names, secrets and leaked session paths, evals/evals.json, the data/tools.json registry with its generated hub files, power-count drift in the entry docs, and the USIP protocol structure (PROTOCOL.md core and references/protocol/). It can also run the routing evals, then prints a text or JSON report and exits 1 on any error.
tools.summary_ar: يفحص مهارة kosif-superpowers بثلاثة عشر فحصًا لا تكتب شيئًا: ترويسة ملف SKILL.md، وسجلات القدرات، ومسارات الأدلة، وروابط Markdown النسبية، وعناوين المحتويات، والفصول المولَّدة، وعلامة العدّادات، وأسماء النماذج، والأسرار ومسارات الجلسات المسرَّبة، وملف evals/evals.json، وسجل الأدوات data/tools.json مع الملفات المولَّدة منه، وتطابق أعداد القدرات المذكورة في الوثائق الرئيسية، وبنية بروتوكول USIP (نواة PROTOCOL.md وملاحق references/protocol/). ويستطيع أيضًا تشغيل تقييمات التوجيه، ثم يطبع تقريرًا نصيًا أو بصيغة JSON ويخرج بالرمز 1 عند وجود أي خطأ.
use_when: افحص المهارة قبل ما نعمل commit
شيك على المهارة وشوف فيه روابط مكسورة أو أعداد غلط
تأكد إن عدادات القدرات في SKILL.md مطابقة للكتالوج
validate the kosif-superpowers skill before packaging
run the routing evals and tell me the pass rate
